summary: Complete planning pass with 175 stable target nodes, 480 API entries and 323 test contracts (453 API entries and 316 tests on definitions/constructions counted by the structural checker), 40 planets, 27 gaps, 40 supplier requests and 69 exact signature omissions. All seven stages remain planned, none closed, and every implementation status is unchecked. Finite raw distance, real, p-adic residue, coefficient-dominance and sieve checks have explicit data/check/soundness interfaces. Thue and geometric Chabauty/QC targets retain their actual mathematical carriers through precise omissions where suppliers are unavailable. The saturation citations use the recovered primary Siksek proof; numerical examples retain their explicit completeness and replay obligations. The historical independent review object is preserved for the next reviewer.

nodes.title: Certified enclosures and the precision contract
nodes.statement: Three enclosure types carry every approximate value of this roadmap. (i) For t ∈ ℝ, a RealEnclosure t is a closed nonempty rational interval I = [l, u] (Mathlib's NonemptyInterval ℚ) with l ≤ t ≤ u in ℝ. Its rational error bound is width(I) = u − l, and it has absolute precision n ∈ ℕ when u − l ≤ 2^(−n). (ii) For z ∈ ℂ, a ComplexEnclosure z is a pair (R, I) of closed nonempty rational intervals with Re z ∈ R and Im z ∈ I. Its error bound is max(width R, width I) and absolute precision n means width R ≤ 2^(−n) and width I ≤ 2^(−n). (iii) For a prime p and x ∈ ℚ_p, a PadicEnclosure x is a rational centre c and an integer N with ‖x − c‖_p ≤ p^(−N); N is its absolute precision, and its canonical record is the CN.0 PadicApproximation (N, v, s) with (v, s) = (N, 0) when c = 0; otherwise v = min(v_p(c), N), s = 0 when v = N, and when v < N s the residue of c·p^(−v) in [1, p^(N−v)) prime to p; that record denotes the same ball and so contains x. Every check on an enclosure (width, precision, membership of a rational, exclusion of zero) is a finite comparison of rationals or of p-adic valuations of rationals. An enclosure never certifies an equality: two different numbers can have overlapping or identical enclosures.
hypotheses: p is a prime in (iii); n ∈ ℕ and N ∈ ℤ.
Endpoints and centres are exact rationals; no floating-point value enters a check.
proofSteps: Represent real intervals by Mathlib's NonemptyInterval ℚ and read membership after casting the endpoints to ℝ.
Represent complex boxes by pairs of such intervals; membership is membership of the real and imaginary parts.

Represent p-adic balls by (c, N); the ultrametric inequality shows that the ball of (c, N) equals the ball of the canonical ComputationalNumberTheory:CN.0/padic-approximation record described above (the residue s ≡ c·p^(−v) modulo p^(N−v) changes the centre by an element of norm ≤ p^(−N)).
Width, precision and membership are decidable rational comparisons, which is what de Weger's two-sided rounding (§2.5) achieves by hand.
acceptance: Every enclosure check is a comparison of rationals: [141/100, 142/100] ∋ √2 is verified by 141² < 2·100² < 142².
An enclosure containing two distinct numbers exists (realEnclosure_overlap), so no equality is ever read from enclosures.

uses.how: logarithms and roots are computed with two-sided rounding so that the exact number lies in a known interval
every height and every embedding value is replaced by a rational approximation with an explicit error δ
the integers φ_i ≈ Cθ_i are rounded from a real enclosure of θ_i whose width is checked
enclosures of logarithms and of their combinations feed the reduction lattices and the final inequalities

api.name: TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.RealEnclosure

api.name: TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.RealEnclosure.width
api.statement: The rational error bound u − l; it is nonnegative.

api.name: TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.RealEnclosure.abs_sub_le

api.name: TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.RealEnclosure.ofRat

api.name: TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.RealEnclosure.widen
api.statement: An interval containing a RealEnclosure's interval is again a RealEnclosure of the same number.

api.name: TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.ComplexEnclosure
api.statement: A pair of rational intervals (R, I) with Re z ∈ R and Im z ∈ I.

api.name: TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.ComplexEnclosure.mem_box
api.statement: z belongs to the box {w : Re w ∈ R, Im w ∈ I}.

api.statement: |z|² ≤ max(l_R², u_R²) + max(l_I², u_I²), a rational upper bound for |z|².

api.statement: When I = [0, 0], R is a RealEnclosure of Re z.

api.name: TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.PadicEnclosure
api.statement: A rational centre c and an integer N with ‖x − c‖ ≤ p^(−N).

api.name: TauCeti.EffectiveDiophantine.ED0.PadicEnclosure.ofRat
api.statement: For q ∈ ℚ and every N, (q, N) encloses (q : ℚ_[p]).

api.statement: The canonical CN.0 PadicApproximation record of (c, N) denotes the closed ball of radius p^(−N) about c, which contains x.

nodes.title: Refinement of isolating intervals by exact bisection
nodes.statement: A real isolating interval for g ∈ ℚ[X], g ≠ 0, is a closed rational interval [l, u] containing exactly one real root u_0 of g. refine I n is obtained by exact bisection: replace g by its squarefree part g_0 = g / gcd(g, g′), so that u_0 is a simple root and the only root of g_0 in [l, u]; if g_0(l) = 0 or g_0(u) = 0 the root is that endpoint and [u_0, u_0] is returned; otherwise g_0(l)·g_0(u) < 0, and with m = (l + u)/2 either g_0(m) = 0 (return [m, m]) or the half on which g_0 changes sign is kept; after n steps the width is at most 2^(−n)·(u − l). The refined interval isolates the same root. Real algebraic numbers arise from CN.0 certificates: if (h, R, I) is a CN.0 AlgebraicRootCertificate whose root w is real, then R is a real isolating interval of w for h. For the root z of an archimedean embedding certificate, Re z = (z + z̄)/2 and Im z = (z − z̄)/(2i) are real algebraic numbers with CN.0 certificates obtained from those of z, of z̄ (the conjugate box) and of i (the box [0, 0] × [1, 1] for X² + 1) by CN.0's addition, multiplication and inversion certificates; refining their isolating intervals refines the box of z to any width. This is the only refinement ED.0 uses: no analytic function is evaluated.
hypotheses: g ∈ ℚ[X] nonzero; [l, u] contains exactly one real root of g.
All evaluations g_0(q) are at rationals q and are exact.
proofSteps: The squarefree part g_0 = g / gcd(g, g′) has the same roots as g, all simple (exact Euclidean algorithm in ℚ[X]).
A simple root is a sign change of g_0, and since u_0 is the only root in [l, u], g_0 has constant nonzero sign on [l, u_0) and on (u_0, u]; so if the endpoints are not roots, g_0(l)·g_0(u) < 0.

If g_0(l)·g_0(m) < 0 the intermediate value theorem (intermediate_value_Icc, Polynomial.continuous) gives a root in (l, m), which is u_0 by uniqueness; otherwise u_0 ∈ [m, u]. Induction on n gives the width bound and that the root is preserved.
If the CN.0 box R × I contains exactly one root of h and that root w is real, then 0 ∈ I and w is the only root of h in R × {0} ⊆ R × I.

Re z and Im z: CN.0/algebraic-add-certificate, /algebraic-mul-certificate, /algebraic-inv-certificate and /rational-root-presentation provide certificates for z + z̄, (z − z̄)·(2i)^(−1) and the factor 1/2; the conjugate box (R, −I) certifies z̄ because f has rational coefficients.
acceptance: X² − 2 on [1, 2]: three bisection steps give [11/8, 3/2], which isolates √2 with width 1/8.
X − 1/2 on [0, 1]: the first midpoint is the root and [1/2, 1/2] is returned.

boxes of σ(θ) are shrunk until the evaluation error ρ is below 2^(−n−1)

nodes.title: Archimedean embeddings pinned by isolating boxes
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field with a power basis pb over ℚ, generator θ and minimal polynomial f = minpoly ℚ θ of degree d. An archimedean embedding certificate for pb is a CN.0 AlgebraicRootCertificate (f, R, I): closed rational intervals R, I such that exactly one complex root z of f satisfies Re z ∈ R and Im z ∈ I. Its embedding σ_c : K →+* ℂ is PowerBasis.lift pb z, the unique ring homomorphism with σ_c(θ) = z, and σ_c is the only embedding K →+* ℂ sending θ into the box. Every embedding of K into ℂ has a certificate. For α ∈ K with power-basis coordinates (a_0, …, a_{d−1}) ∈ ℚ^d and a certificate whose box has rational centre w = w_1 + i·w_2 and half-widths at most r, put M = |w_1| + |w_2| + 2r; then σ_c(α) = Σ_j a_j z^j and |σ_c(α) − Σ_j a_j w^j| ≤ ρ := 2r · Σ_j j·|a_j|·M^(j−1), so the box with centre Σ_j a_j w^j ∈ ℚ(i) and half-widths ρ is a ComplexEnclosure of σ_c(α). Refining the box of z (same root, smaller box; EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/isolating-interval-refinement applied to Re z and Im z) until ρ ≤ 2^(−n−1) yields enclosures of absolute precision n. A list of d certificates with pairwise disjoint boxes is complete: it contains every embedding K →+* ℂ. If I = [−b, b] is symmetric about 0 then σ_c is real (ComplexEmbedding.IsReal), and R is a RealEnclosure of σ_c(θ). The infinite place of σ_c is InfinitePlace.mk σ_c; two certificates define the same place exactly when their roots are equal or complex conjugate.
hypotheses: K is a number field and pb : PowerBasis ℚ K; f = minpoly ℚ pb.gen.
(f, R, I) is a ComputationalNumberTheory:CN.0/algebraic-root-certificate for the polynomial f itself.
Coordinates of α are pb.basis.repr α; all arithmetic on centres and radii is exact rational arithmetic.
proofSteps: The decoded value z of the certificate is a root of f lying in the box (CN.0 value_spec), so PowerBasis.lift pb z is defined and sends θ to z (PowerBasis.lift_gen); two embeddings that agree on θ agree on K (PowerBasis.liftEquiv' is injective).
If σ(θ) lies in the box then σ(θ) is a root of f in the box, hence equals z by CN.0 value_unique, hence σ = σ_c.

Every embedding σ sends θ to a root of f (NumberField.Embeddings.range_eval_eq_rootSet_minpoly); f has finitely many roots, so a box around σ(θ) excluding the others exists. Since f is separable of degree d, K has exactly d embeddings (PowerBasis.liftEquiv'), so d certificates with pairwise disjoint boxes exhaust them.
σ_c(α) = Σ_j a_j z^j because σ_c is a ring homomorphism and α = Σ_j a_j θ^j; with |z − w| ≤ 2r and |z|, |w| ≤ M the identity z^j − w^j = (z − w)Σ_k z^k w^(j−1−k) gives |z^j − w^j| ≤ 2r·j·M^(j−1).

Refinement: EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/isolating-interval-refinement gives real isolating intervals of Re z and Im z of any width; their product is a smaller box containing z, hence again a certificate with the same root, and by step 2 the same embedding.

f has rational coefficients, so the complex conjugate of z is a root of f; if I is symmetric it lies in the box, hence equals z, so conjugate σ_c = σ_c (ComplexEmbedding.isReal_iff). The statement about places is InfinitePlace.mk_eq_iff.
acceptance: For ℚ(√2) the two certificates [1, 2] × [0, 0] and [−2, −1] × [0, 0] are the two real embeddings, and the enclosure of σ_c(3363 − 2378θ) at precision 14 excludes 0.
For ℚ(i) the certificates [0, 0] × [1/2, 2] and [0, 0] × [−2, −1/2] give the two complex embeddings, which define one infinite place.

nodes.title: Hensel's lemma with the exact distance to the root
nodes.statement: Let p be prime, R a commutative semiring with an algebra map to ℤ_p, F ∈ R[X] and a ∈ ℤ_p with ‖F(a)‖ < ‖F′(a)‖². Let z ∈ ℤ_p be the root given by Mathlib's hensels_lemma: F(z) = 0, ‖z − a‖ < ‖F′(a)‖, ‖F′(z)‖ = ‖F′(a)‖, and z is the only root within distance ‖F′(a)‖ of a. Then for every b ∈ ℤ_p with ‖b − a‖ < ‖F′(a)‖: ‖F′(b)‖ = ‖F′(a)‖ and ‖z − b‖ = ‖F(b)‖ / ‖F′(a)‖. In particular b satisfies the Hensel hypothesis with the same root, and for integers b and N with v_p(F(b)) ≥ N + v_p(F′(a)) one has z ≡ b (mod p^N).
hypotheses: p prime; F ∈ R[X] with [Algebra R ℤ_[p]], evaluated by aeval; a, b ∈ ℤ_p.
proofSteps: Taylor expansion (Polynomial.binomExpansion) at z gives F(b) = F(z) + F′(z)(b − z) + (b − z)²G with ‖G‖ ≤ 1, and F′(b) = F′(z) + (b − z)H with ‖H‖ ≤ 1.
‖b − z‖ ≤ max(‖b − a‖, ‖a − z‖) < ‖F′(a)‖ = ‖F′(z)‖ by the ultrametric inequality (PadicInt.nonarchimedean) and hensels_lemma.
Hence ‖(b − z)²G‖ < ‖F′(z)‖·‖b − z‖ when b ≠ z, so ‖F(b)‖ = ‖F′(z)‖·‖b − z‖ by the strict ultrametric inequality; the case b = z is trivial. Similarly ‖F′(b)‖ = ‖F′(z)‖.
This is the public form of the private Mathlib lemma soln_dist_to_a in Mathlib/NumberTheory/Padics/Hensel.lean, extended from a to every b in the Hensel disc.
acceptance: If F(a) = 0 the formula gives ‖z − a‖ = 0, i.e. z = a.

nodes.title: p-adic embeddings pinned by Hensel certificates
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field with a power basis pb over ℚ whose generator θ is integral over ℤ, so that f = minpoly ℚ θ has integer coefficients and is monic, and let p be prime. A p-adic embedding certificate is an integer a with f′(a) ≠ 0 and either f(a) = 0 or v_p(f(a)) > 2·v_p(f′(a)), an exact check on two integers. By hensels_lemma there is a unique z ∈ ℤ_p with f(z) = 0 and ‖z − a‖ < ‖f′(a)‖; the embedding σ_a : K →+* ℚ_p is PowerBasis.lift pb z, the unique embedding with σ_a(θ) = z, and σ_a is the only embedding sending θ into the open disc of radius ‖f′(a)‖ about a. Approximation contract: given N, Newton iteration in ℤ/p^(N+2v_p(f′(a)))ℤ produces an integer b with ‖b − a‖ < ‖f′(a)‖ and either f(b) = 0 or v_p(f(b)) ≥ N + v_p(f′(a)), and then z ≡ b (mod p^N) (EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/hensel-root-distance). For α ∈ K with power-basis coordinates (a_0, …, a_{d−1}) ∈ ℚ^d put e = max(0, −min_j v_p(a_j)); then (Σ_j a_j b^j, N − e) is a PadicEnclosure of σ_a(α), so N = n + e gives absolute precision n. Two certificates a, a′ define different embeddings when ‖a − a′‖ ≥ max(‖f′(a)‖, ‖f′(a′)‖). The embeddings K →+* ℚ_p correspond exactly to the roots of f in ℚ_p (PowerBasis.liftEquiv'); a simple root of f modulo p gives a certificate with v_p(f′(a)) = 0. Here v_p is Mathlib padicValRat, whose value at zero is 0; exact zero residuals are therefore handled by the explicit disjunction, rather than by treating that value as +∞.
hypotheses: K a number field, pb : PowerBasis ℚ K with IsIntegral ℤ pb.gen; f = minpoly ℚ pb.gen viewed in ℤ[X].
p prime; a ∈ ℤ with f′(a) ≠ 0 and either f(a) = 0 or v_p(f(a)) > 2·v_p(f′(a)); α given by its rational coordinates pb.basis.repr α.
proofSteps: The integer check f′(a) ≠ 0 and (f(a) = 0 or v_p(f(a)) > 2·v_p(f′(a))) is ‖f(a)‖ < ‖f′(a)‖² in ℤ_p (Padic.norm_eq_zpow_neg_valuation), so hensels_lemma gives the root z and its uniqueness in the disc.
PowerBasis.lift pb z is a ring homomorphism K → ℚ_p with θ ↦ z; any σ with ‖σ(θ) − a‖ < ‖f′(a)‖ sends θ to a root in the disc, hence to z, hence equals σ_a (PowerBasis.liftEquiv').
EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/hensel-root-distance applied to the Newton iterate b gives ‖z − b‖ = ‖f(b)‖/‖f′(a)‖ ≤ p^(−N).
z, b ∈ ℤ_p and z ≡ b (mod p^N) give z^j ≡ b^j (mod p^N); multiplying by a_j with v_p(a_j) ≥ −e gives ‖σ_a(α) − Σ_j a_j b^j‖ ≤ p^(e−N).
If ‖a − a′‖ ≥ max(‖f′(a)‖, ‖f′(a′)‖) then the two roots z, z′ satisfy ‖z − z′‖ = ‖a − a′‖ > 0 by the strict ultrametric inequality.
The canonical record of the enclosure is the ComputationalNumberTheory:CN.0/padic-approximation record of (Σ_j a_j b^j, N − e) (EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/certified-enclosure).
acceptance: Tzanakis–de Weger 1992, §3E–§4E: at p = 5 their polynomial has three roots in ℚ_5, each pinned by a certificate of this form.

nodes.title: Certified nonvanishing and the exact zero test
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field with power basis pb and α ∈ K with power-basis coordinates (a_j) ∈ ℚ^d. (a) α = 0 if and only if every a_j = 0; this exact test is the only way an identity α = 0 (or α = β, applied to α − β) is established, and for algebraic numbers given as CN.0 isolated roots the exact test is CN.0's algebraicEqual. (b) If c is an archimedean embedding certificate and (R, I) a ComplexEnclosure of σ_c(α) whose box excludes 0 (R.fst > 0, R.snd < 0, I.fst > 0 or I.snd < 0), then α ≠ 0, and therefore τ(α) ≠ 0 for every ring homomorphism τ from K to a field. (c) If a is a p-adic embedding certificate and (c, N) a PadicEnclosure of σ_a(α) with c ≠ 0 and v_p(c) < N, then α ≠ 0. (d) The exclusion test is complete: if α ≠ 0, every ComplexEnclosure of σ_c(α) of absolute precision n with 2·4^(−n) < |σ_c(α)|² excludes 0, and every PadicEnclosure (c, N) of σ_a(α) with N > v_p(σ_a(α)) has c ≠ 0 and v_p(c) = v_p(σ_a(α)) < N; so refining until exclusion terminates. (e) No enclosure containing 0 proves α = 0: for every n the rational α = 2^(−n−1) has the precision-n enclosure [0, 2^(−n)] containing 0.
hypotheses: K a number field, pb : PowerBasis ℚ K; σ_c from EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/archimedean-embedding-certificate and σ_a from EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/padic-embedding-certificate.
Enclosures are those of EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/certified-enclosure.
proofSteps: (a) pb.basis is a basis, so α = Σ_j a_j θ^j vanishes exactly when its coordinates do (Basis.repr is injective).
(b) If 0 is not in the box then σ_c(α) ≠ 0, so α ≠ 0 since σ_c(0) = 0; ring homomorphisms out of a field are injective (RingHom.injective).
(c) The strict ultrametric inequality gives ‖σ_a(α)‖ = ‖c‖ = p^(−v_p(c)) > 0 when ‖σ_a(α) − c‖ ≤ p^(−N) < p^(−v_p(c)).
(d) If 0 and σ_c(α) lie in a box of widths ≤ 2^(−n), then |Re σ_c(α)| ≤ 2^(−n) and |Im σ_c(α)| ≤ 2^(−n), so |σ_c(α)|² ≤ 2·4^(−n); the p-adic statement is the converse direction of (c).
(e) is a direct computation and records the stage's acceptance that numerical agreement proves no identity.
acceptance: Pell unit test: in K = ℚ(√2) with the certificate [1, 2] × [0, 0], α = 3363 − 2378·θ has σ_c(α) = (1 − √2)^10 = 1.4867…·10^(−4). The exact test (a) gives α ≠ 0 from the coordinates (3363, −2378). An enclosure of precision 10 (width 2^(−10) ≈ 9.8·10^(−4)) can contain 0, while every enclosure of precision 14 excludes 0 by (d), since 2·4^(−14) ≈ 7.5·10^(−9) < 2.2·10^(−8) ≈ |σ_c(α)|².
At p = 7 with the certificate a = 3 for X² − 2, the enclosure (7, 2) of σ_a(θ − 3) certifies θ − 3 ≠ 0 and v_7(σ_a(θ − 3)) = 1.

nodes.title: Certified valuations from p-adic enclosures
nodes.statement: Let a be a p-adic embedding certificate for (K, pb, p) with embedding σ_a : K →+* ℚ_p, and α ∈ K^×. A valuation certificate for α is a PadicEnclosure (c, N) of σ_a(α) with c ≠ 0 and v_p(c) < N (precision exceeding the valuation); it certifies Padic.valuation(σ_a(α)) = v_p(c) = padicValRat p c. Every α ≠ 0 has one: evaluate σ_a(α) (ED.0/padic-embedding-certificate) at increasing precision until the centre has valuation below the precision, which happens as soon as N > v_p(σ_a(α)). Prime ideals: 𝔭_a := {x ∈ 𝓞_K : ‖σ_a(x)‖ < 1} is a height-one prime of 𝓞_K above p with completion ℚ_p, so ramification index and residue degree are 1, and for α ∈ K^× the 𝔭_a-adic valuation is v_{𝔭_a}(α) = v_p(σ_a(α)); in Mathlib's normalisation HeightOneSpectrum.valuation K α = WithZero.exp(−v_p(σ_a(α))). Certificates multiply: valuation certificates (c, N) of α and (c′, N′) of β, with v = v_p(c) and v′ = v_p(c′), give the certificate (cc′, min(v + N′, N + v′)) of αβ with valuation v + v′.
hypotheses: a is an EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/padic-embedding-certificate; α ≠ 0.
Only primes 𝔭 arising from embeddings K → ℚ_p (degree-one primes) are covered; their valuations are read from σ_a.
proofSteps: If ‖σ_a(α) − c‖ ≤ p^(−N) < p^(−v_p(c)) = ‖c‖, then ‖σ_a(α)‖ = ‖c‖ (ultrametric), so the valuations agree (Padic.norm_eq_zpow_neg_valuation).
Existence: the enclosures of absolute precision n converge to σ_a(α) ≠ 0; once n > v_p(σ_a(α)) the centre has the same valuation (EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/certified-nonvanishing (d)).

σ_a extends by continuity to the completion of K at 𝔭_a, whose image is closed and contains ℚ, hence is ℚ_p; thus e(𝔭_a/p) = f(𝔭_a/p) = 1 and the normalised valuation of K at 𝔭_a is v_p ∘ σ_a. In Mathlib terms the comparison is with IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.valuation, whose value at a uniformiser is WithZero.exp(−1).
Product rule: σ(αβ) − cc′ = σ(α)(σ(β) − c′) + c′(σ(α) − c), so ‖σ(αβ) − cc′‖ ≤ max(p^(−v−N′), p^(−v′−N)) by the ultrametric inequality, and v + v′ < min(v + N′, N + v′).
acceptance: For X² − 2 at p = 7, a = 3: v_7(σ_a(θ − 3)) = 1 and v_7(σ_a(θ − 10)) = 2, from the enclosures (7, 2) and (98, 3) of σ_a(θ − 3) and σ_a(θ − 10).
For K = ℚ the certificate reproduces padicValRat.

nodes.title: Certified enclosures of the height of a number-field element
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field of degree d with power basis pb and a complete list of archimedean embedding certificates (d certificates with pairwise disjoint boxes, so their embeddings σ_1, …, σ_d are all embeddings K →+* ℂ). For x ∈ K let χ_x ∈ ℚ[X] be the characteristic polynomial of multiplication by x (Matrix.charpoly of Algebra.leftMulMatrix pb.basis x) and P_x ∈ ℤ[X] its primitive integral multiple with positive leading coefficient a_x. Then Mathlib's relative height is Height.mulHeight₁ x = a_x · ∏_{i=1}^{d} max(1, |σ_i(x)|): the archimedean factors come from the certificates and the whole non-archimedean part of the height is the integer a_x. The construction heightEnclosure x n returns a RealEnclosure of mulHeight₁ x of absolute precision n: compute a_x exactly (rational linear algebra and a gcd of numerators), take ComplexEnclosures of the σ_i(x) (ED.0/archimedean-embedding-certificate), bound each |σ_i(x)|² in a rational interval from the box corners, apply max(1, ·), multiply the nonnegative intervals endpoint by endpoint, multiply by a_x², and take rational square-root brackets of the endpoints; the precision of the σ_i(x)-enclosures is increased until the final width is at most 2^(−n).
hypotheses: K a number field, pb : PowerBasis ℚ K, and d = [K : ℚ] archimedean embedding certificates with pairwise disjoint boxes.
x ∈ K arbitrary (x = 0 has height 1). No analytic function is evaluated; only |·|² of algebraic numbers is enclosed.
proofSteps: For arbitrary x, first prove charpoly_leftMul_arbitrary using the tower Q⊆Q(x)⊆K and basis invariance. The pinned charpoly_leftMulMatrix theorem covers only a power-basis generator; it is one input, not this bridge.

Over ℂ, χ_x = ∏_{i}(X − σ_i(x)): χ_x = (minpoly ℚ x)^k with k = [K : ℚ(x)], and each conjugate of x is σ_i(x) for exactly k of the d embeddings (NumberField.Embeddings.range_eval_eq_rootSet_minpoly; charpoly_leftMulMatrix for the power basis of ℚ(x) and the tower formula). By Gauss's lemma P_x = F_x^k for the primitive minimal polynomial F_x, so a_x = lead(F_x)^k.

DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.0/height-comparisons gives M(F_x) = absMulHeight₁(x)^(deg x) and DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.0/abs-mul-height-eq-rpow gives absMulHeight₁(x) = mulHeight₁(x)^(1/d); with d = k·deg x this gives mulHeight₁ x = M(F_x)^k = M(P_x) (Polynomial.mahlerMeasure_mul).
M(P_x) = a_x·∏_i max(1, |σ_i(x)|) by Polynomial.mahlerMeasure_eq_leadingCoeff_mul_prod_roots, since the complex roots of P_x with multiplicity are the σ_i(x).

From a ComplexEnclosure with real interval [l_1, u_1] and imaginary interval [l_2, u_2], |σ_i(x)|² lies between the rational numbers dist² of the box to 0 and max(l_1², u_1²) + max(l_2², u_2²); max(1, ·) and products of nonnegative intervals are monotone, so the endpoint products enclose mulHeight₁(x)², and the widths tend to 0 as the precision of the σ_i(x)-enclosures grows.
acceptance: For K = ℚ every enclosure contains max(|num x|, den x) (Mathlib's Rat.mulHeight₁_eq_max).
For the golden ratio φ ∈ ℚ(√5) the enclosure at precision 10 is contained in [1.617, 1.620].

nodes.title: Certified enumeration of points of bounded height
nodes.statement: Let L be a number field of degree d with a power basis pb whose generator θ is integral, together with a complete list of archimedean embedding certificates (d certificates with pairwise disjoint boxes, one for each root of f = minpoly ℚ θ), and let D ≥ 1 and τ ∈ (0, 1] be rationals. boundedHeightPoints L pb D τ is a pair of finite sets (S_<, S_≈) of elements of L such that: (completeness) every x ∈ L with Height.mulHeight₁ x ≤ D lies in S_< ∪ S_≈; (soundness) every x ∈ S_< has mulHeight₁ x < D and every x ∈ S_≈ has |mulHeight₁ x − D| < τ. On ℙ¹(L) (Mathlib's Projectivization L (Fin 2 → L)) the set T = {[x : 1] : x ∈ S_< ∪ S_≈} ∪ {[1 : 0]} contains every point P with Height.logHeight P.rep ≤ log D, and every point of T has logHeight < log(D + τ). Construction: (1) every x with mulHeight₁ x ≤ D has c := natDenominator x ≤ D and y := c·x integral; (2) every embedding σ satisfies |σ(x)| ≤ D, so |σ(y)| ≤ D²; (3) with Δ = disc(pb.basis) ∈ ℤ∖{0}, Δ·y ∈ ℤ[θ], so y = Σ_j b_j θ^j with Δ·b_j ∈ ℤ, and b = V^(−1)(σ_i(y))_i for the Vandermonde matrix V = (σ_i(θ)^j), giving |b_j| ≤ Ω·D² with Ω a rational upper bound for the row sums of |V^(−1)| computed from the root boxes; (4) the finite candidate set is {(Σ_j b_j θ^j)/c : 1 ≤ c ≤ ⌊D⌋, Δ·b ∈ ℤ^d, |b_j| ≤ ΩD²} ∪ {0}; (5) for each candidate an enclosure [l, u] of mulHeight₁ of width < τ (EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/height-enclosure) puts it in S_< if u < D, in S_≈ if l ≤ D ≤ u, and discards it if D < l.
hypotheses: L a number field, pb : PowerBasis ℚ L with IsIntegral ℤ pb.gen; d archimedean embedding certificates with pairwise disjoint boxes (EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/archimedean-embedding-certificate, complete_of_disjoint).
D, τ ∈ ℚ with D ≥ 1 and 0 < τ ≤ 1. For a real bound B on logarithmic height take any rational D ≥ exp(B).
proofSteps: Step (1) is NumberField.natDenominator_le_mulHeight₁ and Algebra.isIntegral_natDenominator_smul.
Step (2): in NumberField.mulHeight₁_eq every factor max(w x, 1)^(mult w) and max(v x, 1) is at least 1, so w(x) ≤ mulHeight₁ x ≤ D for every infinite place w; hence |σ(y)| = c·|σ(x)| ≤ D².

Step (3) is Algebra.discr_mul_isIntegral_mem_adjoin; the Vandermonde inverse is given by Lagrange interpolation, (V^(−1))_(j,i) = coefficient of X^j in f(X)/((X − z_i) f′(z_i)), whose enclosures come from the certificates of EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/archimedean-embedding-certificate.
Completeness follows from (1)–(4): each x of height ≤ D equals (Σ_j b_j θ^j)/c for a candidate (c, b); its enclosure has l ≤ mulHeight₁ x ≤ D, so it is not discarded.
Soundness: u < D gives mulHeight₁ x < D; l ≤ D ≤ u and u − l < τ give |mulHeight₁ x − D| < τ.
ℙ¹: every P ∈ ℙ¹(L) is [1 : 0] (logHeight 0) or [x : 1] (rescale the representative, Height.mulHeight_smul_eq_mulHeight), and Height.logHeight ![x, 1] = logHeight₁ x (Height.logHeight₁_eq_logHeight).
acceptance: For L = ℚ and D = 2 the output covers exactly the seven elements 0, ±1, ±2, ±1/2 and T has eight points of ℙ¹(ℚ).
For L = ℚ(i) and D = 1 the output is {0, ±1, ±i} (Kronecker: height 1 means 0 or a root of unity).

nodes.title: The approximation lattice of a real linear form
nodes.statement: Data: n ≥ 2; real numbers θ_1, …, θ_n (and β for an inhomogeneous form); a positive rational scaling constant C; positive integer weights W_1, …, W_{n−1}; integers φ_1, …, φ_n with |φ_i − Cθ_i| ≤ 1 and φ_n ≠ 0 (and an integer ψ with |ψ − Cβ| ≤ 1). Write Λ(x) = Σ_i x_iθ_i and Λ̃(x) = Σ_i x_iφ_i for x ∈ ℤ^n. The approximation lattice Γ ⊂ ℤ^n is the image of ℤ^n under the integer matrix A whose first n − 1 rows are diag(W_1, …, W_{n−1}) padded by a zero last column and whose last row is (φ_1, …, φ_n); thus Ax = (W_1x_1, …, W_{n−1}x_{n−1}, Λ̃(x)) and the columns of A form a ℤ-basis of Γ, with det A = W_1⋯W_{n−1}·φ_n ≠ 0. The inhomogeneous target is y = (0, …, 0, −ψ). The basic identities are ‖Ax‖² = Σ_{i<n} W_i²x_i² + Λ̃(x)², |Λ̃(x) − CΛ(x)| ≤ Σ_i |x_i|, ‖Ax − y‖² = Σ_{i<n} W_i²x_i² + (Λ̃(x) + ψ)² and |Λ̃(x) + ψ − C(β + Λ(x))| ≤ 1 + Σ_i |x_i|. Rounding contract: from a RealEnclosure [l_i, u_i] of θ_i with C(u_i − l_i) ≤ 1, φ_i := round(C(l_i + u_i)/2) satisfies |φ_i − Cθ_i| ≤ 1/2 + C(u_i − l_i)/2 ≤ 1. The columns of A, as vectors of Euclidean ℝ^n, have integer Gram matrix AᵀA, which is the input of GN.5's exact LLL; a reduced basis AU (U unimodular) gives exact rational coordinates s = (AU)^(−1)y. de Weger takes W_i = γ for all i; Tzanakis–de Weger 1989 take W_i = 1 and C = c_0; Tzanakis–de Weger 1992 §16 take general weights.
hypotheses: n ≥ 2, C ∈ ℚ with C > 0, W_i ∈ ℤ with W_i ≥ 1, φ_n ≠ 0.
The rounding errors satisfy |φ_i − Cθ_i| ≤ 1 and |ψ − Cβ| ≤ 1; these are checked from EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/certified-enclosure enclosures.
proofSteps: Ax is computed coordinatewise from the definition of A (Matrix.mulVec); det A is the product of the diagonal of the lower-triangular-by-blocks matrix (Matrix.det).
‖Ax‖² and ‖Ax − y‖² are sums of squares of the coordinates.
Λ̃(x) − CΛ(x) = Σ_i x_i(φ_i − Cθ_i), so the triangle inequality gives the rounding bounds; adding ψ − Cβ gives the inhomogeneous bound.
Rounding: |round(q) − q| ≤ 1/2 for rational q (Mathlib's round), and |Cm_i − Cθ_i| ≤ C(u_i − l_i)/2 for the midpoint m_i.
The Gram matrix AᵀA is integral, so GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic:GN.5/lll-exact-reduction applies and returns a GN.5/unimodular-basis-certificate.
acceptance: Tzanakis–de Weger 1989, §III.2: n = 3, W_i = 1, C = c_0 = 10^140, φ_i = [c_0μ_i] for μ_i = log|ε_i^(4)/ε_i^(3)| (or log|ε_i^(2)/ε_i^(1)|), ψ = [c_0δ].

nodes.title: Lower bounds for lattice distances from a reduced basis
nodes.statement: Let E be a real inner product space and c_0, …, c_{n−1} ∈ E linearly independent (n ≥ 1, zero-based indices as in GN.5) with Gram–Schmidt vectors c*_i (Mathlib's gramSchmidt), and suppose ‖c*_i‖² ≥ 2^(−(n−1))‖c_0‖² for all i; this holds for every LLL-reduced family at δ = 3/4 (GN.5/lll-gram-schmidt-growth with j = 0) and is de Weger's (3.12). Let Γ be the ℤ-span of the c_i and ‖s‖ the distance from s ∈ ℝ to the nearest integer. (a) Every nonzero v ∈ Γ satisfies ‖v‖² ≥ 2^(−(n−1))‖c_0‖² (de Weger Lemma 3.4, LLL Proposition 1.11). (b) Let y = Σ_i s_i c_i with s_i ∈ ℝ not all integers and i_0 the largest index with s_{i_0} ∉ ℤ. Then every v ∈ Γ satisfies ‖v − y‖² ≥ 2^(−(n−1))·‖s_{i_0}‖²·‖c_0‖² (de Weger Lemma 3.5). (c) Let instead i_0 be any index (not necessarily the largest non-integral one) and δ_1 ≥ 0, δ_2 > 0 with ‖s_i‖ ≤ δ_1 for all i > i_0 and ‖s_{i_0}‖ ≥ δ_2; then every v ∈ Γ satisfies ‖v − y‖ ≥ 2^(−(n−1)/2)·δ_2·‖c_0‖ − (n − 1 − i_0)·δ_1·max_{i>i_0}‖c_i‖ (de Weger Lemma 3.6, zero-based).
hypotheses: E a real inner product space; c : Fin n → E linearly independent; ∀ i, ‖c*_i‖² ≥ 2^(−(n−1))‖c_0‖².
In (b), (c): s : Fin n → ℝ and y = Σ s_i c_i; in (b) i_0 is the largest index with s_{i_0} ∉ ℤ, in (c) i_0 is any index satisfying the bounds stated there.
proofSteps: Write v = Σ r_i c_i with r_i ∈ ℤ. Gram–Schmidt is triangular: c_i ∈ c*_i + span(c*_j : j < i), so the c*_k-coordinate of Σ_i (r_i − s_i) c_i equals r_k − s_k for the largest k with r_k ≠ s_k.
By orthogonality (InnerProductSpace.gramSchmidt_orthogonal), ‖v − y‖² ≥ (r_k − s_k)²‖c*_k‖² ≥ (r_k − s_k)²·2^(−(n−1))‖c_0‖².

Since s_{i_0} ∉ ℤ and r_{i_0} ∈ ℤ we have k ≥ i_0; if k = i_0 then |r_k − s_k| ≥ ‖s_{i_0}‖, and if k > i_0 then s_k ∈ ℤ, r_k ≠ s_k, so |r_k − s_k| ≥ 1 ≥ ‖s_{i_0}‖. This proves (b); (a) is the same argument with s = 0 and v ≠ 0.

(c): let t_i be the nearest integer to s_i for i > i_0 and t_i = s_i for i ≤ i_0, z = Σ t_i c_i; then ‖z − y‖ ≤ (n − 1 − i_0)δ_1 max_{i>i_0}‖c_i‖, and the argument of (b) applied to z (whose largest non-integral coordinate is i_0, with ‖t_{i_0}‖ ≥ δ_2, and |r_k − t_k| ≥ 1 > δ_2 for k > i_0) gives ‖v − z‖ ≥ 2^(−(n−1)/2)δ_2‖c_0‖; conclude by the triangle inequality.
acceptance: Γ = ℤ² with c = (e_1, e_2) (LLL-reduced) and y = (1/2, 0): i_0 = 0 and (b) gives ‖v − y‖² ≥ 2^(−1)·(1/4)·1 = 1/8, while the true minimum is 1/4.
Tzanakis–de Weger 1989, §III.2: for the lattices Γ_1, Γ_2 with c_0 = 10^12, |b_1| > 1.092·10^4 and ‖s_3‖ > 0.143 give l(Γ, y) > 2^(−1)·0.143·1.092·10^4 > 780 (here i_0 is the last index).

nodes.statement: Let Γ be the approximation lattice of EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/linear-form-lattice for the homogeneous form Λ(x) = Σ_i x_iθ_i (|φ_i − Cθ_i| ≤ 1, φ_n ≠ 0). Let X_1, …, X_n ≥ 0, μ > 0 and L ≥ 0 be reals with L² ≥ Σ_{i<n} W_i²X_i² + (Σ_{i=1}^n X_i + μ)², and suppose every nonzero v ∈ Γ satisfies ‖v‖ ≥ L. Then every x ∈ ℤ^n with x ≠ 0 and |x_i| ≤ X_i for all i satisfies C·|Λ(x)| ≥ μ. Consequently, if c, δ > 0 and x is such a vector with |Λ(x)| < c·exp(−δ·max_i|x_i|), then max_i|x_i| < (1/δ)·log(cC/μ). nodes.title: The approximation lattice of a p-adic linear form
nodes.statement: Data: a prime p, m ∈ ℕ, n ≥ 1, p-adic integers β_0, β_1, …, β_{n−1} ∈ ℤ_p and positive integer weights W_1, …, W_n. The normalised p-adic linear form is Λ′(b) = b_n − β_0 − Σ_{j<n} b_jβ_j for b ∈ ℤ^n (homogeneous when β_0 = 0). For x ∈ ℤ_p let x^(m) ∈ [0, p^m − 1] be the integer with x ≡ x^(m) (mod p^m) (Mathlib's PadicInt.appr x m). The lattice Γ_m ⊂ ℤ^n is generated by the columns of the integer matrix A_m whose first n − 1 rows are diag(W_1, …, W_{n−1}) padded by a zero last column and whose last row is W_n·(β_1^(m), …, β_{n−1}^(m), p^m); the target is y_m = (0, …, 0, −W_nβ_0^(m)). Characterisation (Tzanakis–de Weger 1992, Lemma 14; de Weger, Lemmas 3.13 and 3.15 with the sign of y corrected): for b ∈ ℤ^n, p^m divides Λ′(b) in ℤ_p (i.e. ord_p Λ′(b) ≥ m) if and only if (W_1b_1, …, W_nb_n) + y_m ∈ Γ_m. In that case ‖(W_jb_j)_j‖ = ‖v − y_m‖ for the lattice vector v = (W_jb_j)_j + y_m. det A_m = p^m·W_1⋯W_n. The integers β_j^(m) are read from PadicEnclosures of β_j of absolute precision at least m whose centres are p-integral.
hypotheses: p prime, m ∈ ℕ, n ≥ 1, β_j ∈ ℤ_p, W_j ∈ ℤ with W_j ≥ 1.
The β_j are given by EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/certified-enclosure p-adic enclosures of absolute precision ≥ m.
proofSteps: Given b, set λ = (b_n − β_0^(m) − Σ_{j<n} b_jβ_j^(m))/p^m; then A_m(b_1, …, b_{n−1}, λ) = (W_jb_j)_j + y_m, and this vector is in Γ_m iff λ ∈ ℤ (the columns are a basis since det A_m ≠ 0).
λ ∈ ℤ iff p^m divides b_n − β_0^(m) − Σ b_jβ_j^(m) in ℤ, iff p^m divides Λ′(b) in ℤ_p, because β_j − β_j^(m) ∈ p^mℤ_p (PadicInt.appr_spec).
From a PadicEnclosure (c, N) of β_j with N ≥ m and c p-integral, β_j^(m) is the residue of c modulo p^m in [0, p^m − 1].
acceptance: Tzanakis–de Weger 1992, §15E: for p_1 = 2, m = 1152 and W_j = 1 the six-dimensional lattice Γ_m has det = 2^1152.

nodes.title: Reduction of a p-adic linear form
nodes.statement: In the setting of EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/padic-linear-form-lattice, let X_1, …, X_n ≥ 0 and L ≥ 0 be reals with L² > Σ_j W_j²X_j². (a) Inhomogeneous: if ‖v − y_m‖ ≥ L for every v ∈ Γ_m, then every b ∈ ℤ^n with |b_j| ≤ X_j for all j satisfies ord_p Λ′(b) ≤ m − 1, i.e. p^m ∤ Λ′(b). (b) Zero target (y_m = 0, which holds when β_0 = 0 and more generally when β_0^(m) = 0): if ‖v‖ ≥ L for every nonzero v ∈ Γ_m, the same holds for every nonzero b in the box. Consequently, if Λ = ξ·Λ′ with ord_p ξ = κ known and a solution satisfies ord_p Λ(b) ≥ c_1 + c_2·b_k with c_2 > 0, then b_k ≤ (m − 1 + κ − c_1)/c_2. This is Tzanakis–de Weger 1992, Proposition 15 (weights W_j, X_j the a priori bounds, Q = Σ W_j²X_j²), and de Weger, Lemmas 3.14 and 3.16 (unit weights, X_j = X_1, condition ℓ(Γ_μ) > √n·X_1).
hypotheses: Setting of EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/padic-linear-form-lattice.
L is a certified lower bound, e.g. from EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/reduced-basis-distance-lower-bound applied to an LLL-reduced basis of Γ_m.
proofSteps: Suppose p^m ∣ Λ′(b). By the characterisation, v := (W_jb_j)_j + y_m ∈ Γ_m and ‖v − y_m‖² = Σ_j W_j²b_j² ≤ Σ_j W_j²X_j² < L², contradicting ‖v − y_m‖ ≥ L.
In the homogeneous case b ≠ 0 gives v = (W_jb_j)_j ≠ 0, and the same contradiction arises.
ord_p Λ(b) = κ + ord_p Λ′(b) ≤ κ + m − 1, combined with ord_p Λ(b) ≥ c_1 + c_2b_k, bounds b_k.
acceptance: Tzanakis–de Weger 1992, §15E: p_1 = 2, m = 1152, six unknowns with W_j = 1 and X_j = K_0 = 9.844·10^49, so Σ_j W_j²X_j² = 6K_0² and √6·K_0 = 2.41127…·10^50; the certified bound l(Γ_m, y) > 3.98541·10^56 (case I) exceeds it, so ord_2 Λ′ ≤ 1151 and n_1 ≤ 1153. nodes.title: Fincke–Pohst enumeration of lattice points in an ellipsoid
nodes.statement: Input: n ≥ 1, a symmetric matrix G ∈ ℚ^(n×n) (the Gram matrix AᵀA of a lattice basis A), a centre t ∈ ℚ^n and a bound R ∈ ℚ. Quadratic completion (Fincke–Pohst (2.3)) computes rationals q_ij (1 ≤ i ≤ j ≤ n) with x ᵀGx = Σ_i q_ii(x_i + Σ_{j>i} q_ij x_j)² for all x ∈ ℚ^n; the construction requires every pivot q_ii > 0, which holds exactly when G is positive definite. fpEnumeration G t R is the finite set of x ∈ ℤ^n produced by the recursion: T_n = R; for k = n, n − 1, …, 1, given x_{k+1}, …, x_n put U_k = Σ_{j>k} q_kj(x_j − t_j), let x_k run over the integers with q_kk(x_k − t_k + U_k)² ≤ T_k (a finite interval of integers found by exact rational comparison), and put T_{k−1} = T_k − q_kk(x_k − t_k + U_k)². The output is the set of completed vectors x. With the lattice basis A and y = A t, the vectors A x for x in the output are the lattice points v ∈ Γ with ‖v − y‖² ≤ R (EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/short-vector-enumeration-complete). Fincke–Pohst(2.8), p.465, outputs both signs and excludes zero. De Weger's Figure2 instead prints only x before terminating at zero; E25 supplies the missing −x output. This adaptation scans the full integer intervals and also includes 0 when t = 0 and R ≥ 0; the homogeneous use removes 0. If some pivot q_ii is not positive, fpEnumeration G t R is the empty set.
hypotheses: G symmetric with all pivots q_ii > 0; t ∈ ℚ^n; R ∈ ℚ.
All arithmetic is exact over ℚ; square roots are never formed, the integer range at each level is decided by comparing rationals.
proofSteps: Quadratic completion is Gaussian elimination on the symmetric matrix G (an LDLᵀ decomposition: q_ii are the pivots, q_ij = (L)_ji for j > i), valid when every pivot is nonzero; the identity for x ᵀGx follows by expanding (Fincke–Pohst (2.2)–(2.3)).

At level k the condition q_kk(x_k − t_k + U_k)² ≤ T_k with q_kk > 0 defines a bounded set of integers, so every level is finite and the recursion produces a finite set; the coordinate bound is Fincke–Pohst (2.6)–(2.7).

The order of the coordinates and a preliminary reduction of the basis (Fincke–Pohst (2.12), Steps 2–3, using GN.5's LLL) change only the running time, not the output set after the change of coordinates x = Uy.

Replay de Weger §3.6 Figure 2 using exact rational LDL decomposition of positive definite AᵀA. At each depth enumerate all integer coordinates in the remaining squared-radius interval, including its boundary, translated by the rational target; update the nonnegative remaining radius and backtrack. Induction on depth proves exhaustive enumeration; the raw inverse-row cube is an independent finite fallback and completeness cross-check.
acceptance: G = [[2, 1], [1, 2]], t = 0, R = 2 gives the seven vectors of the hexagonal lattice of norm at most 2.
For the lattice of θ = (1, √2), C = 100, φ = (100, 141), the enumeration with R = 73 is {0} and with R = 74 contains ±(−7, 5).

nodes.title: Soundness and completeness of the Fincke–Pohst enumeration
nodes.statement: Let G ∈ ℚ^(n×n) be symmetric with all pivots of its quadratic completion positive, t ∈ ℚ^n and R ∈ ℚ. Then for every x ∈ ℤ^n: x ∈ fpEnumeration G t R ⟺ (x − t)ᵀG(x − t) ≤ R. Lattice form: if A ∈ ℤ^(n×n) is nonsingular with G = AᵀA, Γ = Aℤ^n and y ∈ ℚ^n with t = A^(−1)y, then {v ∈ Γ : ‖v − y‖² ≤ R} = {A x : x ∈ fpEnumeration G t R}. Corollaries used as distance certificates: if the output is empty then ‖v − y‖² > R for every v ∈ Γ; if t = 0 and the output is {0} then ‖v‖² > R for every nonzero v ∈ Γ; in general every v ∈ Γ satisfies ‖v − y‖² ≥ min({R} ∪ {(x − t)ᵀG(x − t) : x in the output}).
hypotheses: G symmetric with positive pivots (EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/short-vector-enumeration); t ∈ ℚ^n; R ∈ ℚ.
In the lattice form A is a nonsingular integer matrix.
proofSteps: (⇐) If (x − t)ᵀG(x − t) ≤ R then, by the quadratic completion, the partial sums Σ_{i≥k} q_ii(x_i − t_i + U_i)² are at most R, so at each level k the coordinate x_k satisfies q_kk(x_k − t_k + U_k)² ≤ T_k for the tail (x_{k+1}, …, x_n); by downward induction on k the tail is produced, hence x is (Fincke–Pohst (2.6)–(2.7)).
(⇒) Every produced x has T_0 = R − Σ_i q_ii(x_i − t_i + U_i)² ≥ 0, i.e. (x − t)ᵀG(x − t) ≤ R by quadraticCompletion_spec.
Lattice form: ‖Ax − y‖² = (x − t)ᵀAᵀA(x − t), and x ↦ A x is a bijection ℤ^n → Γ.
The corollaries follow because every lattice vector outside the output has squared distance > R.

Induction on depth proves exhaustive enumeration; the raw inverse-row cube is an independent finite fallback and completeness cross-check.

Γ = ℤ(1, 0) + ℤ(0, 10), y = (0, −1), R = 1/2: the output is empty, certifying ‖v − y‖² > 1/2 for all v ∈ Γ (the true distance is 1).

nodes.title: Residual enumeration for a real linear form
nodes.statement: Let Γ, A, y (or y = 0) be as in EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/linear-form-lattice for the form β + Λ (β = 0 and ε = 0 in the homogeneous case, ε = 1 otherwise), let X_1, …, X_n ≥ 0 and K_0 ≥ ε + Σ_i X_i be rationals, R = Σ_{i<n} W_i²X_i² + K_0², and E = fpEnumeration(AᵀA, A^(−1)y, R). Then every x ∈ ℤ^n with |x_i| ≤ X_i for all i satisfies x ∈ E or C·|β + Λ(x)| > K_0 − ε − Σ_i|x_i| ≥ 0. Consequently, when K_0 > ε + Σ_i X_i, all solutions in the box of |β + Λ(x)| < c·exp(−δ max_i|x_i|) are among the finitely many x ∈ E checked individually, together with those satisfying max_i|x_i| < (1/δ)·log(cC/(K_0 − ε − Σ_i|x_i|)) (de Weger, Lemma 3.8 and the procedure after it).
hypotheses: Setting of EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/linear-form-lattice; X_i, K_0 rational with K_0 ≥ ε + Σ X_i.
proofSteps: If x ∉ E then ‖Ax − y‖² > R by EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/short-vector-enumeration-complete, and Σ_{i<n} W_i²x_i² ≤ Σ_{i<n} W_i²X_i², so |Λ̃(x) + ψ| > K_0 (ψ = 0 when homogeneous).
C|β + Λ(x)| ≥ |Λ̃(x) + ψ| − ε − Σ_i|x_i| > K_0 − ε − Σ_i|x_i| (the rounding bound of the lattice construction).
With |β + Λ(x)| < c·exp(−δX) this gives the stated bound for X = max|x_i|; this is de Weger's (3.25).
acceptance: For θ = (1, √2), C = 100, φ = (100, 141), W_1 = 1, X_1 = X_2 = 3 and K_0 = 6: R = 9 + 36 = 45, and every x with |x_i| ≤ 3 is either an enumerated short vector or satisfies 100|x_1 + x_2√2| > 6 − Σ|x_i| ≥ 0; the shortest nonzero vector of Γ is A(−7, 5) = (−7, 5) with squared length 74 > 45, so E = {0}.

nodes.title: Lattice exclusion certificates for linear forms
nodes.statement: A lattice exclusion certificate is finite exact data, checked by rational and integer arithmetic only, of one of two kinds. Real kind: (i) the data of EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/linear-form-lattice (C, W, φ and, for an inhomogeneous form, ψ), with the enclosures certifying |φ_i − Cθ_i| ≤ 1 and |ψ − Cβ| ≤ 1; (ii) rational box bounds X_1, …, X_n ≥ 0 and a rational margin μ > 0; (iii) a distance witness for the matrix A and target y (y = 0 when homogeneous); (iv) the inequality L² ≥ Σ_{i<n} W_i²X_i² + (ε + Σ_i X_i + μ)² with ε = 1 (inhomogeneous) or 0 (homogeneous). p-adic kind: (i) the data of EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/padic-linear-form-lattice (p, m, W, β_j^(m) from enclosures of precision ≥ m); (ii) box bounds X_1, …, X_n ≥ 0; (iii) a distance witness for A_m and y_m; (iv) L² > Σ_j W_j²X_j². A distance witness for (A, y) is either an LLL witness — a GN.5 unimodular certificate (U, U^(−1)) such that the columns c_0, …, c_{n−1} of AU are LLL-reduced at δ = 3/4 (checked on exact rational Gram–Schmidt data), the exact vector s = (AU)^(−1)y, and L² = 2^(−(n−1))·‖s_{i_0}‖²·‖c_0‖² with i_0 the largest index with s_{i_0} ∉ ℤ (rejected if s ∈ ℤ^n), or L² = 2^(−(n−1))‖c_0‖² when y = 0 — or an enumeration witness: a rational R ≥ 0 and E = fpEnumeration(AᵀA, A^(−1)y, R), with L² the minimum of R and of ‖Ax − y‖² over x ∈ E (over x ∈ E∖{0} when y = 0). The certified region is the box {x ∈ ℤ^n : |x_i| ≤ X_i} (minus 0 whenever the target y, resp. y_m, is 0, which includes the homogeneous case). The raw fallback records A,y,Ainv∈Q^(n×n), B>0, 0≤L²≤B² and D∈N. Check AAinv=AinvA=I, Σ_j |Ainv_ij|(|y_j|+B)≤D for each row, and L²≤||Ax-y||² for every x∈[-D,D]^n eligible for the zero-target branch. If ||Ax-y||²<B², all coordinates lie in this checked box; otherwise L²≤B² gives the bound. Thus no real Gram–Schmidt inequality is trusted by this fallback. The raw p-adic form stores p,m∈N, positive integral W, canonical residues r₀,r_j∈{0,…,p^m−1}, rational X≥0 and RawDistanceCertificate data. Its checker verifies primality, every residue range, all weights and bounds, the weighted triangular matrix A (last row W_n(r₁,…,r_{n−1},p^m)), target y=(0,…,0,−W_n r₀), the full rational distance replay and Σ(W_j X_j)²<L². The semantic β₀,β_j∈Z_p occur only in check_sound through independently certified equalities appr(β₀,m)=r₀ and appr(β_j,m)=r_j.
hypotheses: All entries are integers or rationals; θ_i, β and β_j enter only through their enclosures (EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/certified-enclosure).
n ≥ 2 for the real kind and n ≥ 1 for the p-adic kind.
proofSteps: The LLL conditions at δ = 3/4 are GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic:GN.5/lll-reduced; with an integral basis the Gram–Schmidt data are rationals with denominators the integer potentials of GN.5/lll-integer-potential, so the check is exact.
The coordinate vector s is obtained by exact rational linear algebra; ‖s_{i_0}‖ = min(fract s_{i_0}, 1 − fract s_{i_0}) is rational.
Every field of the certificate is decidable, so the certificate is checked by evaluation; its meaning is EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/exclusion-certificate-sound.

Raw soundness splits at normSq<B². The inverse row bounds put every possible violating vector in the finite cube. Exact endpoint inequalities and C>0 extend rounding to the actual enclosed values; then use the real exclusion inequality.

From CN.4 certified enclosures choose rounded φ,ψ and checked endpoints. From GN.5 exact LLL use exact rational Gram–Schmidt data; if its lower-bound check cannot be expressed with the supplier carrier, use the exhaustive cube fallback. Choose B,D and compute the rational minimum over the cube; passing the separation check is the producer success condition, never a guarantee of success for every input.

For the raw p-adic checker, a vector b satisfying the residue congruence yields v=Wb+y=Aa. If r₀=0, b≠0 and positive weights imply a≠0. The raw distance bound then gives L²≤||Aa−y||²=Σ(W_j b_j)²≤Σ(W_j X_j)²<L², a contradiction. PadicInt.appr_spec and the integer-cast divisibility comparison identify the congruence with p^m dividing the actual p-adic linear form; no semantic distance witness is supplied.
acceptance: Tzanakis–de Weger 1989, §III.2 supplies two real inhomogeneous certificates (c_0 = 10^140 and 10^12).
Tzanakis–de Weger 1992, §15E supplies twelve p-adic certificates (cases I, III and V for each of p = 2, 3, 5, 7, with m = 1152, 672, 480, 384).

nodes.title: Soundness of lattice exclusion certificates
nodes.statement: Let a lattice exclusion certificate (EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/exclusion-certificate) check. Real kind: every x ∈ ℤ^n with |x_i| ≤ X_i for all i (and x ≠ 0 whenever the target y = (0, …, 0, −ψ) is 0, in particular in the homogeneous case) satisfies C·|β + Λ(x)| ≥ μ; hence for c, δ > 0 no such x satisfies |β + Λ(x)| < c·exp(−δ·max_i|x_i|) with max_i|x_i| ≥ (1/δ)·log(cC/μ). p-adic kind: every b ∈ ℤ^n with |b_j| ≤ X_j (and b ≠ 0 whenever y_m = 0, i.e. β_0^(m) = 0, in particular when β_0 = 0) satisfies ord_p Λ′(b) ≤ m − 1. This is the stage's acceptance: a lattice basis, a certified reduction, and a proved lower bound that excludes every integer vector of the specified region.
hypotheses: The certificate's Boolean check is true.
θ_i, β, β_j are the numbers enclosed by the certificate's enclosures.
proofSteps: The distance witness is sound: an LLL witness by EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/reduced-basis-distance-lower-bound (a)/(b), using GN.5/lll-gram-schmidt-growth for the hypothesis on ‖c*_i‖ and GN.5/unimodular-basis-certificate for AUℤ^n = Aℤ^n; an enumeration witness by EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/short-vector-enumeration-complete.
Real kind: apply EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/homogeneous-reduction or EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/inhomogeneous-reduction with L from the witness and the checked inequality (iv).
p-adic kind: apply EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/padic-reduction.

The raw p-adic form uses RawPadicExclusionCertificate.not_congruent and check_sound; the only external semantics are the certified coefficient residues. The integer nondivisibility conclusion is stronger and safer than applying an integer-valued valuation to the exact-zero branch.

nodes.title: Certified enclosures of logarithms and arguments of embedded algebraic numbers
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, σ : K →+* ℂ a complex embedding, α ∈ K with α ≠ 0, and let B = (R, I) be a closed rational box (ComputationalNumberTheory:CN.4/complex-box-denotation) with σ(α) ∈ B, delivered by an ED.0 archimedean embedding certificate (EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/archimedean-embedding-certificate). Let m and M be the exact rational minimum and maximum of x² + y² over (x, y) ∈ R × I (m > 0 exactly when 0 ∉ B). For a precision P ∈ ℕ, logAbsEnclosure(B, P) is the closed rational interval obtained by outward dyadic rounding at precision P (ComputationalNumberTheory:CN.4/outward-dyadic-rounding) of [l/2, u/2], where l is the lower end of the CN.4 enclosure of Real.log m and u the upper end of the CN.4 enclosure of Real.log M, both at precision P (Real.log ‖z‖ = Real.log(x² + y²)/2); it returns none when 0 ∈ B. When B is contained in the complement of the closed half-line (−∞, 0] (that is, min R > 0, or min I > 0, or max I < 0), argEnclosure(B, P) is the closed rational interval obtained from the CN.4 arctangent enclosures at precision P of the corner values (at a corner (x, y): arctan(y/x) when x > 0, and sign(y)·π/2 − arctan(x/y) when y ≠ 0, with π/2 enclosed as 2·arctanEnclosure(1, P + 2) by Real.arctan_one) rounded outward at precision P; otherwise it returns none. Conventions pinned: log is Mathlib's principal logarithm Complex.log z = Real.log ‖z‖ + i·Complex.arg z with Complex.arg z ∈ (−π, π]; logarithms of real positive numbers are Real.log. Soundness: Real.log ‖σ(α)‖ ∈ logAbsEnclosure(B, P) and Complex.arg σ(α) ∈ argEnclosure(B, P) whenever these are defined; the outputs are RealEnclosures in the sense of EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/certified-enclosure. Precision budget: if B has diameter w and 0 < ρ⁻ ≤ ‖z‖ for all z ∈ B, then the width of logAbsEnclosure(B, P) is less than w/ρ⁻ + 3·2^{−P} (2^{−P} from the halved CN.4 endpoint enclosures, less than 2·2^{−P} from outward rounding) and that of argEnclosure(B, P) is less than (π/2)·w/ρ⁻ + 5·2^{−P} (3·2^{−P} from the corner and π/2 enclosures), so a requested absolute error ε is met by refining the box to diameter at most ρ⁻ε/4 and taking 2^{−P} ≤ ε/16.
hypotheses: σ(α) lies in the box B (the ED.0 certificate's soundness statement); the enclosure claims nothing about points outside B
Failure (0 ∈ B, or a box meeting the branch cut for the argument) is returned as data and never as an enclosure
proofSteps: For z in B, m ≤ ‖z‖² ≤ M, Real.log ‖z‖ = Real.log ‖z‖²/2 and Real.log is monotone on (0, ∞), so Real.log ‖z‖ ∈ [Real.log m/2, Real.log M/2]; the CN.4 log enclosures of the two rationals m, M and outward rounding give rational endpoints enclosing that interval.

On the complement of (−∞, 0] the function Complex.arg is continuous, and on a box avoiding the closed negative half-axis its extreme values are attained at corners; at a corner (x, y) the value is arctan(y/x) for x > 0 and sign(y)·π/2 − arctan(x/y) for y ≠ 0 (this covers x ≤ 0, where y ≠ 0 on such a box); enclose each with the CN.4 arctangent enclosure, and π/2 as 2·arctan 1 (Mathlib's Real.arctan_one) with the CN.4 arctangent enclosure of 1 at precision P + 2; the six-digit bounds Real.pi_gt_d6 and Real.pi_lt_d6 do not reach precision 2^{−P} for P ≥ 20.

Width: |Real.log ‖z‖ − Real.log ‖z′‖| ≤ ‖z − z′‖/ρ⁻ and |arg z − arg z′| ≤ (π/2)‖z − z′‖/ρ⁻ on the box (mean value theorem along the segment and the arc), the CN.4 enclosures add at most 2^{−P} (logarithm, after halving) and 3·2^{−P} (argument: corner arctangents and π/2), and outward rounding adds less than 2·2^{−P} (ComputationalNumberTheory:CN.4/outward-rounding-width).
acceptance: For the box of the real root ∛2 of X³ − 2 refined to width 10^{−12}, logAbsEnclosure at P = 40 has width below 10^{−11} and contains Real.log 2/3.
No enclosure is returned for a box containing 0, so a nonvanishing claim never rests on an interval around 0.

nodes.title: Certified evaluation of Matveev's constant
nodes.statement: Fix integers n ≥ 1 (the number of logarithms) and D ≥ 1 (a degree bound). Put e⁺ := 27182818286/10¹⁰ (so exp 1 < e⁺ by Real.exp_one_lt_d9). A MatveevConstantCertificate for (n, D) consists of rationals A_1, …, A_n with A_j ≥ 16/100, a rational s⁺ ≥ 0 with (s⁺)² ≥ n (so s⁺ ≥ √n), a rational ℓ⁺ ≥ Real.log D (the upper end of the CN.4 enclosure of Real.log D; ℓ⁺ = 0 is allowed for D = 1), and a rational c satisfying the exact rational inequality c ≥ Ĉ(n)·D²·(1 + ℓ⁺)·A_1⋯A_n, where Ĉ(n) := max(min(e⁺n/2·30^{n+3}·n³·s⁺, 2^{6n+20}), min((1/2)(e⁺n/2)²·30^{n+3}·n³·s⁺, 2^{6n+20})) is a rational number with Ĉ(n) ≥ C_1(n, κ) for κ = 1 and κ = 2, C_1(n, κ) = min{κ^{−1}(en/2)^κ·30^{n+3}·n^{3.5}, 2^{6n+20}} being the constant of Matveev's Corollary 2.3 (DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.3/matveev-corollary-linear-form-bound). The certificate is admissible for a number field K ⊆ ℂ (given with σ : K →+* ℂ) with [K : ℚ] ≤ D, elements α_1, …, α_n ∈ K^× and nonzero complex numbers λ_1, …, λ_n with exp λ_j = σ(α_j), when A_j ≥ D·h_j⁺ and A_j ≥ |λ_j|⁺ for every j, where h_j⁺ ≥ NumberField.absLogHeight₁ α_j is obtained from EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/height-enclosure, converted by h = Real.log(mulHeight₁)/[K : ℚ] (DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.0/abs-mul-height-eq-rpow) and the upper end of ED.2/logarithm-enclosure and |λ_j|⁺ ≥ |λ_j| is read off from ED.2/logarithm-enclosure (for λ_j = Complex.log σ(α_j) + 2πik_j, |λ_j| ≤ |Real.log ‖σα_j‖| + |Complex.arg σα_j + 2πk_j|). The value used downstream is c: for every b ∈ ℤ^n with Λ := Σ b_jλ_j ≠ 0, Real.log |Λ| > −c·(1 + Real.log B*), B* := max_j |b_j| (ED.2/certified-linear-form-lower-bound). Every comparison in the certificate is an exact comparison of rationals; the name of Matveev's theorem supplies no number, and every number is computed here. The real/complex distinction κ of Matveev is not needed by the certificate because Ĉ(n) dominates both values; a logarithm λ_j with σ(α_j) = 1 and λ_j = 0 is never part of the family (such a term is removed from the linear form before the certificate is formed).
hypotheses: n ≥ 1, D ≥ 1; A_j ≥ 0.16 is part of the certificate and is essential: Corollary 2.3 is stated under (2.4)
[K : ℚ] ≤ D is enough: the bound is increasing in D and the admissibility conditions are monotone in D
λ_j ≠ 0 for every j; terms with λ_j = 0 are deleted beforehand, and their coefficients do not enter B*
proofSteps: Ĉ(n) ≥ C_1(n, κ): Real.exp_one_lt_d9 gives e < e⁺, (s⁺)² ≥ n gives n^{3.5} = n³√n ≤ n³s⁺, and each argument of the minimum is monotone in e and in n^{3.5}; the maximum over κ ∈ {1, 2} covers both fields K ⊆ ℝ and K ⊄ ℝ.

Degree monotonicity: if [K : ℚ] = D′ ≤ D then A_j ≥ D·h(α_j) ≥ D′·h(α_j), so the A_j satisfy Matveev's (2.4) for D′, and C_1·D′²·log(eD′) ≤ Ĉ(n)·D²·(1 + ℓ⁺) because log(eD′) = 1 + Real.log D′ ≤ 1 + ℓ⁺.

Admissibility uses NumberField.absLogHeight₁ α_j ≤ h_j⁺ (EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/height-enclosure with DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.0/abs-mul-height-eq-rpow) and |λ_j| ≤ |λ_j|⁺ (ED.2/logarithm-enclosure).
acceptance: The certificate with n = 2, D = 1, A = (7/10, 11/10), c = 8·10⁸ is accepted; with c = 7·10⁸ it is rejected.
Citing Matveev's name supplies no number: every admissible certificate carries its rational c and the checks that bound C_1(n, κ)·D²·log(eD)·∏A_j by it.

sources.match: TdW use Waldschmidt's bound (Acta Arith. 37 (1980), their reference [30]) with constants C_7, C_8 computed in their Appendix II; this node replaces that input by Matveev's Corollary 2.3 (imported from DT.3) with C_7 := c and C_8 := 1.

nodes.title: Certified lower bound for a linear form in logarithms
nodes.statement: Let c be the value of a MatveevConstantCertificate for (n, D) (ED.2/certified-linear-form-constant) admissible for a number field K with σ : K →+* ℂ and [K : ℚ] ≤ D, α_1, …, α_n ∈ K^× and nonzero logarithms λ_1, …, λ_n (exp λ_j = σ(α_j)). Then for every b ∈ ℤ^n with Λ := b_1λ_1 + ⋯ + b_nλ_n ≠ 0: Real.log |Λ| > −c·(1 + Real.log B*), B* := max_j |b_j| ≥ 1; equivalently |Λ| > exp(−c(1 + Real.log B*)). In Tzanakis–de Weger's notation (Lemma 2.3): |Λ| > exp(−C_7(log A + C_8)) with C_7 := c, C_8 := 1, A := B*.
hypotheses: Λ ≠ 0 (nothing is claimed for Λ = 0; nonvanishing is proved separately in each application, never inferred from a numerical enclosure near 0)
Admissibility of the certificate for (K, σ, α, λ)
proofSteps: Let D′ := [K : ℚ] ≤ D. By admissibility and the monotonicity step of ED.2/certified-linear-form-constant, A_j ≥ max{D′h(α_j), |λ_j|, 0.16}.
Apply DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.3/matveev-corollary-linear-form-bound to σ(K) ⊆ ℂ, σ(α_j), λ_j and b, with B* in place of B: Real.log |Λ| > −C_1(n, κ)·D′²·A_1⋯A_n·log(eD′)·log(eB*).
Bound C_1(n, κ)·D′²·log(eD′)·∏A_j ≤ c by the certificate inequality and log(eB*) = 1 + Real.log B*.
acceptance: For α = (2, 3) with real logarithms, n = 2, D = 1 and c = 8·10⁸: every (b_1, b_2) ≠ (0, 0) satisfies |b_1 log 2 + b_2 log 3| > exp(−8·10⁸(1 + log max(|b_1|, |b_2|))) (Λ ≠ 0 because 2^{b_1}3^{b_2} ≠ 1 by unique factorisation).

nodes.title: Certified evaluation of Yu's p-adic constant
nodes.statement: Fix n ≥ 2, a degree bound d ≥ 1 and a prime p. A YuConstantCertificate for (n, d, p) consists of rationals h_1, …, h_n, a rational λ_p⁻ with 0 < λ_p⁻ ≤ Real.log p and λ_p⁻ ≤ h_j for all j (CN.4 enclosure of Real.log p), a rational L⁺ ≥ Real.log(10·n·d·h′) with h′ := max(h_1, …, h_n, 1), and a rational Φ⁺ satisfying the exact rational inequality Φ⁺ ≥ 22000·(9.5(n + 1)d)^{2(n+1)}·(λ_p⁻)^{−(n+1)}·(p^d − 1)·h_1⋯h_n·L⁺, which dominates Yu's Φ = 22000·(9.5(n+1)d/√(log p))^{2(n+1)}·(p^{f_𝔭} − 1)·h_1⋯h_n·log(10ndh′) for every prime 𝔭 above p (f_𝔭 ≤ d). It is admissible for nonzero algebraic numbers α_1, …, α_n generating a number field of degree at most d when h_j ≥ h_j⁺ ≥ NumberField.absLogHeight₁ α_j (EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/height-enclosure, converted by h = Real.log(mulHeight₁)/[K : ℚ] (DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.0/abs-mul-height-eq-rpow) and the upper end of ED.2/logarithm-enclosure), h_j ≥ |log α_j|⁺/10 (ED.2/logarithm-enclosure, principal logarithm; the factor 1/(10d) of Yu is replaced by 1/10, which is admissible for every d ≥ 1) and h_j ≥ λ_p⁻ is replaced by the requirement h_j ≥ ℓ_p⁺ for the upper end ℓ_p⁺ of the enclosure of Real.log p. The value used downstream is Φ⁺: for b ∈ ℤ^n ∖ {0} with α^b ≠ 1, the p-adic valuation v_p (normalised by v_p(p) = 1) of α^b − 1 under any embedding into a finite extension of ℚ_p satisfies v_p(α^b − 1) < Φ⁺·Real.log(d·max(|b_1|, …, |b_n|, 3)) (ED.2/certified-padic-lower-bound). For α_j ∈ ℚ this specialises to d = 1, f_𝔭 = 1, h_j ≥ max(log H(α_j), |log α_j|/10, log p), the form of DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.3/yu-p-adic-lower-bound.
hypotheses: n ≥ 2 (Yu's statement; a single p-adic unit is handled by DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.4/one-term-p-adic-lower-bound or by adjoining a second term with zero coefficient)
The α_j are nonzero and α_1^{b_1}⋯α_n^{b_n} ≠ 1 in the application; the constant itself is pure rational arithmetic
proofSteps: Monotonicity in the residue degree: p^{f_𝔭} − 1 ≤ p^d − 1 since f_𝔭 ≤ [ℚ(α) : ℚ] ≤ d (Yu remarks the same on p. 242).
(√(log p))^{2(n+1)} = (log p)^{n+1} ≥ (λ_p⁻)^{n+1}; d ↦ (9.5(n+1)d)^{2(n+1)} and d ↦ log(10ndh′) are increasing, so the certificate dominates Φ computed with the true degree.

The hypotheses h_j ≥ max(h(α_j), |log α_j|/(10d_0), log p) of DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.3/yu-explicit-p-adic-bound for the true degree d_0 ≤ d follow from h_j ≥ h_j⁺, h_j ≥ |log α_j|⁺/10 and h_j ≥ ℓ_p⁺.
acceptance: For p = 5, n = 2, d = 1, α = (2, 3): the least admissible Φ⁺ at precision 2^{−20} exceeds 10^{14}, and the certificate records it as an exact rational.
The p-adic source (Yu 1994) is registered separately from the archimedean one (Matveev 2000).

nodes.title: Certified upper bound for the p-adic valuation of a multiplicative form
nodes.statement: Let Φ⁺ be the value of a YuConstantCertificate for (n, d, p) (ED.2/certified-padic-linear-form-constant) admissible for nonzero algebraic numbers α_1, …, α_n of a number field K, [K : ℚ] ≤ d, and let ι : K → L be a field embedding into a finite extension L of ℚ_p, with v_p the valuation of L normalised by v_p(p) = 1. Then for every b ∈ ℤ^n ∖ {0} with α_1^{b_1}⋯α_n^{b_n} ≠ 1: v_p(ι(α_1^{b_1}⋯α_n^{b_n}) − 1) < Φ⁺·Real.log(d·max(|b_1|, …, |b_n|, 3)). For α_j ∈ ℚ the valuation is padicValRat p.
hypotheses: b ≠ 0 and α^b ≠ 1 (nonvanishing of α^b − 1 is part of the hypothesis; it is proved structurally in each application)
Admissibility of the certificate
proofSteps: The prime 𝔭 of ℚ(α_1, …, α_n) induced by ι lies above p; v_p(ι(x)) = ord_𝔭(x)/e_𝔭 ≤ ord_𝔭(x) for x ≠ 0 with ord_𝔭(x) ≥ 0, and the claim is trivial when v_p(ι(α^b) − 1) ≤ 0.
DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.3/yu-explicit-p-adic-bound gives ord_𝔭(α^b − 1) < Φ·log(d_0B) with the true degree d_0 ≤ d; Φ ≤ Φ⁺ by the certificate and log(d_0B) ≤ log(dB).
acceptance: For p = 7 and α = (2, 3) ∈ ℚ², with a certificate admissible for (n, d) = (2, 1): for every (b_1, b_2) ≠ 0, padicValRat 7 (2^{b_1}3^{b_2} − 1) < Φ⁺·log max(|b_1|, |b_2|, 3); e.g. (b_1, b_2) = (1, 2) gives padicValRat 7 (17) = 0 and (3, −1) gives padicValRat 7 (8/3 − 1) = 0, while 2³ − 1 = 7 gives valuation 1, all below the bound.

nodes.title: Discrete-logarithm certificates for p-adic multiplicative forms
nodes.statement: Let p be a prime and 𝒪 either ℤ_p or the ring of integers of a finite extension L of ℚ_p, with maximal ideal 𝔓 and a fixed exact presentation of the finite rings 𝒪/𝔓^t (for L given by a defining polynomial over ℚ_p, through the ED.0 p-adic embedding certificates of the relevant elements: EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/padic-embedding-certificate). Let γ_0, γ_1, …, γ_n ∈ 𝒪^× be units, known modulo 𝔓^t. A discrete-logarithm certificate at level t consists of an exponent e ≥ 1, an element g ∈ 𝒪 with g ≡ 1 (mod 𝔓), an integer M ≥ 1, and integers ℓ_0, …, ℓ_n ∈ [0, p^M), such that the following exact congruences hold in 𝒪/𝔓^t: g^{p^M} ≡ 1, g^{p^{M−1}} ≢ 1, and γ_i^e ≡ g^{ℓ_i} for i = 0, …, n. Its congruence lattice is Γ := {b ∈ ℤ^n : Σ_{i≥1} b_iℓ_i ≡ 0 (mod p^M)} and its target coset is Γ_0 := {b ∈ ℤ^n : ℓ_0 + Σ_{i≥1} b_iℓ_i ≡ 0 (mod p^M)}; both are presented by EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/padic-linear-form-lattice after normalisation: let κ := min_{i≥1, ℓ_i ≠ 0} v_p(ℓ_i) < M, attained at a nonzero ℓ_k; if ℓ_0 ≠ 0 and v_p(ℓ_0) < κ then Γ_0 = ∅; otherwise b ∈ Γ_0 exactly when p^{M−κ} divides Λ′(b) := b_k − β_0 − Σ_{i≠k} b_iβ_i with the p-adic integers β_0 := −ℓ_0/ℓ_k and β_i := −ℓ_i/ℓ_k, which is ED.1's normalised form at level m = M − κ (de Weger's μ_0 is this κ). If every ℓ_i (i ≥ 1) is zero (equivalently divisible by p^M under the exponent ranges), then Γ = ℤ^n; Γ_0 is all of ℤ^n if ℓ_0 = 0, and empty otherwise. This also handles n = 0 without taking an empty pivot minimum. Soundness: for b ∈ ℤ^n and ζ ∈ 𝒪^× with ζ^e = 1 (for instance ζ = ±1 when e is even), if ζγ_0∏_{i≥1}γ_i^{b_i} ≡ 1 (mod 𝔓^t), equivalently ord_𝔓(ζγ_0∏γ_i^{b_i} − 1) ≥ t, then b ∈ Γ_0. Standard data over ℚ_p: for odd p, g = 1 + p, t = M + 1, e = p − 1; for p = 2, g = 5, t = M + 2, e = 2; the order conditions then hold by lifting the exponent, and ℓ_i exists for every rational p-adic unit γ_i. In a finite extension the certificate exists whenever the γ_i^e generate a cyclic subgroup of (𝒪/𝔓^t)^× of p-power order, as for the norm-one elements of a quadratic extension that occur in the Thue–Mahler reduction. No p-adic logarithm and no approximation enters: every check is modular exponentiation in a finite ring. Zero coefficients are omitted when choosing κ, and ℓ_0 = 0 always satisfies p^κ ∣ ℓ_0; this is essential because Mathlib padicValRat p 0 = 0. The prime hypothesis is stored in the certificate, as are 0 ≤ ℓ_i < p^M.
hypotheses: γ_i are 𝔓-adic units; the certificate is a finite list of integers checked by exact arithmetic modulo 𝔓^t
Only the implication 'congruence ⇒ lattice membership' is claimed; the lattice may be larger than the set of exponent vectors with the congruence, which keeps every reduction based on it sound
proofSteps: Since g ≡ 1 (mod 𝔓), the image of g in the finite group (𝒪/𝔓^t)^× lies in the p-group (1 + 𝔓)/(1 + 𝔓^t); its order is a power of p, and the two congruences make it exactly p^M.
If x := ζγ_0∏γ_i^{b_i} ≡ 1 then x^e ≡ 1, and x^e = ζ^e·γ_0^e∏(γ_i^e)^{b_i} ≡ g^{ℓ_0 + Σ b_iℓ_i}; hence p^M divides ℓ_0 + Σ b_iℓ_i.

Standard data: DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.3/p-adic-valuation-of-power-minus-one gives v_p((1 + p)^k − 1) = 1 + v_p(k) for odd p and v_2(5^k − 1) = 2 + v_2(k), so 1 + p has order exactly p^M modulo p^{M+1} and 5 has order exactly 2^M modulo 2^{M+2}; the groups (1 + pℤ_p)/(1 + p^{M+1}ℤ_p) and (1 + 4ℤ_2)/(1 + 2^{M+2}ℤ_2) have orders p^M and 2^M, hence are generated by them, and γ^{p−1} ≡ 1 (mod p) (Fermat) resp. γ² ≡ 1 (mod 8) puts γ^e in them.

Comparison with the sources: for 𝒪 = ℤ_p, p odd, ℓ_i ≡ log_p(γ_i^{p−1})/log_p(1 + p) (mod p^M), so Γ_0 is de Weger's lattice Γ_μ of the p-adic linear form in logarithms; the certificate replaces the approximation of p-adic logarithms by exact discrete logarithms.
acceptance: For p = 5, M = 2: the certificate for γ = (2, 3) has (ℓ_2, ℓ_3) with 6^{ℓ_2} ≡ 16 and 6^{ℓ_3} ≡ 81 (mod 125), and its lattice {b : b_2ℓ_2 + b_3ℓ_3 ≡ 0 (mod 25)} contains every b with 2^{b_2}3^{b_3} ≡ ±1 (mod 125).

nodes.title: Exponent reduction chains
nodes.statement: For any finite exponent index Fin q (including q=0) and S⊆Z^q, a componentwise reduction chain consists of k steps, nonnegative X_j∈Q^q, each coordinate antitone in j, finite exceptional sets E_j and the implication a∈S ∧ (∀i,|a_i|≤X_{j,i}) ⇒ (∀i,|a_i|≤X_{j+1,i}) ∨ a∈E_j. Each implication is supplied by a real, p-adic or complete-enumeration reduction. Finite induction gives the final box or an exception. A weighted scalar convenience chain is separately named WeightedExponentReductionChain and means X_{j,i}=w_i X_j, with every w_i≥1 for the conversion. S-unit certificates use the vector chain directly, so a step may lower f(p) without lowering f(q) for q≠p.
hypotheses: Each step carries its own certificate; a chain with a step lacking one is not a chain
Bounds may be different per coordinate through the weights w (TdW 1992 §15 use weights W_j to balance the bounds on the n_i and a_i)
proofSteps: Induction on j: the base case is the hypothesis H_w(a) ≤ X_0; the step is the implication of step j.

For step type (a), the ED.1 real reduction theorem states exactly that no a in the box H_w(a) ≤ X_{j−1} satisfies |Λ(a)| < K_1 exp(−K_2 H_w(a)) with H_w(a) > X_j; for (b) the ED.1 p-adic theorem states that no a in the box lies in the lattice or coset outside the region H_w(a) ≤ X_j; for (c) the completeness theorem of the enumeration places every such a in E_j.
acceptance: The chain of TdW §III.2 (initial bound of size 10^{40}, reduced in several steps to two-digit bounds) is an instance with real steps only.

nodes.title: Thue equations and their solution sets
nodes.statement: A Thue equation is given by g ∈ ℤ[X] with n := g.natDegree ≥ 3, g irreducible over ℚ (its image in ℚ[X] is irreducible), and m ∈ ℤ with m ≠ 0. Its form is F := Polynomial.homogenize g n, evaluated at (x, y) ∈ ℤ² by MvPolynomial.eval ![x, y], and its solution set is thueSolutions g m := {(x, y) ∈ ℤ × ℤ : F(x, y) = m}. Conventions pinned for the Thue part: g = Σ_{k=0}^{n} g_k X^k ∈ ℤ[X] with n = g.natDegree, f_0 := g_n ≠ 0 its leading coefficient; the binary form is F := Polynomial.homogenize g n ∈ ℤ[X_0, X_1], so F(x, y) = Σ_k g_k x^k y^{n−k} and F(x, 1) = g(x) (Tzanakis–de Weger write F = Σ f_i X^{n−i}Y^i, so f_i = g_{n−i}); ξ^{(1)}, …, ξ^{(s)} are the real roots of g and ξ^{(s+1)}, …, ξ^{(s+2t)} the non-real ones with ξ^{(s+t+i)} = conj ξ^{(s+i)}, s + 2t = n, listed in the order of the certified root boxes; for α ∈ K := ℚ[X]/(g) (power-basis coordinates), α^{(i)} := σ_i(α) where σ_i : K →+* ℂ sends the class of X to ξ^{(i)}; β := X − Yξ ∈ K for a solution (X, Y). The solution set is finite (DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.4/thue-equation-effective-bound, whose hypothesis 'at least three distinct complex zeros' follows from irreducibility and n ≥ 3); this stage proves equality of the solution set with an explicit finite set from a certificate (ED.2/thue-certified-solution-set). Reducible forms, forms of degree ≤ 2 and m = 0 are not Thue equations in this sense.
hypotheses: n ≥ 3 and irreducibility over ℚ; m ≠ 0
Solutions are all pairs of integers, with no coprimality condition and no sign normalisation
proofSteps: F(x, y) = y^n g(x/y) for y ≠ 0 and F(x, 0) = f_0 x^n, by the definition of Polynomial.homogenize.
F(tx, ty) = t^n F(x, y), since F is homogeneous of degree n (Polynomial.homogenize is a homogeneous polynomial of degree n).
acceptance: thueSolutions (X³ − 2) 1 ⊇ {(1, 0), (−1, −1)}; the certified equality is the acceptance of ED.2/thue-certified-solution-set.

nodes.title: Factor coverings: units and representatives for X − ξY
nodes.statement: Let (g, m) be a Thue equation with s ≥ 1 real roots, K := ℚ[X]/(g), ξ the class of X, r := s + t − 1. A factor covering for (g, m) consists of units ε_1, …, ε_r of the ring of integers 𝓞_K and a finite list M ⊆ K^× (all given in power-basis coordinates) such that: (U) every unit of 𝓞_K is of the form ±ε_1^{a_1}⋯ε_r^{a_r} with a ∈ ℤ^r (the torsion of K is {±1} because K has a real embedding); (M) for every (X, Y) ∈ thueSolutions g m there are μ ∈ M and a unit η of 𝓞_K with f_0·(X − Yξ) = f_0·μ·η. Consequently every solution satisfies X − Yξ = ±μ·ε_1^{a_1}⋯ε_r^{a_r} for some μ ∈ M and a ∈ ℤ^r, which is the representation β = μ ε_1^{a_1}⋯ε_r^{a_r} of Tzanakis–de Weger (with ± absorbed into M). The two conditions are input hypotheses of the Thue certificate. (U) is discharged by ComputationalNumberTheory:CN.2/units-complete-of-regulator-bound (a family of rank(K) units with linearly independent logarithmic images and regOfFamily < 2·regulator generates the units with the torsion). (M) holds for M := {δ/f_0 : δ ∈ D_u(f_0^{n−1}m), |N_{K/ℚ}(δ)| = |f_0^{n−1}m|}, with D_u the bounded divisor representatives of DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.4/bounded-divisor-representatives for any maximal-rank family u: γ := f_0(X − Yξ) is an algebraic integer (f_0ξ is integral, DT.4/thue-equation-monic-reduction) of norm f_0^{n−1}m, it divides its norm in 𝓞_K, and DT.4/divisors-up-to-units writes it as a unit times an element δ of D_u(f_0^{n−1}m), with |N(δ)| = |N(γ)| because units have norm ±1. A list M obtained from prime-ideal factorisations (ComputationalNumberTheory:CN.2/prime-ideal-factor-certificate and principal generators) satisfies (M) by the same argument. In the Lean Finset K representation, every μ∈M must be nonzero, equivalent to representatives in Kˣ. ofDivisorRepresentatives requires irreducibility over Q, degree≥3, m≠0, g(ξ)=0 and [K:Q]=deg g, a complete generating unit family, and nonzero representatives D⊂O_K for all nonzero divisors of f₀^(n−1)m up to association. Prove integrality of f₀(x−yξ), its norm f₀^(n−1)m and hence divisibility of that constant; set M={δ/f₀ | δ∈D}. No covering-of-solutions hypothesis is passed to this factory. The Lean record pins r = NumberField.Units.rank K. Full generation by exactly rank(K) units implies maximal rank of their logarithmic images; redundant generators are excluded, since they would allow unbounded exponent vectors for a fixed element and invalidate ED.2/thue-exponent-bound.
hypotheses: s ≥ 1 (when s = 0 no covering is needed: every solution has |Y| ≤ Y_0, ED.2/thue-root-approximation)
Condition (U) is a statement about the full unit group; displayed units of finite index are not enough
r = NumberField.Units.rank K; full generation alone with an arbitrary number of generators is insufficient for exponent bounds.
proofSteps: With n=deg g and K=Q(ξ), z=f₀(x−yξ) is integral, Norm(z)=f₀^(n−1)m≠0, and z divides its integer norm. Apply D-completeness, divide by nonzero f₀ and use the unit family. This is the factory, independent of the desired covers field.
An algebraic integer γ ≠ 0 of K divides N(γ) in 𝓞_K (the cofactor is the product of the other conjugates, an algebraic integer lying in K).

Apply DT.4/divisors-up-to-units to γ | f_0^{n−1}m and keep the representatives δ with |N(δ)| = |f_0^{n−1}m| (a unit has norm ±1, so the sign of N(δ) is not determined); combine with (U) to write the unit as ±∏ε_i^{a_i}.

The subgroup generated by ε has index at most two by (U). With r = rank K, NumberField.Units.isMaxRank_iff_closure_finiteIndex gives independent logarithmic images and hence invertible logarithmic coordinate minors.
acceptance: For g = X³ − 2 and m = 1 the covering ({∛2 − 1}, {1}) satisfies (U) and (M).

nodes.title: Certified constants of the Tzanakis–de Weger method
nodes.statement: Let (g, m) be a Thue equation (ED.2/thue-equation) with roots ξ^{(i)} isolated in rational boxes B_1, …, B_n by ComputationalNumberTheory:CN.4/certified-polynomial-root-isolation (real roots in degenerate-imaginary boxes, the boxes of a conjugate pair mirror images). Tzanakis–de Weger's constants are C_1 := 2^{n−1}|m|/min_{i≤s}|g′(ξ^{(i)})|, C_2 := ½·min_{i<j}|ξ^{(i)} − ξ^{(j)}|, C_3 := max over pairwise distinct i_1, i_2, i_3 of |ξ^{(i_1)} − ξ^{(i_2)}|/|ξ^{(i_1)} − ξ^{(i_3)}|, Y_0 := ⌈(2^{n−1}|m|/(min_{i≤t}|g′(ξ^{(s+i)})|·min_{i≤t}|Im ξ^{(s+i)}|))^{1/n}⌉ if t ≥ 1 and Y_0 := 1 if t = 0, Y_1 := max(Y_0, ⌈(4C_1)^{1/(n−2)}⌉), Y_1* := max(Y_1, ⌈(2C_1C_3/C_2)^{1/n}⌉); given a factor covering (ε, M) (ED.2/thue-factor-covering): μ_− := min_{i, μ∈M}|μ^{(i)}|, μ_+ := max_{i, μ∈M}|μ^{(i)}|, C_4 := (½ + max_{i<j}|ξ^{(i)} − ξ^{(j)}|)/μ_−, for an r-subset I = {h_1, …, h_r} of {1, …, n} the matrix U_I with entry log|ε_i^{(h_l)}| in row l and column i (rows indexed by the embeddings, columns by the units; see sourceIssues EffectiveDiophantineMethods/E5), N[U_I^{−1}] the maximal absolute row sum of U_I^{−1}, C_5 := min((n − 1)·min_I N[U_I^{−1}], max_{i_0≤s} N[U_{I(i_0)}^{−1}]) over the invertible U_I and a choice of invertible I(i_0) ∌ i_0, C_6 := 1.39·C_1C_3C_4^n/C_2 and Y_2′ := max(Y_1*, 2|m|^{1/n}, μ_+/C_2). A ThueConstants certificate consists of rationals ĉ_1 ≥ C_1, 0 < ĉ_2 ≤ C_2, ĉ_3 ≥ C_3, 0 < μ̂_− ≤ μ_−, μ̂_+ ≥ μ_+, ĉ_4 ≥ C_4, ĉ_5 ≥ C_5, ĉ_6 ≥ 1.39·ĉ_1ĉ_3ĉ_4^n/ĉ_2 and integers Ŷ_0 ≥ Y_0, Ŷ_1 ≥ max(Ŷ_0, (4ĉ_1)^{1/(n−2)}), Ŷ_1* ≥ max(Ŷ_1, (2ĉ_1ĉ_3/ĉ_2)^{1/n}), Ŷ_2′ ≥ max(Ŷ_1*, 2|m|^{1/n}, μ̂_+/ĉ_2), each inequality verified exactly from the boxes: |g′|, |ξ^{(i)} − ξ^{(j)}|, |Im ξ| and |μ^{(i)}| by rational interval evaluation over the boxes (ComputationalNumberTheory:CN.4/rational-interval-product, ED.0/archimedean-embedding-certificate), n-th roots by comparing integer powers (Ŷ^n ≥ q), logarithms by ED.2/logarithm-enclosure, and N[U_I^{−1}] by an approximate inverse: for a rational matrix V with ‖1 − V·U‖_∞ ≤ ρ < 1 for every U in the interval matrix enclosing U_I, U_I is invertible and N[U_I^{−1}] ≤ ‖V‖_∞/(1 − ρ). Every constant is thereby a certified rational bound in the direction in which the lemmas use it; no unrounded real number is stored. The complete constructor and its s=0/s>0 alternatives are specified under the same names in suggestedOmissions. ThueBoundParameters is only the supporting partial semantic record used by the scalar lemmas; it does not certify c4,c5 or μ± without the explicit covering inequalities. A raw producer receives all unit, representative, root and logarithm enclosures, not merely g,m and a precision.
hypotheses: The boxes isolate the n distinct roots of g (irreducible, hence separable); the covering data are exact elements of K

Only the direction of each inequality matters: the lemmas of ED.2/thue-root-approximation, thue-linear-form and thue-exponent-bound remain true with C_1, C_3, C_4, C_5, C_6, Y_• replaced by larger and C_2, μ_− by smaller positive values
The real-root branch uses nonempty invertible unit matrices; the s=0 branch contains only Y0 and never forms C1 or C5.
proofSteps: Interval evaluation: g′(ξ^{(i)}) and the differences of roots lie in the rational boxes obtained by evaluating g′ and z − w on the boxes; lower bounds of moduli come from the box nearest to 0, upper bounds from the farthest corner.

Approximate inverse: in the normed ring of r×r real matrices with the ∞-operator norm (Matrix.linftyOpNormedRing, Matrix.linfty_opNorm_def: the norm is the maximal absolute row sum), ‖1 − VU‖ ≤ ρ < 1 makes VU = 1 − (1 − VU) a unit with inverse Σ(1 − VU)^k (Units.oneSub) of norm ≤ (1 − ρ)^{−1} (tsum_geometric_le_of_norm_lt_one), so U^{−1} = (VU)^{−1}V has norm ≤ ‖V‖/(1 − ρ); ‖1 − VU‖ is bounded over the interval matrix by interval arithmetic.
Each listed inequality between rationals is decided exactly; the precision of the boxes and of the logarithm enclosures is raised until all checks pass or the certificate is rejected.
acceptance: For g = X³ − 2, m = 1 the certificate has Ŷ_0 = 1 and Ŷ_1 = 4 (C_1 ≈ 0.840, ⌈4C_1⌉ = 4).
