suggestedOmissions.reason: The complete covering-indexed constant and interval-inverse certificate carrier is not built; the former g,m,P producer was not its signature.
suggestedOmissions.requiredSignature: The finite representation is over a certified number-field presentation Q[T]/(G), with rational power-basis coordinates, integral-basis conversion matrices, an irreducibility certificate, labelled real/complex embeddings, and the actual algebraic root θ. Ideal, unit, root-isolation and logarithm data are outputs of the CN.0/CN.2/CN.4 suppliers already named by this packet. No new generic number-field algorithm is owned here. A raw transcript has no proof fields. All loops have explicit finite index sets or integer ranges; checking uses exact integer/rational arithmetic and modular exponentiation. Supplier soundness theorems identify a checked finite record with the actual field, ideals, roots, units and logarithms. This identification belongs to the soundness theorem and is not a Boolean comparison on R or an assumption that the claimed answer is complete. The covering transcript records the complete prime-ideal factorizations of the fixed norm ideal and of every p_i, finite bounded valuation vectors given by the full removing lemma, all ideal-class remainders, principal generators (or certified nonprincipality), torsion representatives and exactly Units.rank K independent units. It checks ideal products, norms, residue degrees, class-order relations, basis conversions and a complete-unit regulator/index certificate. The finite case index set is exactly the product of these bounded choices, modulo explicitly checked duplicates; an omitted combination rejects. Its soundness derives conditions (U),(M)/(C). A finite list with a proof field saying it covers all solutions is only the separate semantic covering, not this finite input. ThueConstants is indexed by the actual ThueEquation E, K, ξ and its complete factor covering, with an explicit s=0/s>0 sum. ofBoxes receives the certified complete root boxes, covering M, exactly rank(K) fundamental units and complete unit certificate, compatible embedding evaluations of ξ, every μ and ε_i, log|ε_i| intervals, precision bounds, and the selected index sets I. It checks disjoint/simple roots, conjugate-pair labels, nonzero representative modulus lower bounds, and all root-distance/derivative bounds. For each chosen U_I it checks a rational approximate inverse V and a uniform interval bound ||1−VU||∞≤ρ<1, with rows=embeddings and columns=units. It returns all correctly oriented c1,…,c6,μ−,μ+,Y0,Y1,Y1*,Y2 inequalities, including c4≥C4(cov), c5≥C5(cov),0<μ−≤min|σμ|,max|σμ|≤μ+, and every coupled threshold. The s=0 branch stores only the root certificate and Y0 and proves all solutions have |y|≤Y0; it never forms C1,C5 or a covering. mono takes new upper/lower bounds in the stated directions, positivity and the complete finite checks of all coupled inequalities, returning a certificate for the same E,K,ξ,cov. The raw computational input, the finite check, and the semantic inequalities deduced from a successful check must be separate. The partial ThueBoundParameters record and weakenC1Bound are supporting semantic data only.

nodes.title: Lemma 1.1: solutions with large |Y| approximate a real root
nodes.statement: Let (g, m) be a Thue equation with certified constants ĉ_1 ≥ C_1, 0 < ĉ_2 ≤ C_2, Ŷ_0 ≥ Y_0, Ŷ_1 ≥ max(Ŷ_0, (4ĉ_1)^{1/(n−2)}) (ED.2/thue-analytic-constants), and let (X, Y) ∈ thueSolutions g m, β^{(i)} := X − Yξ^{(i)}. (i) If |Y| > Ŷ_0 then s ≥ 1 and there is i_0 ∈ {1, …, s} (a real root) with |β^{(i_0)}| ≤ ĉ_1·|Y|^{−(n−1)} and |β^{(i)}| ≥ ĉ_2·|Y| for all i ≠ i_0. In particular, if s = 0 then every solution has |Y| ≤ Ŷ_0. (ii) If |Y| > Ŷ_1 then |X/Y − ξ^{(i_0)}| ≤ ĉ_1|Y|^{−n} ≤ ¼·|Y|^{−2} < 1/(2·den(X/Y)²), hence X/Y = Real.convergent ξ^{(i_0)} k for some k (Legendre's theorem, Mathlib's Real.exists_rat_eq_convergent).
hypotheses: (X, Y) is a solution; no coprimality is assumed (den(X/Y) ≤ |Y| is all that is used)
The constants are any certified bounds in the directions stated
proofSteps: If ξ^{(i_0)} were non-real then |X/Y − ξ^{(i_0)}| ≥ |Im ξ^{(i_0)}| (X/Y is real) contradicts |X/Y − ξ^{(i_0)}| ≤ (Y_0/|Y|)^n·min|Im ξ| for |Y| > Y_0 (Tzanakis–de Weger, p. 104).

(ii): ĉ_1|Y|^{−n} ≤ ¼Ŷ_1^{n−2}|Y|^{−n} < ¼|Y|^{−2} ≤ ¼den(X/Y)^{−2}; Real.exists_rat_eq_convergent applies to the rational q = X/Y. (Tzanakis–de Weger cite Hardy–Wright Theorem 184; Mathlib's version is stated for q in lowest terms, which is why den(X/Y) ≤ |Y| is used.)
acceptance: For g = X³ − 2, m = 1 and the solution (−1, −1): |Y| = 1 ≤ Ŷ_1, so the lemma makes no claim; for every solution with |Y| > Ŷ_1, X/Y is a convergent of ∛2 = [1; 3, 1, 5, 1, 1, 4, …].
For a totally complex g (s = 0) the lemma bounds every solution by |Y| ≤ Ŷ_0, which is the whole proof of finiteness in that case.

nodes.title: Lemma 1.2: the unit equation and a small nonzero linear form in logarithms
nodes.statement: Let (g, m) be a Thue equation with s ≥ 1, a factor covering (ε, M) (ED.2/thue-factor-covering) and certified constants (ED.2/thue-analytic-constants). Let (X, Y) be a solution with |Y| > Ŷ_1*, i_0 the real index of ED.2/thue-root-approximation, and write X − Yξ = ±μ∏_{i≤r}ε_i^{a_i} with μ ∈ M, a ∈ ℤ^r. Choose j, k with i_0, j, k pairwise distinct and either j, k ≤ s (real case) or ξ^{(k)} = conj ξ^{(j)} (complex case); such j, k exist because n ≥ 3. Put δ_μ := ((ξ^{(i_0)} − ξ^{(j)})/(ξ^{(i_0)} − ξ^{(k)}))·(μ^{(k)}/μ^{(j)}). Siegel's identity (DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.4/siegel-identity) gives the unit equation δ_μ∏_i(ε_i^{(k)}/ε_i^{(j)})^{a_i} − 1 = −((ξ^{(k)} − ξ^{(j)})/(ξ^{(k)} − ξ^{(i_0)}))·β^{(i_0)}/β^{(j)} (TdW (1.2)). Define, in the real case, Λ := Real.log|δ_μ| + Σ_i a_i·Real.log|ε_i^{(k)}/ε_i^{(j)}| (TdW (1.3)), and in the complex case Λ := Complex.arg δ_μ + Σ_i a_i·Complex.arg(ε_i^{(k)}/ε_i^{(j)}) + 2πa_0 for the unique a_0 ∈ ℤ making Λ = −i·Complex.log(δ_μ∏(ε_i^{(k)}/ε_i^{(j)})^{a_i}) (TdW (1.4)). Then: (a) Λ ≠ 0; (b) |Λ| < 1.39·ĉ_1ĉ_3/ĉ_2·|Y|^{−n}; (c) in the complex case |a_0| ≤ 1 + rA/2 with A := max_i |a_i|; (d) as a linear form in logarithms, Λ (real case) resp. iΛ (complex case) is Σ_{l} b_lλ_l with integer coefficients b = (1, a_1, …, a_r) resp. (1, a_1, …, a_r, 2a_0), and nonzero logarithms λ_l of the algebraic numbers |δ_μ|, |ε_i^{(k)}/ε_i^{(j)}| (real case) resp. δ_μ, ε_i^{(k)}/ε_i^{(j)}, −1 with λ = Complex.log (complex case), terms with λ_l = 0 being deleted; all these numbers lie in the number field ℚ(ξ^{(i_0)}, ξ^{(j)}, ξ^{(k)}) ⊆ ℂ of degree at most n(n − 1)(n − 2), and B* := max|b_l| ≤ (r + 2)·max(1, A).
hypotheses: |Y| > Ŷ_1* (so |Y| > Ŷ_1 ≥ Ŷ_0 and the right side of (1.2) has modulus < ½)
The sign ± of the covering cancels in the quotients β^{(k)}/β^{(j)}
Nonvanishing (a) is structural (β^{(i_0)} ≠ 0 because m ≠ 0), never read off a numerical enclosure
proofSteps: Siegel's identity with (X, Y) eliminated from β^{(i)} = X − Yξ^{(i)}, i ∈ {i_0, j, k}, gives (1.2); substitute β = ±μ∏ε^a.

By ED.2/thue-root-approximation and the definition of C_3, the right side of (1.2) has modulus ≤ ĉ_1ĉ_3/(ĉ_2|Y|^n) < ½ for |Y| > Ŷ_1*. Real case: the left side plus one is positive, so it equals e^Λ − 1, and |e^Λ − 1| < ½ implies |Λ| ≤ 2 log 2·|e^Λ − 1| ≤ 1.39|e^Λ − 1|. Complex case: the left side plus one has modulus 1 and equals e^{iΛ}; |e^{iΛ} − 1| = 2|sin(Λ/2)| < ½ and |Λ| ≤ π give |Λ/2| < arcsin(1/4), and x/sin x is increasing on (0, π/2], so |Λ| ≤ 4·arcsin(1/4)·|e^{iΛ} − 1| ≤ 1.02|e^{iΛ} − 1| (4·arcsin(1/4) ≈ 1.0107; TdW p. 106 write the factor (1/4)/sin(1/4) ≈ 1.0105, which needs |Λ/2| ≤ 1/4).
(a): β^{(i_0)} ≠ 0 since F(X, Y) = m ≠ 0, and ξ^{(k)} ≠ ξ^{(j)}; so the right side of (1.2) is nonzero and Λ ≠ 0 (TdW, proof of Lemma 2.4).
(c): |Λ| ≤ π, |Complex.arg| ≤ π, so 2π|a_0| ≤ π + π + rAπ.

(d): in the real case |α| = ±α for real α, Real.log|α| is the principal logarithm of the positive algebraic number |α|; in the complex case Complex.log(−1) = πi, so 2πa_0 = −i·2a_0·Complex.log(−1). The field degree bound is the degree of the compositum of three conjugate fields of degree n.
acceptance: For g = X³ − 2 (s = 1, t = 1, r = 1): i_0 = 1 is forced and (j, k) = (2, 3) is the complex case; Λ = Arg δ_μ + a_1 Arg(ε^{(3)}/ε^{(2)}) + 2πa_0 with ε = ∛2 − 1, and |a_0| ≤ 1 + |a_1|/2.

nodes.title: Lemmas 2.1–2.2: the exponents are logarithmic in |Y| and Λ decays exponentially
nodes.statement: In the setting of ED.2/thue-linear-form, let A := max_{i≤r}|a_i| and let ĉ_4, ĉ_5, ĉ_6, Ŷ_2′ be certified constants (ED.2/thue-analytic-constants). (Lemma 2.1) If |Y| > max(Ŷ_1, 2|m|^{1/n}, μ̂_+/ĉ_2) then ĉ_4|Y| > 1 and A < ĉ_5·Real.log(ĉ_4|Y|). (Lemma 2.2) If |Y| > Ŷ_2′ then |Λ| < ĉ_6·exp(−(n/ĉ_5)·A).
hypotheses: U_I is the matrix with entry log|ε_i^{(h_l)}| in row l (embedding h_l) and column i (unit ε_i), so that (log|β^{(h_l)}/μ^{(h_l)}|)_l = U_I·(a_i)_i; N[·] is the maximal absolute row sum
The index sets I used in ĉ_5 index invertible matrices; for the bound with the maximum, I(i_0) avoids the real index i_0 of the solution
proofSteps: Since ∏_h|β^{(h)}/μ^{(h)}| = 1 (equal norms up to sign), each |log|β^{(i)}/μ^{(i)}|| < (n − 1)·log(C_4|Y|) (TdW (2.3)); a = U_I^{−1}(log|β^{(h_l)}/μ^{(h_l)}|)_l gives A ≤ N[U_I^{−1}]·max_l|log|β^{(h_l)}/μ^{(h_l)}||, hence A < (n − 1)N[U_I^{−1}]log(C_4|Y|) for every I.

If i_0 ∉ I then |β^{(h)}/μ^{(h)}| > C_2|Y|/μ_+ > 1 for h ∈ I (ED.2/thue-root-approximation (i)), so 0 < log|β^{(h)}/μ^{(h)}| < log(C_4|Y|) and A < N[U_I^{−1}]log(C_4|Y|); together A < C_5 log(C_4|Y|) ≤ ĉ_5 log(ĉ_4|Y|).
Lemma 2.2: |Y| > exp(A/ĉ_5)/ĉ_4 by Lemma 2.1, and ED.2/thue-linear-form (b) gives |Λ| < 1.39ĉ_1ĉ_3/ĉ_2·|Y|^{−n} < ĉ_6 exp(−nA/ĉ_5).
acceptance: For g = X³ − 2 (r = 1, units ε = ∛2 − 1): U_I is the 1×1 matrix (log|ε^{(h)}|) for one embedding h; with h the real embedding, |log(∛2 − 1)| ≈ 1.347 and N[U_I^{−1}] ≈ 0.742, so A < 2·0.742·log(C_4|Y|) for every solution with |Y| > max(Ŷ_1, 2, μ_+/C_2).

nodes.title: Lemmas 2.3–2.4 with Matveev's bound: the initial exponent bound
nodes.statement: In the setting of ED.2/thue-linear-form and ED.2/thue-exponent-bound, fix the real index i_0 ≤ s, the representative μ ∈ M and the indices j, k, and let c be the value of a MatveevConstantCertificate (ED.2/certified-linear-form-constant) for the family of nonzero logarithms of ED.2/thue-linear-form (d) (at most r + 1 logarithms in the real case, at most r + 2 in the complex case) with degree bound D := n(n − 1)(n − 2), admissible through height bounds h(δ_μ) ≤ 4h(ξ) + 2 log 2 + 2h(μ), h(ε_i^{(k)}/ε_i^{(j)}) ≤ 2h(ε_i), h(−1) = 0 (heights of elements of K from EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/height-enclosure) and the logarithm enclosures of ED.2/logarithm-enclosure. Put C_7 := c, Ĉ_8 ≥ 1 + Real.log(r + 2) (rational), a := (ĉ_5/n)(ℓ⁺(ĉ_6) + C_7Ĉ_8), b := ĉ_5C_7/n, and let K_3 be a rational with K_3 ≥ max(1, 2a + 2b(ℓ⁺(2b) − 1)), ℓ⁺ denoting upper ends of CN.4 logarithm enclosures. Then every solution (X, Y) with |Y| > Ŷ_2′, real index i_0 and representative μ satisfies A ≤ K_3 (and |a_0| ≤ 1 + rK_3/2 in the complex case).
hypotheses: Λ ≠ 0 by ED.2/thue-linear-form (a); this is the nonvanishing hypothesis of the imported lower bound
The Matveev certificate is admissible for the actual family; heights of conjugate quotients are bounded through the height of the field elements, never by numerical evaluation alone
proofSteps: ED.2/certified-linear-form-lower-bound with B* ≤ (r + 2)max(1, A): for A ≥ 1, |Λ| > exp(−C_7(1 + Real.log(r + 2) + Real.log A)) ≥ exp(−C_7(Ĉ_8 + log A)) (TdW Lemma 2.3 with C_8′ = Ĉ_8).
Combined with ED.2/thue-exponent-bound (Lemma 2.2): (n/ĉ_5)A < log ĉ_6 + C_7Ĉ_8 + C_7 log A, i.e. A < a + b log A.

DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.4/log-linear-inequality-bound gives A ≤ 2a + 2b(log(2b) − 1) ≤ K_3 (TdW instead cite Pethő–de Weger, Lemma 2.3, with C_9 = (2C_5/n)(log C_6 + C_7C_8′ + C_7 log(C_5C_7/n))); for A < 1 the bound K_3 ≥ 1 holds trivially.

Heights: Height.logHeight₁_sub_le, Height.logHeight₁_mul_le and Height.logHeight₁_inv, divided by the field degree (NumberField.totalWeight_eq_finrank: totalWeight K = [K : ℚ]), give h(x − y) ≤ log 2 + h(x) + h(y), h(xy) ≤ h(x) + h(y), h(x^{−1}) = h(x); conjugates have the same absolute height (DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.0/abs-mul-height-eq-of-minpoly-eq).

Degree bound: for the three distinct conjugate roots ξ_i, ξ_j, ξ_k of the separable degree-n polynomial, successively adjoin ξ_i, then a root of g/(X−ξ_i), then a root of g/((X−ξ_i)(X−ξ_j)). The extension degrees are at most n, n−1, n−2, respectively. Thus the compositum containing the logarithm arguments has degree ≤ n(n−1)(n−2); three independent degree-n adjunction bounds would give only n³.
acceptance: For a quartic totally real field as in TdW §III (r = 3), with Matveev's constant for r + 1 = 4 logarithms and D ≤ 24, K_3 is of the order 10^{20}–10^{30}; TdW's Waldschmidt-based bound was of size 10^{40} (p. 111).

nodes.title: Reduction of the initial bound and the bound for |Y|
nodes.statement: Let (g, m) be a Thue equation with s ≥ 1, factor covering and certified constants. For each real index i_0 ≤ s and μ ∈ M, with (j, k) fixed for i_0, let 𝒮_{i_0,μ} ⊆ ℤ^q (q = r in the real case, q = r + 1 with the extra coordinate a_0 in the complex case) be the set of exponent vectors of solutions with |Y| > Ŷ_2′, real index i_0 and representative μ, with unit weights and H(a) := max_i|a_i| over all q coordinates. Since A ≥ 1 (if a_1 = ⋯ = a_r = 0 then |β^{(h)}| = |μ^{(h)}| ≤ μ̂_+ < ĉ_2|Y| ≤ |β^{(h)}| for h ≠ i_0, because |Y| > Ŷ_2′ ≥ μ̂_+/ĉ_2) and |a_0| ≤ 1 + rA/2 ≤ (r + 2)A/2, every a ∈ 𝒮_{i_0,μ} satisfies H(a) ≤ (r + 2)K_3/2 and |Λ| < ĉ_6·exp(−δ·H(a)) with δ := n/ĉ_5 (real case) resp. δ := 2n/((r + 2)ĉ_5) (complex case). Let R_{i_0,μ} be an exponent reduction chain (ED.2/exponent-reduction-chain) for 𝒮_{i_0,μ} starting at X_0 := K_3 resp. (r + 2)K_3/2 (ED.2/thue-initial-bound), whose real steps are ED.1 reductions for this inequality with Λ = δ′ + Σ a_iθ_i (δ′ = log|δ_μ|, θ_i = log|ε_i^{(k)}/ε_i^{(j)}| in the real case; δ′ = Arg δ_μ, θ_i = Arg(ε_i^{(k)}/ε_i^{(j)}), θ_{r+1} = 2π in the complex case), the lattice data being integers φ_i, ψ with |φ_i − c_0θ_i| ≤ 1 and |ψ − c_0δ′| ≤ 1 for the scaling constant c_0 of the step (the C of EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/linear-form-lattice; rounding the midpoint of an enclosure of width at most 1/c_0, from ED.2/logarithm-enclosure, meets this precision budget). Let A_red be the maximum of the final bounds (a bound for H, hence for A) and E the union of the exceptional sets. For every index l let E_l := ∏_i |ε_i^{(l)}|^{v_{il}} with v_{il} = ±1 chosen so that |ε_i^{(l)}|^{v_{il}} ≥ 1, with rational upper bounds Ê_l. Then every solution (X, Y) satisfies |Y| ≤ C := max(Ŷ_2′, Ŷ_red) with an integer Ŷ_red ≥ μ̂_+(Ê_{l_1}^{A_red} + Ê_{l_2}^{A_red})/|ξ^{(l_1)} − ξ^{(l_2)}| for any fixed l_1 ≠ l_2, unless its exponent vector lies in E; for a ∈ E the element ±μ∏ε_i^{a_i} is computed exactly in power-basis coordinates and yields the candidate (X, Y) when it equals X − Yξ with X, Y ∈ ℤ.
hypotheses: The real steps of the chains use ED.1/inhomogeneous-reduction (δ′ ≠ 0) or ED.1/homogeneous-reduction (δ′ = 0 exactly, decided by CN.0/algebraic-equality-check on |δ_μ| = 1 resp. δ_μ = 1)
The theorem is a statement about all solutions; the chain certificates are finite data checked by exact arithmetic
proofSteps: Every solution with |Y| > Ŷ_2′ has, for its i_0 and μ, an exponent vector in 𝒮_{i_0,μ} with H ≤ K_3 (real case) resp. H ≤ (r + 2)K_3/2 (complex case) (ED.2/thue-initial-bound with ED.2/thue-linear-form (c)) satisfying the inequality of ED.2/thue-exponent-bound; soundness of the chain gives A ≤ A_red or a ∈ E.

Pethő's argument (TdW p. 118): |β^{(l)}| = |μ^{(l)}|∏|ε_i^{(l)}|^{a_i} ≤ μ_+E_l^A, and Y = (β^{(l_1)} − β^{(l_2)})/(ξ^{(l_2)} − ξ^{(l_1)}), so |Y| ≤ μ_+(E_{l_1}^A + E_{l_2}^A)/|ξ^{(l_1)} − ξ^{(l_2)}|; with A ≤ A_red this is at most Ŷ_red.
Hence a solution not coming from E has |Y| ≤ Ŷ_2′ or |Y| ≤ Ŷ_red.
acceptance: In TdW §III.2 (pp. 124–126) the initial bound A < 3.26·10^{40} is reduced to A ≤ 72 by one step (c_0 = 10^{140}) and to A ≤ 10 by a second step (c_0 = 10^{12}), after which the remaining exponent vectors are enumerated; the theorem turns such a bound into an explicit C for the continued-fraction search.

nodes.title: The continued-fraction search for solutions of moderate size
nodes.statement: Let (g, m) be a Thue equation with certified Ŷ_1 (ED.2/thue-analytic-constants) and let C ≥ Ŷ_1 be an integer. For each real root ξ^{(i)} (i ≤ s) let ξ̃_i ∈ ℚ with |ξ̃_i − ξ^{(i)}| < 1/(6C²) (certified by a refined root box of width < 1/(6C²)). Then every solution (X, Y) with Ŷ_1 < |Y| ≤ C is of the form (X, Y) = (Z·p, Z·q) where p/q = Real.convergent ξ̃_i k for some i ≤ s and k ∈ ℕ, written in lowest terms with q ≥ 1 and q ≤ C, and Z ∈ ℤ ∖ {0} with Z^n ∣ m (so |Z| ≤ |m|^{1/n}). Since ξ̃_i is rational, Real.convergent ξ̃_i k = ξ̃_i for all k beyond the length of its finite continued fraction (GenContFract.terminates_iff_rat for (ξ̃_i : ℝ), GenContFract.convs_stable_of_terminated and Real.convs_eq_convergent), so the candidate set {(Zp, Zq)} is finite and is tested exactly against F(X, Y) = m.
hypotheses: s ≥ 1 (for s = 0 there are no solutions with |Y| > Ŷ_0, and the search is empty)

The test of TdW (3.8) on the partial quotients is not used: it is stated for the partial quotients of ξ^{(i_0)}, while the search computes those of ξ̃_i (sourceIssues EffectiveDiophantineMethods/E7); testing every convergent with q ≤ C is exhaustive and cheap
proofSteps: By ED.2/thue-root-approximation, |X/Y − ξ^{(i_0)}| ≤ ĉ_1|Y|^{−n} ≤ ¼|Y|^{−2} for |Y| > Ŷ_1, with i_0 ≤ s.

Then |ξ̃_{i_0} − X/Y| < 1/(6C²) + 1/(4Y²) ≤ (1/6 + 1/4)/den(X/Y)² < 1/(2 den(X/Y)²), since den(X/Y) ≤ |Y| ≤ C; Mathlib's Real.exists_rat_eq_convergent (Legendre) gives X/Y = Real.convergent ξ̃_{i_0} k for some k.
Write X/Y = p/q in lowest terms, q ≥ 1; then (X, Y) = (Zp, Zq) with Z := Y/q ∈ ℤ ∖ {0}, and m = F(Zp, Zq) = Z^nF(p, q), so Z^n ∣ m; q ≤ |Y| ≤ C.

Finiteness: GenContFract.of (ξ̃_i : ℝ) terminates (GenContFract.terminates_iff_rat), its convergents are constant from the termination index on (GenContFract.convs_stable_of_terminated), and they are the Real.convergent ξ̃_i k (Real.convs_eq_convergent); so Real.convergent ξ̃_i takes finitely many values.
acceptance: For g = X³ − 2, m = 1, ξ̃ = 126/100 (|ξ̃ − ∛2| ≈ 0.0001 < 1/(6·12²) for C = 12): the convergents of 63/50 = [1; 3, 1, 5, 2] are 1, 4/3, 5/4, 29/23, 63/50; those with denominator ≤ 12 are 1, 4/3, 5/4, and with Z^3 ∣ 1 they give |Y| ≤ 4 = Ŷ_1, so there is no solution with Ŷ_1 < |Y| ≤ 12.

nodes.title: Exhaustive enumeration of the solutions with small |Y|
nodes.statement: For a Thue equation (g, m) and a natural number Y_1, thueSmallSolutions g m Y_1 is the finite set of (x, y) ∈ ℤ² with |y| ≤ Y_1 and F(x, y) = m, computed as follows: for each y with |y| ≤ Y_1, the polynomial P_y(X) := F(X, y) − m ∈ ℤ[X] has degree n and leading coefficient f_0 ≠ 0, so it is nonzero and every integer root x satisfies |x| < cauchyBound(P_y) = max_{i<n}|coeff_i(P_y)|/|f_0| + 1 (Polynomial.cauchyBound, Polynomial.IsRoot.norm_lt_cauchyBound over ℚ); the integers x in that range are tested exactly. Equivalently, thueSmallSolutions g m Y_1 = thueSolutions g m ∩ {|y| ≤ Y_1}, and the construction is the explicit finite enumeration that proves this equality.
hypotheses: n ≥ 1 and f_0 ≠ 0 make every P_y a nonzero polynomial of degree n, so the Cauchy bound applies for every y, including y = 0 (where P_0 = f_0X^n − m)
proofSteps: Membership: (x, y) is a solution with |y| ≤ Y_1 iff x is an integer root of P_y.
Completeness: by Polynomial.IsRoot.norm_lt_cauchyBound (applied to P_y mapped to ℚ), every root satisfies |x| < cauchyBound P_y; the enumerated range contains every integer root.
Exactness: each tested pair is accepted iff F(x, y) = m, an exact integer identity.

nodes.title: Thue solution certificates
nodes.statement: A ThueCertificate for a Thue equation (g, m) (ED.2/thue-equation) is the following finite data, each item with its exact check: (1) root boxes and a ThueConstants certificate (ED.2/thue-analytic-constants) with Ŷ_0, Ŷ_1; (2) if s = 0: nothing more; (3) if s ≥ 1: a factor covering (ε, M) (ED.2/thue-factor-covering, whose conditions (U), (M) are hypotheses of the soundness theorem, not checks); for every real index i_0 ≤ s and μ ∈ M a choice of (j, k), a MatveevConstantCertificate admissible for the logarithms of ED.2/thue-linear-form (d), a rational K_3 as in ED.2/thue-initial-bound and an exponent reduction chain from K_3 (real case) resp. (r + 2)K_3/2 (complex case) (ED.2/exponent-reduction-chain) with its exceptional sets; rational bounds Ê_l, an integer Ŷ_red and the integer C := max(Ŷ_2′, Ŷ_red) of ED.2/thue-reduced-bound; for every real root a rational ξ̃_i with |ξ̃_i − ξ^{(i)}| < 1/(6C²); (4) the claimed list L ⊆ ℤ², required to be the set of pairs that pass the exact test F(x, y) = m among: the small solutions thueSmallSolutions g m Ŷ_1 (ED.2/thue-small-solutions) (with Ŷ_0 in place of Ŷ_1 when s = 0), the candidates (Zp, Zq) of ED.2/thue-convergent-search for all real roots, convergents p/q of ξ̃_i with q ≤ C and Z^n ∣ m, and the candidates obtained from the exceptional exponent vectors. The predicate ThueCertificate.Valid is the conjunction of all checks; each check is a decidable statement about integers and rationals (polynomial evaluations, comparisons, exact arithmetic in K and in ZMod), with precision budgets fixed by the data: the root boxes have the widths needed for the constants and for |ξ̃_i − ξ^{(i)}| < 1/(6C²), and the lattice entries of every real reduction step are integers within the certified error of c_0·θ_i required by ED.1/linear-form-lattice (c_0 the scaling constant of that step, distinct from the search bound C). The four classes of Tzanakis–de Weger are: (I) |Y| ≤ Ŷ_1, enumerated; (II) Ŷ_1 < |Y| ≤ C, continued fractions; (III) C < |Y| with A ≤ K_3, excluded by the reduction chains; (IV) A > K_3, excluded by the imported Matveev bound. This is the target raw finite format specified in suggestedOmissions. SemanticThueCertificate is the separately named mathematical summary; its Valid field contains real inequalities and universal solution implications, and has no claimed computational Decidable instance. The raw checker derives those implications from the finite transcript and supplier soundness, including all nonsolution rows.
hypotheses: All data are finite; a certificate that fails a check proves nothing
The covering conditions (U), (M) are input hypotheses discharged by ComputationalNumberTheory:CN.2 or by DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.4/divisors-up-to-units (ED.2/thue-factor-covering)
proofSteps: Each check is one of: an inequality between rationals, an exact polynomial identity over ℤ or ℚ, a modular computation, or a finite enumeration; Valid is decidable.
The data structure records, per (i_0, μ), all inputs of the theorems ED.2/thue-initial-bound and ED.2/thue-reduced-bound.

Separate finite check from semantic interpretation: first evaluate the full bounded transcript; then use supplier correctness and the named bound/reduction lemmas to prove the semantic summary. No proof field asserting completeness is accepted as raw data.
acceptance: Every check of a ThueCertificate is decidable; validity of a concrete certificate is established by evaluation, and only then does ED.2/thue-certified-solution-set apply.

suggestedOmissions.reason: The actual raw covering/bound/reduction/search transcript type and its finite checker are not built; the former signatures expressed semantic validity.
suggestedOmissions.requiredSignature: The finite representation is over a certified number-field presentation Q[T]/(G), with rational power-basis coordinates, integral-basis conversion matrices, an irreducibility certificate, labelled real/complex embeddings, and the actual algebraic root θ. Ideal, unit, root-isolation and logarithm data are outputs of the CN.0/CN.2/CN.4 suppliers already named by this packet. No new generic number-field algorithm is owned here. A raw transcript has no proof fields. All loops have explicit finite index sets or integer ranges; checking uses exact integer/rational arithmetic and modular exponentiation. Supplier soundness theorems identify a checked finite record with the actual field, ideals, roots, units and logarithms. This identification belongs to the soundness theorem and is not a Boolean comparison on R or an assumption that the claimed answer is complete. The covering transcript records the complete prime-ideal factorizations of the fixed norm ideal and of every p_i, finite bounded valuation vectors given by the full removing lemma, all ideal-class remainders, principal generators (or certified nonprincipality), torsion representatives and exactly Units.rank K independent units. It checks ideal products, norms, residue degrees, class-order relations, basis conversions and a complete-unit regulator/index certificate. The finite case index set is exactly the product of these bounded choices, modulo explicitly checked duplicates; an omitted combination rejects. Its soundness derives conditions (U),(M)/(C). A finite list with a proof field saying it covers all solutions is only the separate semantic covering, not this finite input. An initial-bound transcript records every logarithm/height enclosure, degree and nonvanishing input, the chosen Matveev/Yu source formula and all rounded rational constants; it verifies the finitely many rational inequalities of the DT.3/DT.4 bound derivation. A reduction transcript records successive nonnegative componentwise boxes, the exact real or p-adic form and its coefficient/residue identities, the raw ED.1 exclusion or complete enumeration data, and the exceptional exponent vectors. Each step is tagged with the applicable ED.1/ED.2 lemma and checks its complete finite numerical hypotheses. The theorem that all genuine solutions remain in the new box or exception set is derived from those checked records and the identified logarithms; it is never a proof field universally quantifying over the unknown solution set. ThueCertificate(E, certified K, ξ) is a tagged finite record. The no-real-root branch has a complete root isolation showing s=0, the certified Y0 threshold, a finite Cauchy-bounded search for each integer |y|≤Y0, and the exact accepted list. It forms no unit matrix or minimum over an empty real-root set. The real-root branch has the complete covering, ThueConstants output, all (i0,μ) cases, explicit conjugate choices, Matveev constants, initial and reduction transcripts, Pethő bounds, and a search integer C≥Y2′. The root approximants are rationals enclosed within1/(6C²) of every real root. The transcript contains a finite Euclidean-algorithm trace for each rational approximant, ending at its exact finite continued fraction, and all signed nonzero divisors Z with Z^n|m. It checks every convergent with denominator≤C, every small-search pair and every exceptional exponent vector: exact power-basis arithmetic determines whether ±μ∏ε^a has the form x−yξ with integral x,y, and polynomial evaluation determines acceptance. All finite candidates, including nonsolutions, have an evaluated outcome; no unbounded convergent index or unbounded x,y search occurs. The listed Finset is exactly the union of accepted outputs. ThueCertificate.Valid c means c.check=true. Its solutions/searchBound projections are raw data, and solutions_subset/solutions_eq take the checked transcript and actual supplier-semantic identification, with irreducible deg(g)≥3,m≠0, ξ a root and [K:Q]=deg(g), and conclude L⊆/L=thueSolutions g m.  The named tests use these raw types and evaluate the entire checker, including invalid enclosures, wrong output pairs and missing nonsolution rows. The S={2} and S=∅ tests instantiate all finite branches and compute the exact lists; larger named examples require their complete replay data. Before applying Matveev, the finite logarithm list must delete certified zero terms or supply nonzero logarithms for every retained term, and certify the remaining linear form is nonzero; branch choices and the root-of-unity sign are explicit.

nodes.title: Certified solution sets of Thue equations
nodes.statement: Let (g, m) be a Thue equation (n = deg g ≥ 3, g irreducible over ℚ, m ≠ 0) and let c be a ThueCertificate for (g, m) with c.Valid (ED.2/thue-certificate). If s ≥ 1 assume moreover the covering hypotheses (U) and (M) of its factor covering (ED.2/thue-factor-covering). Then thueSolutions g m = c.solutions (as subsets of ℤ × ℤ). In particular every solution either lies in the enumerated box |Y| ≤ C (C = c.searchBound) or is one of the tested candidates obtained from the exceptional exponent vectors, and every solution satisfies |X| < cauchyBound of F(·, Y) − m; there are no other solutions. The proof uses Matveev's lower bound only through ED.2/certified-linear-form-lower-bound, whose constant is computed in the certificate; the name of the theorem supplies no number.
hypotheses: Thue equation hypotheses; c.Valid; covering hypotheses (U), (M) when s ≥ 1
Nothing is assumed about the size of the solutions; nonvanishing of every linear form is proved, not checked numerically
proofSteps: For the target raw theorem first derive the mathematical coverage, initial bounds, reduction implications and complete residual evaluation from the checked finite transcript and supplier semantics; then use the following semantic argument.
⊇: every element of c.solutions passed the exact test F(x, y) = m.
⊆, s = 0: by ED.2/thue-root-approximation (i) every solution has |Y| ≤ Ŷ_0, and the small-solution enumeration up to Ŷ_0 is complete (ED.2/thue-small-solutions).

⊆, s ≥ 1: let (X, Y) be a solution. If |Y| ≤ Ŷ_1 it is in the small-solution list. If |Y| > Ŷ_2′ (≥ Ŷ_1*), ED.2/thue-root-approximation gives the real index i_0, the covering gives μ and a, ED.2/thue-linear-form gives Λ ≠ 0 with the bounds of Lemma 1.2, ED.2/thue-initial-bound gives A ≤ K_3 and ED.2/thue-reduced-bound gives |Y| ≤ C or an exceptional exponent vector (then (X, Y) is among the tested exceptional candidates). If |Y| ≤ C, ED.2/thue-convergent-search puts (X, Y) among the tested convergent candidates. In each case (X, Y) ∈ c.solutions.
acceptance: A theorem row proves that every solution lies in the enumerated box or among the tested exceptional candidates: thueSolutions g m ⊆ {(x, y) : |y| ≤ C} ∪ E_cand, with E_cand the candidates obtained from the exceptional exponent vectors, and thueSolutions g m equals the listed set.

Small instance: for g = X³ − 2 and m = 1 a valid certificate must have c.solutions = {(1, 0), (−1, −1)} (the classical result for x³ − 2y³ = 1); the worked certificate itself belongs to EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6.
The Baker/Matveev source (Matveev, Izv. Math. 64 (2000), Corollary 2.3) is registered separately from Tzanakis–de Weger, and its constant enters only through ED.2/certified-linear-form-constant.

nodes.title: Thue–Mahler equations and their normalised solution sets
nodes.statement: A Thue–Mahler equation is given by g ∈ ℤ[X] with n := g.natDegree ≥ 3, irreducible over ℚ, leading coefficient f_0, an integer c ≠ 0 and distinct primes p_1, …, p_v (v ≥ 0; Tzanakis–de Weger take v ≥ 1, and v = 0 is the Thue equation F(X, Y) = c with normalised solutions) with gcd(c, p_1⋯p_v) = 1; with F := Polynomial.homogenize g n its normalised solution set is thueMahlerSolutions g c p := {(X, Y, z) ∈ ℤ × ℤ × ℕ^v : gcd(X, Y) = 1, gcd(Y, f_0) = 1, F(X, Y) = c·p_1^{z_1}⋯p_v^{z_v}}. The conditions gcd(X, Y) = 1 (essential: otherwise (kX, kY) with k a product of the p_i gives infinitely many solutions) and gcd(Y, f_0) = 1 are part of the definition; the second is automatic when f_0 = ±1. The equation with right side −c·∏p_i^{z_i} is the instance (g, −c, p). With x := f_0X, y := Y, θ := f_0ξ (ξ the class of X in K := ℚ[X]/(g)), the equation becomes N_{K/ℚ}(x − yθ) = f_0^{n−1}c·∏p_i^{z_i} with gcd(x, y) = 1, and θ is a root of the monic G := integralNormalization g (DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.4/thue-equation-monic-reduction). The set is finite (DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.4/thue-mahler-effective-finiteness); this stage certifies it exactly (ED.2/thue-mahler-certified-solution-set).
hypotheses: n ≥ 3, irreducibility, c ≠ 0, the p_i distinct primes not dividing c
Solutions are triples with coprime (X, Y) and gcd(Y, f_0) = 1; the exponents z_i are natural numbers
proofSteps: F(x, y) = c∏p_i^{z_i} ⟺ f_0·N(X − Yξ) = c∏p_i^{z_i}, since f_0∏_i(X − Yξ^{(i)}) = F(X, Y).
N(f_0X − Yθ) = f_0^n N(X − Yξ) = f_0^{n−1}·F(X, Y); gcd(f_0X, Y) divides gcd(f_0, Y)·gcd(X, Y) = 1 under the two coprimality conditions, and conversely gcd(f_0X, Y) = 1 gives both conditions.
acceptance: (3, 1, 2) ∈ thueMahlerSolutions (X³ − 2) 1 (5), since 3³ − 2 = 5².

nodes.title: The Prime Ideal Removing Lemma
nodes.statement: Let θ be an algebraic integer of degree n with minimal polynomial G ∈ ℤ[t] and discriminant D_θ, K = ℚ(θ), p a prime, G = G_1⋯G_m the factorisation into monic irreducibles over ℚ_p, 𝔭_i the prime of K above p corresponding to G_i, with ramification index e_i and residue degree d_i (e_id_i = deg G_i), θ_i^{(1)}, …, θ_i^{(n_i)} the roots of G_i in ℂ_p, ord_p the valuation of ℂ_p with ord_p(p) = 1, e := max_i e_i. Let x, y ∈ ℤ with gcd(x, y) = 1. (i) For every pair i ≠ j there is at most one 𝔭 ∈ {𝔭_i, 𝔭_j} with ord_𝔭(x − yθ) > max(e_i, e_j)·ord_p(θ_i^{(k)} − θ_j^{(l)}) (any k, l). (ii) If d_i > 1 or e_i > 1, then ord_{𝔭_i}(x − yθ) ≤ e_i·ord_p(θ_i^{(k)} − θ_i^{(l)}) for any k ≠ l. Corollary: there is at most one 𝔭_i above p with ord_{𝔭_i}(x − yθ) > ½e·ord_p(D_θ), and it has d_i = e_i = 1; if p ∤ D_θ, at most one 𝔭_i above p divides x − yθ, and it has d_i = e_i = 1. Consequently the ideal (x − yθ) factors as 𝔞·𝔟·𝔭_1^{u_1}⋯𝔭_v^{u_v} with 𝔭_i a prime of degree one above p_i, 𝔞 of absolute ideal norm |f_0^{n−1}c|, 𝔟 supported on the other primes above the p_i with exponents bounded by (i) (at the other degree-one primes) and (ii) (at the primes with d_i > 1 or e_i > 1), and u_i + ord_{p_i}(N𝔟) = z_i, for finitely many explicit choices (TdW (9)).
hypotheses: gcd(x, y) = 1 is essential (it gives ord_p(x − yθ_i^{(k)}) = 0 when p ∣ y)
Orders of ℂ_p-elements are rational; the bounds are computed from finitely many p-adic root approximations (ED.0/padic-embedding-certificate) and are exact rationals
proofSteps: (i): if (x − yθ) = 𝔭_i^{v_i}𝔭_j^{v_j}𝔞 then ord_p(x − yθ_i^{(k)}) = v_i/e_i through the embedding K → K_{𝔭_i} → ℂ_p, similarly for j; hence ord_p(y(θ_i^{(k)} − θ_j^{(l)})) ≥ min(v_i, v_j)/max(e_i, e_j), and ord_p(y) = 0 (if p ∣ y then p ∤ x and both orders vanish) (TdW pp. 231–232).
(ii): if deg G_i > 1 take two roots k ≠ l of G_i; both x − yθ_i^{(k)} and x − yθ_i^{(l)} have order v/e_i and the same argument applies.

Corollaries: ord_p(D_θ) ≥ 2·ord_p(θ^{(h)} − θ^{(l)}) for all h ≠ l, so (8) implies the hypothesis of the first corollary; part (i) of the first corollary gives uniqueness and part (ii) gives d_i = e_i = 1 (TdW pp. 232–233; see sourceIssues EffectiveDiophantineMethods/E8 for the reference to part (i)).

The finite ideal enumeration uses absolute ideal norms, so the fixed norm is |f0^(n−1)c| for either sign of c. Its prime/exponent labels and principal-element reconstruction are distinct obligations; the unramified uniqueness helper proves neither the ramified bounds nor the finite factorization consequence.
acceptance: TdW 5^Ex: for G of the example and p = 5, ord_5(D_θ) = 2 and three degree-one primes above 5; the lemma leaves the five forms 𝔭_{21}^{n_1}𝔭_{31}^{n_2}𝔭_{5j}^{n_3}𝔭_{71}^{n_4}·(bounded) listed on p. 233.
If p ∤ D_θ then at most one prime above p divides x − yθ: for G = t³ − 2 and p = 5 (5 ∤ D = −108), x − y∛2 is divisible by at most one prime above 5.

suggestedOmissions.requiredSignature: For a primitive integral θ of degree n≥2 with K=Q(θ), a prime p, the complete monic irreducible factorization G=∏G_i over Q_p, corresponding prime ideals P_i⊂O_K, their e_i,f_i with deg(G_i)=e_i f_i, and the roots θ_i,k in an actual common finite extension of Q_p, normalize v_p(p)=1 and certify ord_{P_i}(x−yθ)=e_i v_p(x−yθ_i,k). For coprime x,y prove (i) for i≠j at most one v_i,v_j exceeds max(e_i,e_j)v_p(θ_i,k−θ_j,l); (ii) if e_i f_i>1, v_i≤e_i v_p(θ_i,k−θ_i,l) for all distinct k,l. Then with e=max e_i, at most one v_i>(e/2)v_p(disc G), and any such factor has e_i=f_i=1; if p does not divide disc G, any factor dividing x−yθ is the unique such degree-one unramified factor. For a normalized Thue–Mahler equation apply this to each p_i and the certified fixed-norm ideal factorization to enumerate finitely many (a,b,P_i) with (x−yθ)=a b∏P_i^u_i, absolute norm(a)=|f0^(n−1)c|, b supported above the p_i with every nonfree valuation bounded by the explicit pairwise/within-factor bounds, each free P_i of degree one, and u_i+v_{p_i}(norm b)=z_i after separating the fixed norm. Where no degree-one factor exists there is no free exponent. The output has completeness for every normalized solution, obtained from the valuation theorem, not supplied as a generic predicate. The present prime_ideal_removing_unramified signature gives only uniqueness in its squarefree-mod-p branch and does not stand for these conclusions.

nodes.title: Thue–Mahler S-unit coverings
nodes.statement: Let (g, c, p) be a Thue–Mahler equation (ED.2/thue-mahler-equation), θ = f_0ξ, 𝒪 an order of K containing θ, r := s + t − 1. A Thue–Mahler S-unit covering consists of units ε_1, …, ε_r of 𝒪 and a finite list of cases, each case being (α, π_1, …, π_v, h, s′, t′) with α ∈ 𝒪 ∖ {0}, π_i ∈ 𝒪 generating 𝔭_i^{h_i} for a prime 𝔭_i of degree one above p_i (or π_i := 1, h_i := 0 and s′_i := 0 when there is none, and then the representation is normalized to n_i = 0 in (C)), for active primes integers h_i ≥ 1, 0 ≤ s′_i < h_i and t′_i ≥ 0, such that: (U) every unit of 𝒪 is ζ∏ε_i^{a_i} with ζ a root of unity of K (ζ = ±1 when s ≥ 1); (C) for every (X, Y, z) ∈ thueMahlerSolutions g c p, with x = f_0X, y = Y, there are a case, a ∈ ℤ^r and n ∈ ℕ^v with x − yθ = ±α·ε_1^{a_1}⋯ε_r^{a_r}·π_1^{n_1}⋯π_v^{n_v} (TdW (11)) and z_i = n_ih_i + s′_i + t′_i (TdW (10)); roots of unity other than ±1 are absorbed into the finitely many α. The conditions are input hypotheses of the certificate; for 𝒪 = 𝓞_K they are discharged by the Prime Ideal Removing Lemma (ED.2/prime-ideal-removing-lemma) and the ideal factorisations of f_0^{n−1}c and of the p_i (ComputationalNumberTheory:CN.2/prime-ideal-factor-certificate), principal generators of 𝔞𝔟𝔭_1^{s′_1}⋯𝔭_v^{s′_v} and of 𝔭_i^{h_i}, and the unit certificate ComputationalNumberTheory:CN.2/units-complete-of-regulator-bound; DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.4/s-integral-divisor-representation shows that a finite list of cases always exists. The Lean record fixes r = Units.rank K, excludes zero α and π in every case, and records either h_i=0,π_i=1,s′_i=0 or h_i>0,s′_i<h_i. Inactive exponents are normalized to zero by the representation theorem.
hypotheses: The class number is not needed: any h_i with 𝔭_i^{h_i} principal works (TdW p. 226)
(C) is a statement about all normalised solutions; it is not checked by computation inside the certificate
Exactly rank(K) unit generators; every case has nonzero α and π_i, with positive active class orders and bounded remainders.
proofSteps: From (9): (x − yθ) = 𝔞𝔟𝔭_1^{u_1}⋯𝔭_v^{u_v}; write u_i = h_in_i + s′_i with 0 ≤ s′_i < h_i and t′_i := ord_{p_i}(N𝔟); then (α) := 𝔞𝔟𝔭_1^{s′_1}⋯𝔭_v^{s′_v} is principal and x − yθ = unit·α·∏π_i^{n_i}.
The unit is ±∏ε_i^{a_i} by (U); finitely many α arise because 𝔞 and 𝔟 range over finitely many ideals.
acceptance: TdW's five cases of 6^Ex (p. 234) form a covering of their example once (U) and (C) are certified.

nodes.title: Initial bounds for the Thue–Mahler exponents from Yu's and Matveev's bounds
nodes.statement: Fix a case of a Thue–Mahler S-unit covering (ED.2/thue-mahler-s-unit-covering) and put N := max_i n_i, A := max_i |a_i|, H := max(N, A). (a) p-adic step (TdW §7–8): for each l with π_l ≠ 1 let θ^{(i_0)} ∈ ℚ_{p_l} be the root corresponding to 𝔭_l and j, k two further indices (roots of two other linear factors of G over ℚ_{p_l}, or the two roots of one factor of degree ≥ 2); with δ_1 := ((θ^{(i_0)} − θ^{(j)})/(θ^{(i_0)} − θ^{(k)}))·α^{(k)}/α^{(j)}, δ_2 := ((θ^{(j)} − θ^{(k)})/(θ^{(k)} − θ^{(i_0)}))·α^{(i_0)}/α^{(j)} and λ := δ_1∏_i(π_i^{(k)}/π_i^{(j)})^{n_i}∏_i(ε_i^{(k)}/ε_i^{(j)})^{a_i} − 1 = δ_2∏_i(π_i^{(i_0)}/π_i^{(j)})^{n_i}∏_i(ε_i^{(i_0)}/ε_i^{(j)})^{a_i} (TdW (12), from DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.4/siegel-identity), all factors of the first product are p_l-adic units and ord_{p_l}(λ) = ord_{p_l}(δ_2) + n_lh_l (TdW (13), Lemmas 2–4); λ ≠ 0 because x − yθ^{(i_0)} ≠ 0. A YuConstantCertificate (ED.2/certified-padic-linear-form-constant) for (1 + v + r, n(n − 1)(n − 2), p_l), admissible for (δ_1, π^{(k)}/π^{(j)}, ε^{(k)}/ε^{(j)}) in ℚ(θ^{(i_0)}, θ^{(j)}, θ^{(k)}) with exponent vector b = (1, n, a) ≠ 0 and α^b = 1 + λ ≠ 1, gives, through ED.2/certified-padic-lower-bound, n_lh_l + ord(δ_2) < Φ⁺_l·log(n(n−1)(n−2)·max(H, 3)), hence N ≤ c_13(log H + c_14) with explicit rationals c_13, c_14. (b) Archimedean step (TdW §§9–10): with Lemma 6 (A ≤ N[U_{I_0}^{−1}]·|log|ε^{(k)}|| for a suitable k), c_15 := 1/N[U_{I_0}^{−1}] and 0 < c_16 < c_15/(n − 1): if min_i|β^{(i)}| > e^{−c_16A} then A < c_18 + c_17N (Proposition 7), where c_17, c_18 are formed as in TdW from c′_17 := Σ_i max(0, max_j log(p_i^{h_i}/|π_i^{(j)}|)), c′′_17 := Σ_i max(0, log house(π_i)) and c′_18, c′′_18 (c′_17, c′′_17 are the corrected constants of sourceIssues EffectiveDiophantineMethods/E9); otherwise (Case 3, s ≥ 1) the real or complex linear form Λ_0 := log(1 + λ_0) built at an index i_0 ≤ s with |β^{(i_0)}| ≤ e^{−c_16A} satisfies 0 < |Λ_0| < c_27·e^{−c_16A} (c_27 = 1.39c_21 resp. 1.02c_21), and a MatveevConstantCertificate for its nonzero logarithms (terms with zero logarithm deleted, degree bound n(n − 1)(n − 2)) gives through ED.2/certified-linear-form-lower-bound H ≤ c_23 + c_24 log H (resp. the complex analogue with |a_0| ≤ ½(1 + vN + rA)); for s = 0 Proposition 9 bounds A directly. (c) Combining (a), (b) and DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.4/log-linear-inequality-bound gives a rational K_0 with H ≤ K_0 and N ≤ N_0 for every solution in the case (TdW Theorem 10). All constants are certified rationals computed from the root boxes, the p-adic approximations and ED.2/logarithm-enclosure, and every nonvanishing (λ ≠ 0, Λ_0 ≠ 0) is proved from x − yθ^{(i)} ≠ 0.
hypotheses: One case of the covering; the theorem is applied to every case

TdW use Yu (Compositio 1990) and Blass–Glass–Manski–Meronk–Steiner; here the imported bounds are Yu 1994 and Matveev 2000 through the certified constants, and the BGMMS threshold restriction does not arise
proofSteps: (a): the factors π_i^{(k)}/π_i^{(j)} (i ≠ l and i = l by TdW Lemma 3(i)) and ε_i^{(k)}/ε_i^{(j)} are p_l-adic units (Lemma 2: an algebraic integer whose norm is prime to p has unit conjugates); ord(π_l^{(i_0)}/π_l^{(j)}) = h_l (Lemma 3(ii)) gives (13); Yu's bound for the first expression of λ bounds ord(λ), hence n_l.

(b): Cases 1 and 2 of TdW §9 bound |ε^{(k)}| through |β^{(k)}| and the conjugates of α and π_i; the product ∏_i(p_i^{h_i}/|π_i^{(k)}|)^{n_i} is at most exp(N·Σ_i max(0, log(p_i^{h_i}/min_j|π_i^{(j)}|))) and ∏_i|π_i^{(k)}|^{n_i} ≤ exp(N·Σ_i max(0, log house(π_i))), which is where the printed c′_17, c′′_17 must be replaced.
Case 3 follows ED.2/thue-linear-form with π-factors added: Siegel's identity at (i_0, j, k), |e^{Λ_0} − 1| < ½ and the 1.39 resp. 1.02 factors; Λ_0 ≠ 0 because β^{(i_0)} ≠ 0.
(c): H < c_19 + c_20 log H (Proposition 8) and its Case 3 analogues; DT.4/log-linear-inequality-bound turns each into an explicit bound.
acceptance: For TdW's example (using the Baker–Wüstholz constants of the1993 published correction, p.242) the initial bound is H < c_real < 9.844 × 10^{49} (TdW 11Ex); the reduction of ED.2/thue-mahler-reduced-bounds brings it to n_1 ≤ 19, n_2 ≤ 11, n_3 ≤ 8, n_4 ≤ 6, A ≤ 86 outside six exceptional solutions (TdW 17Ex). The uncorrected1992 Appendix A3 constants do not establish this initial bound: use the1993 Baker–Wüstholz route, or start at1.511×10^50 with the corrected BGMMS factor and its H≤4919 bridge (sourceIssues E29).

nodes.title: p-adic and real reduction of the Thue–Mahler exponent bounds
nodes.statement: Fix a case of a Thue–Mahler S-unit covering with initial bounds H ≤ K_0, N ≤ N_0 (ED.2/thue-mahler-initial-bounds) and let 𝒮 ⊆ ℤ^{v+r} be the set of exponent vectors (n, a) of the normalised solutions in that case, with weights W ∈ ℕ^{v+r}_{>0}. (a) p-adic step at p_l (TdW §§12–15): let 𝒪_L be ℤ_{p_l} when θ^{(i_0)}, θ^{(j)}, θ^{(k)} ∈ ℚ_{p_l} (first special case; the images of K-elements are given by EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0/padic-embedding-certificate), or the ring of integers of the extension of ℚ_{p_l} generated by θ^{(j)}, θ^{(k)} (second special case, given by an exact model of 𝒪_L/𝔓^t), with maximal ideal 𝔓 and ramification e_L; for a PadicDiscreteLogCertificate (ED.2/padic-discrete-logarithm-certificate) at level t for γ_0 := δ_1 and the units γ := (π_i^{(k)}/π_i^{(j)})_i, (ε_i^{(k)}/ε_i^{(j)})_i, every (n, a) ∈ 𝒮 with e_L·(n_lh_l + ord_{p_l}(δ_2)) ≥ t lies in the target coset Γ_0, since then δ_1∏γ^{(n,a)} ≡ 1 (mod 𝔓^t). An ED.1 p-adic reduction certificate (EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/padic-reduction) showing that Γ_0 has no point of weighted height ≤ X then gives n_l < (t/e_L − ord_{p_l}(δ_2))/h_l for every (n, a) ∈ 𝒮 with H_W ≤ X (TdW Lemma 14, Proposition 15). (b) Real step (TdW §16): with Λ_0 = ρ_0 + Σn_iλ_{0i} + Σa_iμ_{0i} (+ 2πa_0) from Case 3 and the inequality |Λ_0| < c_27 e^{−c_16A}, an ED.1 real reduction certificate (ED.1/inhomogeneous-reduction, lattice from ED.1/linear-form-lattice with the enclosures of ED.2/logarithm-enclosure) gives A ≤ A_1 for every (n, a) ∈ 𝒮 in Case 3 with H_W ≤ X (Proposition 16); Cases 1–2 give A < c_18 + c_17N directly. (c) Iterating (a) for all l and (b) for all real i_0 is an exponent reduction chain (ED.2/exponent-reduction-chain), possibly with enumeration steps (TdW §17, Fincke–Pohst); its soundness gives final bounds n_i ≤ N_i, |a_i| ≤ A_fin for every (n, a) ∈ 𝒮 outside the finite exceptional sets.

nodes.title: Sieving exponent tuples with auxiliary primes
nodes.statement: Fix a case of a Thue–Mahler S-unit covering. Let q be a prime and 𝔮_1, 𝔮_2, 𝔮_3 three distinct primes of K of degree one above q not dividing f_0·c·∏p_i·disc(θ) and not dividing α, π_i, ε_i; let m_i, A_i, P_{ij}, E_{ij} ∈ 𝔽_q be the residues of θ, α, π_j, ε_j modulo 𝔮_i. Eliminating x and y from x − ym_i ≡ ±A_i∏_jP_{ij}^{n_j}∏_jE_{ij}^{a_j} (i = 1, 2, 3) gives the congruence C_1∏_jP_{1j}^{n_j}∏_jE_{1j}^{a_j} + C_2∏_jP_{2j}^{n_j}∏_jE_{2j}^{a_j} ≡ C_3∏_jP_{3j}^{n_j}∏_jE_{3j}^{a_j} (mod q) with C_1 := (m_2 − m_3)A_1, C_2 := (m_3 − m_1)A_2, C_3 := (m_2 − m_1)A_3 (TdW (38)). Every exponent tuple (n, a) of a solution in the case satisfies this congruence for every such q. Hence a tuple violating it for one admissible q is not the tuple of a solution, and the residual box {n_i ≤ N_i, |a_i| ≤ A_fin} can be reduced to the survivors of finitely many such congruences before the exact test; the congruence depends only on (n, a) modulo the orders of the residues, so it is evaluated on residue classes.
hypotheses: The sieve is a necessary condition only; survivors are tested exactly against (11) and F(X, Y) = c∏p_i^{z_i}
The three primes are of degree one so that the residues lie in 𝔽_q
proofSteps: Reduce x − yθ = ±α∏ε^a∏π^n modulo 𝔮_i (each element involved is 𝔮_i-integral and the 𝔮_i are distinct of degree one).

Siegel's identity in 𝔽_q: (m_2 − m_3)(x − ym_1) + (m_3 − m_1)(x − ym_2) + (m_1 − m_2)(x − ym_3) = 0, which is the stated congruence after substitution (the common sign cancels) (DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.4/siegel-identity, in every commutative ring).
acceptance: A tuple failing (38) for one admissible q is eliminated without any exact test; TdW's final box of (N_1 + 1)⋯(N_v + 1)(2A_0 + 1)^r tuples per case is reduced by sieving before testing (TdW 18Ex).

nodes.title: Thue–Mahler solution certificates
nodes.statement: A ThueMahlerCertificate for a Thue–Mahler equation (g, c, p) (ED.2/thue-mahler-equation) consists of: an S-unit covering (ED.2/thue-mahler-s-unit-covering; its conditions (U), (C) are hypotheses of the soundness theorem); root boxes and p_l-adic root approximations of G (ED.0/archimedean-embedding-certificate, ED.0/padic-embedding-certificate); for every case: the certified constants and the initial bounds K_0, N_0 of ED.2/thue-mahler-initial-bounds (with their Yu and Matveev constant certificates), an exponent reduction chain with p-adic steps given by discrete-logarithm certificates and ED.1 certificates and real steps given by ED.1 certificates (ED.2/thue-mahler-reduced-bounds), the final bounds N_i, A_fin, the exceptional tuples, and a list of auxiliary primes with their residue data (ED.2/auxiliary-prime-sieve); finally the claimed list L of solutions. ThueMahlerCertificate.Valid is the conjunction of: every constant inequality, discrete-logarithm congruence and ED.1 check; every tuple of the residual box of each case either violates a listed sieve congruence or is tested exactly: the element ±α∏ε^a∏π^n is computed in power-basis coordinates, it is accepted when it equals x − yθ with x, y ∈ ℤ, f_0 ∣ x, gcd(x/f_0, y) = gcd(y, f_0) = 1, and (X, Y, z) := (x/f_0, y, (n_ih_i + s′_i + t′_i)_i) satisfies F(X, Y) = c∏p_i^{z_i}; the exceptional tuples are tested the same way; L is exactly the set of accepted triples. All checks are exact computations with integers, rationals and residue rings. This is the target raw finite format specified in suggestedOmissions. SemanticThueMahlerCertificate is the separately named mathematical summary; its Valid field contains real inequalities and universal solution implications, and has no claimed computational Decidable instance. The raw checker derives those implications from the finite transcript and supplier soundness, including all nonsolution rows.
hypotheses: Finite data; a failed check proves nothing
The residual box of each case is finite: (N_1 + 1)⋯(N_v + 1)·(2A_fin + 1)^r tuples
proofSteps: Each check is decidable: rational inequalities, modular exponentiation, exact arithmetic in K, finite enumeration of a box.

Separate finite check from semantic interpretation: first evaluate the full bounded transcript; then use supplier correctness and the named bound/reduction lemmas to prove the semantic summary. No proof field asserting completeness is accepted as raw data.
acceptance: Every check is decidable; a certificate whose residual boxes are not exhausted (an unterminated search) is not valid and proves nothing.

suggestedOmissions.reason: The actual raw covering/bound/reduction/search transcript type and its finite checker are not built; the former signatures expressed semantic validity.
suggestedOmissions.requiredSignature: The finite representation is over a certified number-field presentation Q[T]/(G), with rational power-basis coordinates, integral-basis conversion matrices, an irreducibility certificate, labelled real/complex embeddings, and the actual algebraic root θ. Ideal, unit, root-isolation and logarithm data are outputs of the CN.0/CN.2/CN.4 suppliers already named by this packet. No new generic number-field algorithm is owned here. A raw transcript has no proof fields. All loops have explicit finite index sets or integer ranges; checking uses exact integer/rational arithmetic and modular exponentiation. Supplier soundness theorems identify a checked finite record with the actual field, ideals, roots, units and logarithms. This identification belongs to the soundness theorem and is not a Boolean comparison on R or an assumption that the claimed answer is complete. The covering transcript records the complete prime-ideal factorizations of the fixed norm ideal and of every p_i, finite bounded valuation vectors given by the full removing lemma, all ideal-class remainders, principal generators (or certified nonprincipality), torsion representatives and exactly Units.rank K independent units. It checks ideal products, norms, residue degrees, class-order relations, basis conversions and a complete-unit regulator/index certificate. The finite case index set is exactly the product of these bounded choices, modulo explicitly checked duplicates; an omitted combination rejects. Its soundness derives conditions (U),(M)/(C). A finite list with a proof field saying it covers all solutions is only the separate semantic covering, not this finite input. An initial-bound transcript records every logarithm/height enclosure, degree and nonvanishing input, the chosen Matveev/Yu source formula and all rounded rational constants; it verifies the finitely many rational inequalities of the DT.3/DT.4 bound derivation. A reduction transcript records successive nonnegative componentwise boxes, the exact real or p-adic form and its coefficient/residue identities, the raw ED.1 exclusion or complete enumeration data, and the exceptional exponent vectors. Each step is tagged with the applicable ED.1/ED.2 lemma and checks its complete finite numerical hypotheses. The theorem that all genuine solutions remain in the new box or exception set is derived from those checked records and the identified logarithms; it is never a proof field universally quantifying over the unknown solution set. ThueMahlerCertificate(E, certified K, θ) records the complete finite covering, all initial/reduction transcripts, final componentwise bounds N_i,A, the exact finite exception set, and labelled auxiliary-prime factorization/residue data. Residual rows are indexed by every (case,sign,n,a) in [0,N_1]×…×[0,N_v]×[-A,A]^r and by every exception tuple. A row either names a checked violated sieve congruence or contains the exact power-basis evaluation of ±α∏ε^a∏π^n. Coordinates outside span{1,θ}, nonintegral coefficients, f0∤x, failed coprimality, or failed F(x/f0,y)=c∏p_i^z_i are explicit rejecting outcomes for that row, where z_i=n_i h_i+s_i+t_i. Every bounded row must be covered even when it cannot be a solution; omitting such a row rejects the transcript. Duplicate accepted outputs are removed by Finset equality, and the claimed L is exactly the accepted set. ThueMahlerCertificate.Valid c means c.check=true. Its solutions/residualBox projections are raw finite data; solutions_subset/solutions_eq derive L⊆/L=thueMahlerSolutions from the actual normalized equation, θ a root of integralNormalization(g), [K:Q]=deg(g), checked supplier semantics and the initial/reduction/coverage soundness theorems.  The named tests use these raw types and evaluate the entire checker, including invalid enclosures, wrong output pairs and missing nonsolution rows. The S={2} and S=∅ tests instantiate all finite branches and compute the exact lists; larger named examples require their complete replay data. Before applying Matveev, the finite logarithm list must delete certified zero terms or supply nonzero logarithms for every retained term, and certify the remaining linear form is nonzero; branch choices and the root-of-unity sign are explicit.

nodes.title: Certified solution sets of Thue–Mahler equations
nodes.statement: Let (g, c, p) be a Thue–Mahler equation and C a ThueMahlerCertificate with C.Valid whose S-unit covering satisfies (U) and (C). Then thueMahlerSolutions g c p = C.solutions. In particular every normalised solution has, in its case of the covering, exponents in the residual box n_i ≤ N_i, |a_i| ≤ A_fin (or among the exceptional tuples), hence z_i ≤ N_ih_i + s′_i + t′_i: there are no solutions outside the enumerated box. Yu's and Matveev's bounds enter only through ED.2/certified-padic-lower-bound and ED.2/certified-linear-form-lower-bound with constants computed in the certificate.
hypotheses: Thue–Mahler hypotheses (n ≥ 3, irreducible g, c ≠ 0, gcd(c, ∏p_i) = 1); C.Valid; (U), (C)
proofSteps: For the target raw theorem first derive the mathematical coverage, initial bounds, reduction implications and complete residual evaluation from the checked finite transcript and supplier semantics; then use the following semantic argument.
⊇: every listed triple passed the exact test.

⊆: a solution has a case and exponents (n, a) by (C); ED.2/thue-mahler-initial-bounds gives H ≤ K_0; ED.2/thue-mahler-reduced-bounds puts (n, a) in the residual box or in an exceptional set; by ED.2/auxiliary-prime-sieve it is not eliminated by any listed congruence, so it was tested exactly and accepted, hence it is in C.solutions.
acceptance: A theorem row proves that every solution lies in the enumerated box: thueMahlerSolutions g c p equals the listed set and its exponent tuples lie in the residual boxes.
Small instance: for g = X³ − 2, c = 1, p = (5) a valid certificate's list contains (1, 0, 0), (−1, −1, 0) and (3, 1, 2); the worked certificates belong to EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6.

nodes.title: The S-unit equation x + y = 1 over ℚ and its solution set
nodes.statement: For a finite set S of primes let U_S be the group of rational S-units (DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.4/rational-s-unit-group: x ∈ ℚ^× with padicValRat q x = 0 for every prime q ∉ S). The S-unit equation is x + y = 1 with x, y ∈ U_S, and sUnitSolutions S := {(x, y) ∈ ℚ × ℚ : x ∈ U_S, y ∈ U_S, x + y = 1}. The exponent height of a solution is m(x, y) := max_{p∈S} max(|padicValRat p x|, |padicValRat p y|). Equivalent normalisations: (x, y) ↦ (u, v, w) with u + v = w, pairwise coprime integers composed of primes of S, w > 0 (DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.4/s-unit-equation-coprime-reduction) — de Weger's equation x + y = z in S-integers with gcd 1 (Chapter 6, (6.1)) is the subset with u, v > 0; the six maps (x, y) ↦ (y, x), (1/x, −y/x), (−x/y, 1/y) and their composites permute sUnitSolutions S and preserve m. Scoped exponential equations are instances: for a, b, c ∈ U_S the solutions of ax′ + by′ = c with x′, y′ ∈ U_S correspond to the solutions (ax′/c, by′/c), and equations such as 2^α + 3^β = 5^γ are the subsets of de Weger's triples with prescribed prime supports.
hypotheses: S finite, consisting of primes
x, y range over U_S, signs included
proofSteps: U_S is a subgroup of ℚ^× (DT.4/rational-s-unit-group); the six maps send solutions to solutions because 1 − x = y, 1/x + (−y/x) = 1 and (−x/y) + 1/y = 1.
The coprime normal form is DT.4/s-unit-equation-coprime-reduction; padicValRat of x = u/w and y = v/w are read off from u, v, w, each prime of S dividing at most one of them.
acceptance: (1/2, 1/2), (2, −1), (−1, 2) ∈ sUnitSolutions {2}, and these are all of its elements.

nodes.title: Initial exponent bound for the S-unit equation from certified Yu constants
nodes.statement: Let S be a finite set of primes with |S| ≥ 2. For each p ∈ S let Φ⁺_p be the value of a YuConstantCertificate (ED.2/certified-padic-linear-form-constant) for n = |S|, d = 1, admissible for the rationals (−1, (q)_{q∈S∖{p}}) (h_{−1} ≥ log p ≥ π/10 and h_q ≥ max(log q, log p) suffice), and ℓ⁺_p ≥ Real.log p. Put C_p := (11/10)·Φ⁺_p·ℓ⁺_p, C := max_{p∈S} C_p and let X_0 be a rational with X_0 ≥ max(1, (2C/λ⁻)·L⁺) where 0 < λ⁻ ≤ Real.log 2 and L⁺ ≥ Real.log(2C/λ⁻). Then every (x, y) ∈ sUnitSolutions S satisfies |padicValRat p x|, |padicValRat p y| ≤ X_0 for all p. For |S| ≤ 1 every solution has all |padicValRat p x|, |padicValRat p y| ≤ 1.
hypotheses: S consists of primes; |S| ≥ 2 for the Yu step (Yu's statement needs at least two numbers; the sign −1 is one of them)
The sign −1 is included in the family, as DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.4/s-unit-equation-exponent-bound requires
proofSteps: For p ∈ S, ε ∈ {±1} and b ∈ ℤ^{S∖{p}} with ε∏q^{b_q} ≠ 1: ED.2/certified-padic-lower-bound (with exponent vector (b_{−1}, b), b_{−1} ∈ {0, 1}, B ≤ max(max|b_q|, 3)) gives padicValRat p (ε∏q^{b_q} − 1) < Φ⁺_p·log max(B, 3); since log max(B, 3) ≤ (11/10)(1 + log max(1, B)), |ε∏q^{b_q} − 1|_p ≥ (e·max(1, max|b_q|))^{−C_p}.
This is the hypothesis of DT.4/s-unit-equation-exponent-bound with the constant C, which gives |v_p(x)|, |v_p(y)| ≤ max(1, (2C/log 2)·log(2C/log 2)) ≤ X_0.

Consequently, if an ED.1 certificate (EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/padic-reduction) shows that Γ contains no nonzero vector with max_q|b_q| ≤ 2X (or an ED.1 enumeration lists them all, EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.1/short-vector-enumeration-complete), then every solution with exponent height m(x, y) ≤ X and p ∤ uv has padicValRat p w ≤ t − 1, or b = 0 (then (u, v, w) = (1, 1, 2)), or b is a listed vector. nodes.title: S-unit solution certificates
nodes.statement: An SUnitCertificate for a finite set S of primes consists of: for each p ∈ S a YuConstantCertificate and the initial bound X_0 of ED.2/s-unit-initial-bounds (or the bound 1 when |S| ≤ 1); per-prime bounds f_0(p) := X_0 and an exponent reduction chain (ED.2/exponent-reduction-chain) whose steps are p-adic reductions of ED.2/s-unit-padic-reduction (a prime p, a level M, a PadicDiscreteLogCertificate and an ED.1 lattice certificate or complete enumeration, lowering f(p) to t − 1 (= M for odd p, M + 1 for p = 2, where t = M + 2) given the current bounds f(q) for all q), ending with bounds f(p) for all p ∈ S and a finite list E of exceptional solutions found by enumeration; and the claimed list L ⊆ ℚ × ℚ. SUnitCertificate.Valid is the conjunction of: every certificate check; L equals the set of pairs (x, 1 − x) with x = ±∏_{p∈S}p^{a_p}, |a_p| ≤ f(p), such that 1 − x ∈ U_S (exact factorisation over S of the numerator and denominator of 1 − x), together with the members of E that pass the same test. The residual box has 2∏_{p∈S}(2f(p) + 1) elements and is enumerated exhaustively. This is the target raw finite format specified in suggestedOmissions. SemanticSUnitCertificate is the separately named mathematical summary; its Valid field contains real inequalities and universal solution implications, and has no claimed computational Decidable instance. The raw checker derives those implications from the finite transcript and supplier soundness, including all nonsolution rows.
hypotheses: Finite data; validity is decidable
The bounds f(p) apply to |padicValRat p x| and |padicValRat p y| for every solution outside E
proofSteps: Each check is exact: rational inequalities for the constants, modular exponentiation for the discrete logarithms, the ED.1 checks, and trial division by the primes of S for membership in U_S.

Separate finite check from semantic interpretation: first evaluate the full bounded transcript; then use supplier correctness and the named bound/reduction lemmas to prove the semantic summary. No proof field asserting completeness is accepted as raw data.
acceptance: For S = {2} the certificate with f(2) = 1 and list {(2, −1), (−1, 2), (1/2, 1/2)} is valid.

suggestedOmissions.reason: The actual raw covering/bound/reduction/search transcript type and its finite checker are not built; the former signatures expressed semantic validity.
suggestedOmissions.requiredSignature: An initial-bound transcript records every logarithm/height enclosure, degree and nonvanishing input, the chosen Matveev/Yu source formula and all rounded rational constants; it verifies the finitely many rational inequalities of the DT.3/DT.4 bound derivation. A reduction transcript records successive nonnegative componentwise boxes, the exact real or p-adic form and its coefficient/residue identities, the raw ED.1 exclusion or complete enumeration data, and the exceptional exponent vectors. Each step is tagged with the applicable ED.1/ED.2 lemma and checks its complete finite numerical hypotheses. The theorem that all genuine solutions remain in the new box or exception set is derived from those checked records and the identified logarithms; it is never a proof field universally quantifying over the unknown solution set. SUnitCertificate(S) records the increasing list of distinct primes, certified Yu/logarithm initial-bound data (or the proved |S|≤1 branch), successive per-prime boxes and tagged raw p-adic reduction/enumeration steps, all exceptions, the final bounds f(p), and L. Its final search domain is exactly {±1}×∏_{p∈S}[-f(p),f(p)]. For every sign/exponent tuple, including nonsolutions, it computes x=±∏p^a and y=1−x as reduced rationals, rejects y=0, and strips the primes of S from the absolute numerator and positive denominator of y to certify that both remainders are1. Each exceptional exponent box is enumerated in the same way. All rows are present exactly once in a fixed enumeration, and L is exactly their accepted pairs. Valid c means c.check=true; solutions/finalBound are finite projections, and solutions_subset/solutions_eq take the checked raw record and certified logarithm semantics and conclude L⊆/L=sUnitSolutions S. A quantified real-log inequality or a proof that every true solution was tested is not a checker input.  The named tests use these raw types and evaluate the entire checker, including invalid enclosures, wrong output pairs and missing nonsolution rows. The S={2} and S=∅ tests instantiate all finite branches and compute the exact lists; larger named examples require their complete replay data.

nodes.statement: Let S be a finite set of primes and C an SUnitCertificate for S with C.Valid. Then sUnitSolutions S = C.solutions. In particular every solution (x, y) satisfies |padicValRat p x|, |padicValRat p y| ≤ f(p) for all p ∈ S or lies in the exceptional list: no solution lies outside the enumerated box. Consequently, for a, b, c ∈ U_S, the solutions (x′, y′) ∈ U_S² of ax′ + by′ = c are exactly the pairs (cx/a, cy/b) with (x, y) ∈ C.solutions, and the solutions of exponential equations ±p_1^{α_1}⋯ ± q_1^{β_1}⋯ = r_1^{γ_1}⋯ in primes of S are read off from C.solutions. Yu's bound enters only through ED.2/certified-padic-lower-bound with constants computed in the certificate.
hypotheses: S consists of primes; C.Valid
proofSteps: For the target raw theorem first derive the mathematical coverage, initial bounds, reduction implications and complete residual evaluation from the checked finite transcript and supplier semantics; then use the following semantic argument.
⊇: every listed pair passed the exact membership test.

⊆: by ED.2/s-unit-initial-bounds every solution has height ≤ X_0; by soundness of the reduction chain (ED.2/s-unit-padic-reduction, ED.2/exponent-reduction-chain) every solution outside E satisfies the final bounds f(p), so x = ±∏p^{a_p} with |a_p| ≤ f(p) lies in the enumerated box and passed the test.
The scoped exponential equations are the image of sUnitSolutions S under (x, y) ↦ (cx/a, cy/b), a bijection onto the solutions of ax′ + by′ = c.
acceptance: A theorem row proves that every solution lies in the enumerated box: sUnitSolutions S equals the listed set, and every solution has |padicValRat p x| ≤ f(p) for all p ∈ S or lies in the exceptional list E.

nodes.title: Size of E(ℚ_v)/2E(ℚ_v) at a finite or real place
nodes.statement: Let p be a prime and W an elliptic Weierstrass curve over ℚ_p. Then 2E(ℚ_p) has finite index in E(ℚ_p) and [E(ℚ_p) : 2E(ℚ_p)] = #E(ℚ_p)[2] · |2|_p^{-1}, with |·|_p normalised by |p|_p = p^{-1}; that is, the index equals #E(ℚ_p)[2] for odd p and 2·#E(ℚ_p)[2] for p = 2. For an elliptic Weierstrass curve W over ℝ, 2·[E(ℝ) : 2E(ℝ)] = #E(ℝ)[2]. In the normal form y² = f(x), #E(K)[2] = 1 + #{x ∈ K : f(x) = 0} for K = ℚ_p or ℝ. Because ker μ_K = 2E(K) (Tau Ceti ker_μ_eq over the field K), the same numbers are the orders of the local descent images μ_K(E(K)).
hypotheses: W : WeierstrassCurve K with W.IsElliptic, K = ℚ_p (p prime) or K = ℝ; for the descent-image reading also W.IsCharNeTwoNF.
Index means AddSubgroup.index of the range of nsmulAddMonoidHom 2 on W.toAffine.Point; #E(K)[2] means Nat.card of its kernel.
proofSteps: p-adic case. By the reduction filtration (EllipticCurves Layer 4) E₀(ℚ_p) has finite index in E(ℚ_p), E₀(ℚ_p)/E₁(ℚ_p) ≅ Ẽ_ns(𝔽_p) is finite and E₁(ℚ_p) ≅ Ê(pℤ_p) (Tau Ceti WeierstrassCurve.formalPointHomAdicCompletion, an injective additive map Ê(𝔪_v) → E(K_v) for a model over the valuation ring, whose range is O together with the points whose x-coordinate has a pole, by range_formalPointHomAdicCompletion); for r ≥ 2 the formal logarithm (Layer 1 formal groups, via Layer 4) gives Ê(p^rℤ_p) ≅ (p^rℤ_p, +) ≅ ℤ_p. So E(ℚ_p) has a finite-index subgroup U ≅ ℤ_p. The pinned formal-point range theorem describes the pole-valuation locus; its identification with E₁ and the finite reduction/logarithm comparison remain exactly the existing Layer 4 supplier request, not a claimed current implementation.

For an abelian group B with B[2] and B/2B finite put q(B) = #(B/2B)/#B[2]. The snake lemma for multiplication by 2 on 0 → U → E(ℚ_p) → F → 0 with F finite gives q(E(ℚ_p)) = q(U)·q(F); q(F) = 1 for finite F and q(ℤ_p) = #(ℤ_p/2ℤ_p) = |2|_p^{-1}. This is the Haar-measure count of Flynn–Poonen–Schaefer Lemma 3 in dimension one.

Real case. Order the real roots of f. If f has one real root e then x ≥ e on E(ℝ), so every μ_ℝ(P) has the sign class of x − e equal to +, the image is trivial and #E(ℝ)[2] = 2. If f has three real roots e₁ < e₂ < e₃ then E(ℝ) lies over [e₁, e₂] ∪ [e₃, ∞); the sign vector of (x − e₁, x − e₂, x − e₃) is (+,−,−) or (+,+,+) (at x = e_i the corrected representative of μX has the same signs, f′(e_i) being (+) for i = 1, 3 and (−) for i = 2 in the relevant slot), so the image has 2 elements and #E(ℝ)[2] = 4. Tau Ceti ker_μ_eq over ℝ turns #image into [E(ℝ):2E(ℝ)]. This agrees with E(ℝ) ≅ S¹ or S¹ × C₂ (Cremona §3.3).
The 2-torsion count is Tau Ceti card_ker_nsmul_two.
acceptance: y² = x³ − x over ℚ_3: f has the three roots 0, ±1 in ℚ_3, so [E(ℚ_3) : 2E(ℚ_3)] = 4.
y² = x³ + 1 over ℝ: one real root, [E(ℝ):2E(ℝ)] = 1; y² = x³ − x over ℝ: [E(ℝ):2E(ℝ)] = 2.

nodes.title: Certified local image of the 2-descent map
nodes.statement: Fix W as in the hypotheses and a place v of ℚ, with K_v = ℚ_p (v = p) or ℝ (v = ∞), and write M_v for the square classes (W⁄K_v).M of the local étale algebra A_v = K_v[X]/(f). A certified local image at v (CertifiedLocalImage W v) consists of: (i) a factorisation f = ∏_j f_j into monic irreducibles over K_v — linear factors pinned by Hensel data (ED.0 p-adic embedding certificates), the others certified irreducible by the Newton-polygon criterion (CN.2 Ore residual irreducibility, with the prime-ideal factorisation of p in the global factor fields), real roots isolated at ∞ (ED.0 archimedean certificates) — so that A_v ≅ ∏_j L_j with L_j = K_v[X]/(f_j); (ii) square-class coordinates: an explicit group isomorphism κ_v : M_v ≅ (ℤ/2)^{n_v} built from the valuation parity and finitely many residual quadratic characters on each L_j^×/L_j^{×2} (for odd p: the valuation mod 2 and the Legendre character of the unit part; for p = 2 the unit part read modulo 8 in each L_j; for ℝ the signs at the real factors); (iii) finitely many x₁,…,x_k ∈ ℚ with f(x_i) a nonzero square in K_v, checked by exact rational arithmetic (for odd p: v_p(f(x_i)) even and the unit part a square mod p; for p = 2: even valuation and unit part ≡ 1 mod 8; for ℝ: f(x_i) > 0), so that each x_i is the x-coordinate of some P_i ∈ E(K_v); (iv) the coordinate vectors c_i = κ_v(class of x_i − T) ∈ (ℤ/2)^{n_v}, computed exactly from x_i. The output is the subgroup H_v = κ_v^{-1}(span_{𝔽₂}{c_1,…,c_k}) of M_v. The certificate is complete when #H_v equals the number of local-quotient-cardinality, that is |2|_v^{-1}·#E(K_v)[2] at a finite place and #E(ℝ)[2]/2 at ∞.

μ_v(P_i) is the class of x_i − T because f(x_i) ≠ 0 (Tau Ceti μX_of_eval_f_ne_zero); the y-coordinate of P_i is never needed.

nodes.title: Certified 2-Selmer group of an elliptic curve over ℚ
nodes.statement: A certified 2-Selmer computation for W (TwoSelmerCertificate W) consists of: (i) a finite set S of primes containing 2 and every prime of W.badPrimes; (ii) for each monic irreducible factor f_j of f over ℚ, with field L_j = ℚ[X]/(f_j) and the primes of L_j above S, a certified finite generating set of the group L_j(S,2) of classes in L_j^×/L_j^{×2} with even valuation outside S (Mathlib's IsDedekindDomain.selmerGroup for the ring of integers of L_j): S-unit generators modulo squares and lifts of generators of the 2-torsion of the S-class group, certified complete by the ComputationalNumberTheory CN.2 class-and-unit certificate and Tau Ceti's exact sequence S-units → L_j(S,2) → Cl_S[2]; together these give an 𝔽₂-basis of A(S,2), the classes of M unramified outside S (A(S,2) contains Tau Ceti's W.selmerGroupA (𝓞 ℚ), which is the group for the fixed set W.badPrimes (𝓞 ℚ), and equals it exactly when S = W.badPrimes (𝓞 ℚ)); (iii) the norm map N : A(S,2) → ℚ^×/ℚ^{×2} on that basis, whose kernel K_S is computed by 𝔽₂-linear algebra; (iv) a complete certified local image C_v (local-descent-image, local-image-completeness) for every v ∈ S ∪ {∞}, with the 𝔽₂-linear maps κ_v ∘ localRes_v on the basis of K_S. Its Selmer group is Sel(C) = {m ∈ K_S : κ_v(localRes_v(m)) ∈ span(C_v) for every v ∈ S ∪ {∞}}, an explicit 𝔽₂-subspace with a computed basis; its order is 2^{s(C)}.
hypotheses: W : WeierstrassCurve ℚ with W.IsElliptic, W.IsCharNeTwoNF and a₂, a₄, a₆ ∈ ℤ.
Only the places of S ∪ {∞} carry computed local data; good-place-local-image shows no other place changes the group.

Generators of L_j(S,2): Tau Ceti IsDedekindDomain.selmerGroup.ker_toClassGroup and range_toClassGroup give 0 → O_{L_j,S}^×/squares → L_j(S,2) → Cl_S(L_j)[2] → 0; CN.2/certified-class-unit-completeness certifies the class group and a unit basis, and CN.2/prime-ideal-factor-certificate the primes above S.

nodes.title: Certified local solubility test for y² = g(x)
nodes.statement: For g = ax⁴ + bx³ + cx² + dx + e ∈ ℤ[x] squarefree of degree 4 and a place v, quarticLocallySoluble g v ∈ Bool is defined as follows. v = ∞: true iff a > 0 or g has a real root (certified real root isolation). v = p prime: true iff ZpSoluble(g, 0, 0) or ZpSoluble(g*, 0, 1), with g*(x) = x⁴g(1/x) the reversed quartic (points with x ∈ pℤ_p on g* cover x ∉ ℤ_p and the points at infinity). ZpSoluble(g, x_k, k): let ℓ = v_p(g(x_k)), m = v_p(g′(x_k)); for odd p return true if g(x_k) is a p-adic square or (ℓ ≥ m + k and k > m), false unless (ℓ ≥ 2k and m ≥ k), and otherwise return the disjunction of ZpSoluble(g, x_k + t p^k, k + 1) over t = 0,…,p − 1 (Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer Lemma 6); for p = 2 the same with the Lemma 7 rules: true if g(x_k) is a 2-adic square, or k > m and either ℓ ≥ m + k, or ℓ = m + k − 1 with ℓ even, or ℓ = m + k − 2 with ℓ even and the odd part of g(x_k) ≡ 1 mod 4; recurse if m ≥ k and either ℓ ≥ 2k or (ℓ = 2k − 2 and the odd part ≡ 1 mod 4); false otherwise. The recursion stops by depth k = v_p(disc g) + 2 at the latest. The reversal uses all five coefficient positions, even when e=0; Polynomial.reverse agrees on degree-four inputs, but reverses a lower-degree reciprocal by that smaller degree when reused. Zero polynomial values are accepted as squares before taking their totalized valuation. Only ∞ or prime places are in the correctness domain; generalized even degrees require a separate extension.

nodes.title: Correctness of the quartic local solubility test
nodes.statement: For g ∈ ℤ[x] squarefree of degree 4 and a place v of ℚ, quarticLocallySoluble g v = true if and only if the smooth projective curve y² = g(x) has a ℚ_v-point. For odd p ∤ disc g the answer is true; for the even quartics g = d₁u⁴ + cu² + d₂ of descent via 2-isogeny, disc g = 16·d₁d₂(c² − 4d₁d₂)², so this covers every odd p ∤ d₁d₂(c² − 4d₁d₂). Hence everywhere local solubility is decided by the finitely many places p | 2·disc g and ∞.
hypotheses: g of degree 4 with disc g ≠ 0; v a prime or ∞.
proofSteps: Soundness and completeness of lemma6/lemma7 are Hensel-lemma statements (Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer Lemmas 6 and 7 as transcribed by Cremona); a point with x ∈ ℤ_p or with x ∉ ℤ_p is found by the two calls.

Good odd p: a smooth genus-one curve over 𝔽_p has an 𝔽_p-point (Aitken–Lemmermeyer Lemma 13 for the 2-isogeny quartics, elementary; in general Hasse's bound for the Jacobian, EllipticCurves Layer 3), and a nonsingular point lifts by Hensel's lemma (Aitken–Lemmermeyer Lemma 14).
The real test is immediate from the intermediate value theorem.
acceptance: The test returns true for 2x⁴ − 34 at 2, 17 and ∞, in agreement with Aitken–Lemmermeyer Theorem 4.
For Fermigier's rank-13 curve the test, run over the primes dividing 2dd′, returns n₂ = 256 and n₂′ = 128, the values Cremona reports.

nodes.title: The descent map for a rational 2-isogeny
nodes.statement: Let E : y² = x(x² + cx + d) with c, d ∈ ℤ and d(c² − 4d) ≠ 0, and E′ : y² = x(x² + c′x + d′), c′ = −2c, d′ = c² − 4d. The 2-isogenies are φ : E → E′, (x, y) ↦ (y²/x², y(x² − d)/x²) and φ′ : E′ → E, (x, y) ↦ (y²/(4x²), y(x² − d′)/(8x²)), with φ′ ∘ φ = [2]. The descent map α = α_{c,d} : E(ℚ) → ℚ^×/ℚ^{×2} sends O ↦ 1, (0,0) ↦ d, and (x, y) ↦ x for x ≠ 0. For a squarefree divisor d₁ of d (positive or negative) put H(d₁, c, d/d₁) : v² = d₁u⁴ + cu² + d/d₁. α is a group homomorphism with kernel φ′(E′(ℚ)); its image lies in the group generated by −1 and the primes dividing d, and consists of classes d₁ for which H(d₁, c, d/d₁) has a rational point; the φ′-Selmer group S^{(φ′)} is the set of d₁ for which H(d₁, c, d/d₁) is everywhere locally soluble. Write n₁ = #α(E(ℚ)), n₂ = #S^{(φ′)}, and n₁′, n₂′ for the same with (c′, d′).
hypotheses: c, d ∈ ℤ with d ≠ 0 and c² − 4d ≠ 0; E and E′ as Mathlib WeierstrassCurve ℚ (a₂ = c, a₄ = d, other coefficients 0).
proofSteps: The formulas for φ, φ′ and the identity φ′ ∘ φ = [2] are polynomial identities checked on Mathlib's affine addition formulas.

Homomorphism and kernel: two points have the same x modulo squares iff their difference is in φ′(E′(ℚ)) (Cremona p. 85); x = d₁u², v = uy/x gives a rational point of H(d₁, c, d₂), and conversely (u, v) ↦ (d₁u², d₁uv).
Image in the S-classes: if a prime ℓ ∤ d divides the numerator or denominator of x to an odd power then it divides x² + cx + d to the complementary odd power, impossible since y² = x(x² + cx + d).
acceptance: For E : y² = x³ − x² + x (c = −1, d = 1): α(E(ℚ)) = {1}, n₁ = 1.
