suggestedOmissions.requiredSignature: For a genuine geometric Chabauty datum, a residue disc D(x̃), a certified nonzero differential annihilating a finite-index Mordell–Weil subgroup, and η(P)=∫_O^Pω, a ResidueDiscVerdict is finite raw data with a terminating checker, not a record containing a universal bound on unknown points. It contains: (i) exact curve/base-point/local-parameter identifiers and a certified integration constant; (ii) finite coefficient residue tables for scaled pullback series F(u)=p^sη(φ(p(a+p^k u))) in each encoded ball, where φ is the inverse geometric parameter chart and the finite integers a,k describe the ball (the root uses a=k=0), common absolute precision, a certified nonzero leading coefficient and a last dominant index; (iii) a finite tail-bound transcript whose soundness follows from integral differential coefficients or the CN.4 certified analytic supplier; (iv) either the whole disc as one leaf or a finite full residue-subdivision tree, with all p children at each internal ℤ_p-ball and disjoint leaves covering the root; (v) exact rational/algebraic zero records, their embeddings in ℚ_p via isolating balls, checks of the curve equation and geometric vanishing relation, rationality/nonrationality certificates and distinctness; (vi) for each leaf, the number of distinct recorded zeros equals its checked Strassmann upper bound. Zero-root leaves have bound0 and no point records. Valid means that every finite arithmetic, identifier, covering, disjointness and exact algebraic check succeeds. Under separately stated geometric interpretation and supplier-soundness hypotheses this proves X(ℚ)∩D(x̃)=Z_rat. No list of approximate roots, semantic all-point validity predicate or asserted bound is a raw certificate. Raw shape, finite checks, soundness hypotheses and all tests are exactly the associated hypotheses/API/proofSteps/tests. No universal semantic Valid is advertised as executable. Hypotheses: G of finite index in J(ℚ), so that ω also annihilates J(ℚ) (ED.4/annihilating-differentials (b)); without the finite-index certificate a verdict proves only that the rational points of D(x̃) whose image lies in the saturation of G are listed. Distinct points of Z_rat ∪ Z_irr have distinct parameters t; points are compared exactly, not to finite precision. Interpretation is external to the raw payload: a proved chart identifies every encoded ball with its geometric subdisc, the certified differential has integral derivative in the recorded coordinate, the integration constant and coefficient congruences are sound, and the imported tail producer certifies all omitted coefficients. These are theorems of the actual curve/integration and arithmetic suppliers, not arbitrary Prop fields stored in the certificate. Each nonrational zero is specified by exact algebraic coordinates/defining polynomials and a chosen ℚ_p embedding, with an exact nonrationality certificate. A Hensel-isolated analytic root alone does not prove rationality or nonrationality. Distinct zeros consume one unit of the distinct-zero bound; multiplicity is never inferred from rounded equality. One sufficient root-disc tail rule is: for F(u)=p^s I(pu), s≥0, I′ integral and I≠0, v_p([u^n]F)≥s+n−v_p(n) for n≥1. If the chosen minimum coefficient valuation is m≥0, a cutoff K≥2(m+1) gives every n≥K valuation≥m+1. The constant coefficient is certified separately. The finite table modulo p^M must have M>m and must verify the last coefficient at valuation m. This rule is sufficient, not necessary; refinement may be needed. The interpreted rescaled series must be restricted (coefficients tend to zero), proved by the integral-derivative estimate or a separate analytic supplier theorem, before applying Strassmann.

nodes.title: Chabauty–Coleman certificate
nodes.statement: A Chabauty–Coleman certificate for a smooth projective geometrically integral curve X over ℚ of genus g ≥ 2, given by explicit equations, consists of: (1) a rational base point O ∈ X(ℚ) and a finite list L ⊆ X(ℚ) of verified rational points; (2) a finite-index subgroup certificate (ED.3/finite-index-subgroup-certificate) for a subgroup G = ⟨D₁, …, D_r⟩ ⊆ J(ℚ), whose rank certificate (ED.3/rank-upper-bound) gives rank J(ℚ) = r < g, or, in the conditional variant, a labelled hypothesis 'rank J(ℚ) ≤ r' together with an unconditional certificate that the D_j are independent; (3) a prime p and a good-reduction datum (X, O, p, 𝒳) with a certificate that 𝒳 is smooth over ℤ_p; (4) the complete list of X̃(𝔽_p), with its completeness proved by enumeration of the finite set of points of the special fibre; (5) annihilating differentials ω₁, …, ω_k ∈ Ann_p(G) with certified precision (ED.4/annihilator-precision); (6) for every x̃ ∈ X̃(𝔽_p) a residue-disc verdict (ED.4/residue-disc-verdict) for one of the ω_i, whose Z_rat is contained in L. It is valid when every component certificate is valid and every listed point of X̃(𝔽_p) carries a valid verdict. A certificate whose rank input is the labelled hypothesis is conditional, and every consequence drawn from it carries the same label.
hypotheses: X/ℚ smooth projective geometrically integral of genus g ≥ 2 with explicit equations; r < g.
The prime p may be any prime of good reduction for the chosen model, including p ≤ 2g; exceptional discs are covered by verdicts with certified Strassmann bounds.

Number-field and bad-reduction variants are separate statements with their own hypotheses (ED.4/number-field-chabauty-criterion, ED.4/bad-reduction-bound); this certificate is the good-reduction version over ℚ.
proofSteps: The data are finite: G by finitely many divisors, ω_i by finitely many p-adic digits, verdicts by finitely many coefficients and points; each condition is a finite check whose soundness is the corresponding ED.0, ED.3 or ED.4 node.
The conditional variant records the rank hypothesis as an input field rather than a certificate, following Stoll's Theorem 6 and Theorem 7.
acceptance: The certificate of ED.4/fps-quintic-cycle-curve for C₀(5) at p = 3 is valid and unconditional; those of ED.4/poonen-type-three-two-curve and ED.4/stoll-six-cycle-curve are conditional with their labels.
Degenerate case r = 0: G = 0 and every differential is annihilating.

nodes.title: A valid Chabauty–Coleman certificate determines X(ℚ)
nodes.statement: Let 𝒞 be a valid Chabauty–Coleman certificate (ED.4/chabauty-coleman-certificate) for X with list L. Then X(ℚ) = L. If 𝒞 is conditional on the labelled hypothesis rank J(ℚ) ≤ r, then X(ℚ) = L holds under that hypothesis, and unconditionally every P ∈ X(ℚ) with ι_O(P) in the saturation of G in J(ℚ_p) lies in L.
hypotheses: 𝒞 valid; in the conditional case the conclusion carries the rank hypothesis as a label.
proofSteps: L ⊆ X(ℚ) by verification of the listed points.
Let P ∈ X(ℚ). X is proper, so P ∈ X(ℚ_p) reduces to some x̃ ∈ X̃(𝔽_p), which appears in the complete list (4).

ι_O(P) ∈ J(ℚ); G has finite index (unconditionally from ED.3, or by the labelled hypothesis together with the independence of the D_j), so each ω_i ∈ Ann_p(G) = Ann_p(J(ℚ)) (ED.4/annihilating-differentials (b)) and η(P) = 0.
The verdict at x̃ is valid, so P ∈ Z_rat ⊆ L (ED.4/residue-disc-verdict).
Unconditional part: ω_i annihilates the saturation of G (ED.4/annihilating-differentials (c)), so the same argument applies to P with ι_O(P) in it (Stoll Lemma 5).
acceptance: C₀(5): X(ℚ) = {∞⁺, ∞⁻, (0, ±1), (−3, ±1)} (ED.4/fps-quintic-cycle-curve).
Degenerate case: a certificate in which every disc has N equal to the number of known rational points and Z_irr = ∅ gives #X(ℚ) = Σ N.

nodes.title: Siksek's criterion: Chabauty in a single unit ball over a number field
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field of degree d, C a smooth projective geometrically integral curve over K of genus g ≥ 2 with Jacobian J, D₁, …, D_r a basis of a free subgroup of finite index in J(K), and p a rational prime such that (p1) p is odd, (p2) p is unramified in K, (p3) every prime υ | p of K is a prime of good reduction for C (a good-reduction datum over O_υ, ED.4/good-reduction-chabauty-datum). Fix ℤ_p-bases θ_{υ,1}, …, θ_{υ,d_υ} of O_υ and O_υ-bases ω_{υ,1}, …, ω_{υ,g} of H⁰(𝒞_υ, Ω¹). For ω ∈ H⁰(𝒞_υ, Ω¹) let τ_j = ∫_{D_j} ω = Σ_i t_{ij} θ_{υ,i} (t_{ij} ∈ ℚ_p), T_{υ,ω} = (t_{ij}), T_υ the stack of the T_{υ,ω_{υ,l}} and T the stack over υ | p (a gd × r matrix over ℚ_p). For Q ∈ C(K), a well-behaved uniformiser t_Q at Q (a local coordinate at Q̃ shifted to vanish at Q) and α = (ω/dt_Q)(Q) ∈ O_υ, let A_{υ,ω} be the d_υ × d_υ matrix of multiplication by α in the basis θ, A_υ the stack over ω_{υ,l} and A the block-diagonal matrix of the A_υ (gd × d over ℤ_p). Choose a ≥ 0 with p^a T integral and a unimodular U with U(p^a T) in Hermite normal form with h zero rows; let M_p(Q) be the last h rows of U A. If the reduction M̃_p(Q) ∈ M_{h×d}(𝔽_p) has rank d, then C(K) ∩ B_p(Q) = {Q}, where B_p(Q) = ∏_{υ|p} B_υ(Q) is the p-unit ball of points reducing to Q̃ at every υ | p. The rank of M̃_p(Q) does not depend on U; the necessary dimension condition is h ≥ d. The familiar r ≤ d(g − 1) condition follows when rank(T)=r, hence h=gd−r; without this full-rank assumption it is a sufficient dimension heuristic, not a necessary condition.
hypotheses: Separately stated hypotheses of the number-field variant: (p1) p odd; (p2) p unramified in K; (p3) good reduction at every υ | p; D₁, …, D_r a basis of a free finite-index subgroup of J(K) (its finite index requires an unconditional rank certificate, ED.3).

Finite approximations alone generally certify all h kernel rows only in the full-rank case h=max(gd−r,0), using annihilator-precision. Exact dependencies or another certified kernel construction may also certify a larger h; r≤d(g−1) is not a universal necessity.
proofSteps: Integrality (Siksek Lemma 3.2): for p odd and K_υ/ℚ_p unramified, ∫_Q^P ω = α z + β z² with z = t_Q(P) ∈ πO_υ, α, β ∈ O_υ (ED.4/tiny-integral-expansion (d)).
If P ∈ C(K) ∩ B_p(Q), then m(P − Q) = Σ n'_j D_j with m the index, so ∫_Q^P ω = Σ n_j τ_j with n_j = n'_j/m ∈ ℚ (ED.4/abelian-integral).

Write z = Σ z_{υ,i} θ_{υ,i} and s_υ = min ord_p(z_{υ,i}) ≥ 1; comparing the linear term α z with Σ n_j τ_j in the θ-coordinates and eliminating the n_j by the kernel of p^a T (the rows u_1, …, u_h) gives (u_l A)·(z coordinates) ≡ 0 modulo p^{s+1} where s = min s_υ (Siksek proof of Theorem 2, pp. 9–10).
Rank d of M̃_p(Q) forces s = ∞, i.e. z = 0 and P = Q by injectivity of t_Q on B_υ(Q) (Siksek Lemma 3.1).
acceptance: Siksek §6 applies the criterion with Theorem 3 (sieve combination) to the generalized Fermat equation with signature (2, 3, 10); ED.4 supplies the single-ball criterion, the sieve combination belongs to ED.5.
K = ℚ (d = 1): M̃_p(Q) has rank 1 iff some annihilating ω ∈ H⁰(𝒳, Ω¹) has ω̃(Q̃) ≠ 0 at the reduction, recovering the m = 0 case of ED.4/coleman-bound (a) for p odd.

Choose a ≥ 0 with p^a T integral and a unimodular U with U(p^a T) in Hermite normal form with h zero rows; let M_p(Q) be the last h rows of U A. If the reduction M̃_p(Q) ∈ M_{h×d}(𝔽_p) has rank d, then C(K) ∩ B_p(Q) = {Q}, where B_p(Q) = ∏_{υ|p} B_υ(Q) is the p-unit ball of points reducing to Q̃ at every υ | p. The rank of M̃_p(Q) does not depend on U; the necessary dimension condition is h ≥ d. The familiar r ≤ d(g − 1) condition follows when rank(T)=r, hence h=gd−r; without this full-rank assumption it is a sufficient dimension heuristic, not a necessary condition. Hypotheses: Separately stated hypotheses of the number-field variant: (p1) p odd; (p2) p unramified in K; (p3) good reduction at every υ | p; D₁, …, D_r a basis of a free finite-index subgroup of J(K) (its finite index requires an unconditional rank certificate, ED.3). Finite approximations alone generally certify all h kernel rows only in the full-rank case h=max(gd−r,0), using annihilator-precision. Exact dependencies or another certified kernel construction may also certify a larger h; r≤d(g−1) is not a universal necessity.

nodes.title: Symmetric-square Chabauty datum: X⁽²⁾, its Abel–Jacobi map and reduced vanishing differentials
nodes.statement: Let X be a smooth projective non-hyperelliptic curve of genus g ≥ 3 over ℚ with Jacobian J, ∞ a rational effective divisor of degree 2 (for example 2O or O + O'), and p a prime with a good-reduction datum 𝒳 (ED.4/good-reduction-chabauty-datum, with the base point replaced by ∞). The symmetric square X⁽²⁾ parametrises effective divisors of degree 2; X⁽²⁾(ℚ) consists of the pairs {P, P^σ} of a quadratic point and its conjugate and the pairs {P, Q} of rational points, including the doubled divisor 2P. Braces denote a multiset/effective divisor, never a Finset that loses repeated points. The datum consists of: (i) ι⁽²⁾ : X⁽²⁾ → J, 𝒬 ↦ [𝒬 − ∞], injective because X is not hyperelliptic; (ii) the reduction X⁽²⁾(ℚ) → X̃⁽²⁾(𝔽_p) and its residue classes; (iii) the integral vanishing lattice V = Ann_p(J(ℚ)) ∩ H⁰(𝒳, Ω¹) and its reduction Ṽ (ED.4/annihilating-differentials); (iv) for 𝒬 = {Q₁, Q₂} ∈ X⁽²⁾(ℚ), a prime v of ℚ(Q₁) above p, uniformisers t_{Q̃_j} at the reductions and the expansions ω_i = (a₀(ω_i, t_{Q̃_j}) + a₁(ω_i, t_{Q̃_j}) t + ⋯) dt for a basis ω₁, …, ω_k of Ṽ; (v) the matrix Ã(𝒬): the k × 2 matrix (a₀(ω_i, t_{Q̃₁}), a₀(ω_i, t_{Q̃₂})) when Q₁ ≠ Q₂, and (a₀(ω_i, t_{Q̃₁}), a₁(ω_i, t_{Q̃₁})/2) when Q₁ = Q₂; (vi) in the relative case, a degree-two morphism ρ : X → C to a curve C with good reduction at p, extending to ρ : 𝒳 → 𝒞, the trace Tr : H⁰(X, Ω¹) → H⁰(C, Ω¹), V₀ := V ∩ ker Tr and its reduction Ṽ₀, and the set ρ*C(ℚ) ⊆ X⁽²⁾(ℚ) of pullbacks of rational points.
hypotheses: X non-hyperelliptic of genus g ≥ 3 (so ι⁽²⁾ is an embedding); p of good reduction for X; p odd wherever the diagonal matrix (v) is used (and for C in the relative case, with ρ extending to the smooth models).
The symmetric square of a curve and its points as effective divisors are requested from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3.

The reduced matrix has entries in the residue field generated by the support (or its algebraic closure), not necessarily 𝔽_p. Its two columns retain geometric multiplicities; arbitrary injective coordinates or an assumed Abel–Jacobi injection are not this geometric datum.
proofSteps: X⁽²⁾ = X × X / S₂ is a smooth projective surface whose ℚ-points are Galois-stable effective divisors of degree 2 (SF.3); ι⁽²⁾ is injective since two distinct effective divisors of degree 2 are linearly equivalent only on a hyperelliptic curve.

Expansions of differentials on the reduction with respect to uniformisers at Q̃_j coincide with the reductions of expansions on 𝒳 with respect to lifted uniformisers (Box proof of Theorem 2.1), so Ã(𝒬) depends only on Ṽ.
acceptance: Caraiani–Newton §7.4: X = X(ns3°, ns5), C = X(ns3, ns5), p = 43, with L consisting of eight pulled-back degree-two divisors.

nodes.title: Symmetric Chabauty: a rational point of X⁽²⁾ alone in its residue class
nodes.statement: In a symmetric-square Chabauty datum (ED.4/symmetric-square-chabauty-datum) for X/ℚ non-hyperelliptic of genus g ≥ 3 and a prime p of good reduction, let 𝒬 = {Q₁, Q₂} ∈ X⁽²⁾(ℚ) and ω₁, …, ω_k a basis of Ṽ. Suppose p > 2, and p ≠ 3 when [𝔽_p(Q̃₁) : 𝔽_p] = 1. If rank Ã(𝒬) = 2, then 𝒬 is the unique point of X⁽²⁾(ℚ) in its residue class modulo p. Two independent vanishing differentials exist when r < g − 1; the criterion can fail even then.
hypotheses: Hypotheses of Box Theorem 2.1: p > 2; p ≠ 3 when Q̃₁ is 𝔽_p-rational; X non-hyperelliptic of genus ≥ 3 with good reduction at p.
Ṽ is the reduction of the integral annihilator of J(ℚ) (ED.4/annihilating-differentials); computing it from a finite-index subgroup suffices.
proofSteps: Pass to a common finite extension containing the supports of both rational effective divisors 𝒫 and 𝒬 and extend the chosen prime compatibly. Order the geometric points with multiplicity so that they have matching reductions. The fields of the comparison points are not assumed contained in ℚ_p(Q₁). The divisor 𝒫−𝒬 gives a class in J(ℚ), so the sum of its tiny integrals against every annihilator differential is zero.

Apply the degree-two specialization of Siksek2009 published Theorem3.2, pp.217–222: for each support point of multiplicity d_j, use the first d_j primitive coefficients a₀,a₁/2,…,a_{d_j−1}/d_j and the corresponding power sums of local parameters. Its ramification bound N=e max lcm(e_j,b), 1≤b≤d/f_j, gives N≤2 for d=2 over ℚ. With p>2 and p≠3 in the residue-degree-one case, the integral-tail inequality ord_p(d_j+i+1)≤i/N and p>d_j hold. This is the source valuation argument, not an arbitrary multivariate coefficient bound.

Choose the block of parameters minimizing m_j(d_j+1). Rank2 of the reduced matrix forces the first d_j power sums to vanish modulo the corresponding power of the common uniformizer. Siksek Lemmas3.3–3.4 use Newton identities and p>d_j to force every parameter in that block to have larger valuation, a contradiction unless all vanish. Therefore 𝒫=𝒬 as effective divisors. Box Theorem2.1 pp.4–5 identifies the matrix with reduced differential expansions and allows redundant rows to be removed without changing rank.
acceptance: Box §4.4: for X₀(57) the symmetric Chabauty method alone determines all quadratic points.
Degenerate case k < 2: Ã(𝒬) has rank ≤ 1 and the theorem gives nothing.

nodes.title: Relative symmetric Chabauty (Siksek, Box) and the good-residue-class criterion
nodes.statement: Work in a relative symmetric-square Chabauty datum (ED.4/symmetric-square-chabauty-datum (vi)): X/ℚ non-hyperelliptic of genus g ≥ 3, ρ : X → C of degree 2 to a curve C over ℚ, p a prime of good reduction for X and C with ρ extending to the smooth models, ω₁, …, ω_k a basis of Ṽ₀ (reduction of Ann_p(J(ℚ)) ∩ ker Tr). (a) (Box Theorem 2.4) Let 𝒬 = {Q₁, Q₂} ∈ ρ*C(ℚ) and suppose p > 2 when [𝔽_p(Q̃₁) : 𝔽_p] = 1. If (ω_i/dt_{Q̃₁})(Q̃₁) ≠ 0 for some i, i.e. the k × 1 matrix of constant coefficients has rank 1, then every point of X⁽²⁾(ℚ) in the residue class of 𝒬 lies in ρ*C(ℚ). (b) (Caraiani–Newton Proposition 7.4.1) Let p₁, …, p_s be primes of good reduction for X and C, L ⊆ X⁽²⁾(ℚ) a finite set, and for each i let L_i^good ⊆ L be the set of x ∈ L for which either ED.4/symmetric-chabauty applies at p_i (x is alone in its residue class) or x ∈ ρ*C(ℚ) and (a) applies at p_i. If x ∈ X⁽²⁾(ℚ) satisfies red_{p_i}(x) ∈ red_{p_i}(L_i^good) for at least one i, then x ∈ L ∪ ρ*C(ℚ).
hypotheses: Hypotheses of (a): those of Box Theorem 2.4, including good reduction of C and the extension of ρ to the smooth models; Ṽ₀ computed from Ann_p(J(ℚ)) ∩ ker Tr, for which a finite-index subgroup of J(ℚ) suffices.

Input of (b): finitely many good primes and a finite list L of known points with its partition into pullbacks and non-pullbacks; the sieve over the set M_i^bad := ι_{p_i}⁻¹(red_{p_i}(G)) − red_{p_i}(L_i^good) (Caraiani–Newton Theorem 7.4.2) is ED.5/relative-symmetric-sieve.
proofSteps: (a) For 𝒫 in the residue class of 𝒬 = ρ*(c), [𝒫 − 𝒬] ∈ J(ℚ) and ω ∈ ker Tr annihilates every [ρ*(c') − ρ*(c)] (ED.4/abelian-integral (v)), so the equations Σ_j ∫_{Q_j}^{P_j} ω = 0 cut out, to first order in the residue class, the pullback locus ρ*C; a nonzero constant coefficient a₀(ω_i, t_{Q̃₁}) makes the first-order equation transversal to ρ*C, forcing 𝒫 ∈ ρ*C(ℚ) (Box Theorem 2.4, a special case of Siksek's Theorem 2 for symmetric powers; expansions on the reduction as in ED.4/symmetric-chabauty).

(b) If red_{p_i}(x) = red_{p_i}(y) with y ∈ L_i^good: when y is alone in its class, x = y ∈ L; when y ∈ ρ*C(ℚ) satisfies (a), x ∈ ρ*C(ℚ). This is immediate from the definitions (Caraiani–Newton §7.4).
acceptance: Caraiani–Newton Proposition 7.4.5(1): for X = X(ns3°, ns5), C = X(ns3, ns5) and p = 43, the eight pulled-back divisors in L satisfy (a), red₄₃(G) is cyclic of order 7, and X⁽²⁾(ℚ) = π*C(ℚ).
Box §4: for X₀(N), N ∈ {43, 53, 61, 65}, C = X₀(N)/w_N an elliptic curve of positive rank, (a) handles the infinitely many pullback points.

nodes.title: Chabauty–Coleman certificate for the 5-cycle curve C₀(5) at p = 3
nodes.statement: Let X = C₀(5) be the smooth projective genus-2 curve y² = f(x), f = x⁶ + 8x⁵ + 22x⁴ + 22x³ + 5x² + 6x + 1, birational to the curve of quadratic polynomials with a marked 5-cycle. Then X(ℚ) = {∞⁺, ∞⁻, (0, 1), (0, −1), (−3, 1), (−3, −1)}. Certificate (ED.4/chabauty-coleman-certificate): O = ∞⁺; rank input J(ℚ) ≅ ℤ (Flynn–Poonen–Schaefer Theorem 3, a 2-descent with trivial torsion, certified by ED.3/fps-genus-two-mordell-weil); G = ⟨[(−3, 1) − (0, 1)]⟩, of finite index since its generator is nonzero in the torsion-free group J(ℚ) ≅ ℤ; p = 3 with the two-chart model, smooth since f has unit leading coefficient and is squarefree mod 3 (ED.4/hyperelliptic-residue-discs); X̃(𝔽_3) = {∞⁺, ∞⁻, (0, 1), (0, −1)}; annihilating differential ω = ε dx/y + x dx/y with ε ≡ 2·3 + 3² + 2·3³ (mod 3⁴), from ∫_{(0,1)}^{(−3,1)} dx/y ≡ 2·3 + 3⁴ and ∫_{(0,1)}^{(−3,1)} x dx/y ≡ 2·3² + 2·3³ (mod 3⁵), so ω̃ = x dx/y; verdicts: at ∞^±, m = 0 < p − 2, N = 1, Z_rat = {∞^±}; at (0, 1), t = x, m = 1 and the coefficient of t² in w vanishes mod 3, N = 2, Z_rat = {(0, 1), (−3, 1)}; at (0, −1), by the hyperelliptic involution, N = 2, Z_rat = {(0, −1), (−3, −1)}.
hypotheses: Rank input: J(ℚ) ≅ ℤ, an unconditional 2-descent (FPS Theorem 3), supplied as an ED.3 finite-index and rank certificate (ArithmeticDynamics request to ED.3).
proofSteps: Model and discs: ED.4/hyperelliptic-residue-discs at p = 3 (f mod 3 is squarefree of degree 6 with leading coefficient 1).

Annihilator: Ann_3(G) is one-dimensional (g − r = 1) and is computed from the tiny integrals between (0, 1) and (−3, 1) in the disc of (0, 1) (ED.4/annihilator-precision; McCallum–Poonen Example 3 (4)).

Verdicts: ED.4/residue-disc-zero-bound (b) on the discs at infinity and (c) on the discs (0, ±1) (McCallum–Poonen Example 2); the involution (x, y) ↦ (x, −y) maps Ann_3(G) to itself and exchanges the discs (0, 1) and (0, −1).
Completeness: ED.4/chabauty-coleman-completeness; total Σ N = 6 = #X̃(𝔽_3) + 2g − 2.
acceptance: Supplies part (a) of the ArithmeticDynamics request to ED.4 (consumer ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/flynn-poonen-schaefer-no-rational-five-cycles).

nodes.title: Chabauty–Coleman certificate for Poonen's curve C₁(3₂) at p = 3
nodes.statement: Let X = C₁(3₂) be the smooth projective genus-2 curve y² = g(x), g = x⁶ − 2x⁴ + 2x³ + 5x² + 2x + 1, classifying z² + c with a rational point of preperiodic type 3₂. Then X(ℚ) = {(−1, ±1), (0, ±1), (1, ±3), ∞⁺, ∞⁻}. The certificate is conditional on the rank input rank J(ℚ) ≤ 1 (Poonen Proposition 1), whose corrected 2-descent ED.3/poonen-genus-two-mordell-weil records as a gap; unconditionally, the eight points are the only rational points P with ι_O(P) in the saturation of G in J(ℚ_3). Certificate: O = ∞⁺; rank input as just stated, with J(ℚ)_tors = 0 and rank J(ℚ) ≥ 1 certified; G = ⟨[S⁺ − S⁻]⟩ with S^± = (1, ±3), of finite index; p = 3 with the two-chart model (g mod 3 squarefree, leading coefficient 1); X̃(𝔽_3) = {∞⁺, ∞⁻, (0, ±1), (2, ±1), (1, 0)}, seven points; annihilating differential ω = α dx/y + x dx/y with ∫_{S⁻}^{S⁺} ω = 0, computed in the disc of the Weierstrass point (1, 0) with the parameter t = y + 3, giving α ≡ 68 (mod 3⁴) and ω̃ = (x − 1) dx/y; verdicts: on the six discs other than (1, 0), ω̃ does not vanish, so N = 1 with Z_rat the unique known point ((−1, ±1) reduce to (2, ±1)); on the disc of (1, 0), m = 2 ≥ p − 2 (exceptional disc), the certified disc Strassmann bound of ∫_{S⁻} ω is N = 3, Z_rat = {S⁻, S⁺} (t = 0, 6) and Z_irr = {W}, the Weierstrass point of X(ℚ_3) with x(W) ≡ 1 (mod 3) (t = 3), which is not rational because g has no rational root and is a zero because 2[W − S⁻] = [S⁺ − S⁻] ∈ G.
hypotheses: Conditionality label: 'conditional on rank J(ℚ) ≤ 1'. Poonen's printed 2-descent uses the point (2, √33), which is not on C; his errata replace it by (−2, √33) and the 2-adic information without printing the corrected computation, and ED.3/poonen-genus-two-mordell-weil records this as a gap. Torsion is trivial since #J(𝔽_3) = 27 and #J(𝔽_5) = 43.

The Coleman-integral certificate replaces Poonen's formal-group computation; its numerical values (α, the disc Strassmann indices) are computed in this blueprint from the tiny-integral expansions and are not printed in the source.
proofSteps: Model and discs: ED.4/hyperelliptic-residue-discs; the Weierstrass disc of (1, 0) uses t = y + 3, with x = ξ(t) ∈ ℤ_3[[t]], ξ(0) = 1, and dx/y = 2 dt/g'(ξ(t)).
Annihilator: ∫_{S⁻}^{S⁺} dx/y and ∫_{S⁻}^{S⁺} x dx/y are tiny integrals evaluated at t = 6, both of valuation 1; α = −(∫ x dx/y)/(∫ dx/y) ≡ 68 (mod 3⁴) (ED.4/annihilator-precision).
Orders of ω̃ = (x − 1) dx/y: a double zero at the Weierstrass point (1, 0) and no other zero (degree 2g − 2 = 2), so ED.4/residue-disc-zero-bound (b) gives N = 1 on six discs.

Exceptional disc: the rescaled coefficients of ∫_{S⁻} ω have v(a_i) + i = ∞, 2, 3, 2, 6, 6, 7, … for i = 0, 1, 2, …, so N_3 = 3 by ED.4/residue-disc-zero-bound (d); the zeros t = 0, 3, 6 are S⁻, W, S⁺, where 2W ∼ S⁺ + S⁻ gives 2∫_{S⁻}^{W} ω = ∫_{S⁻}^{S⁺} ω = 0 (ED.4/abelian-integral).
Completeness: ED.4/chabauty-coleman-completeness in its conditional form gives the eight points, in agreement with Poonen Proposition 2; its unconditional part gives the saturation statement.
acceptance: Supplies part (b) of the ArithmeticDynamics request to ED.4 (consumer ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/poonen-type-three-two), with the conditionality label on the rank input; the variant embedding P ↦ [P + S⁺] of Poonen's formal-group proof is not needed in the Coleman version because the exceptional disc is settled by its certified Strassmann bound with the zero W listed.
Check: Σ N = 6·1 + 3 = 9 zeros, of which W is not rational, leaving the eight listed rational points.

nodes.title: Conditional Chabauty–Coleman certificate for Stoll's curve X₀^dyn(6) at p = 5
nodes.statement: Let X = X₀^dyn(6) be the genus-4 curve given by the smooth model G(u, w) = w²(w + 1)u³ − (5w² + w + 1)u² − w(w² − 2w − 7)u + (w + 1)(w − 3) = 0 of bidegree (3, 3) in ℙ¹ × ℙ¹, with the ten rational points P₀, …, P₉ of Stoll's table. Unconditionally: J(ℚ) has trivial torsion, the subgroup G generated by differences of the P_i is ≅ ℤ³, and the P_i are the only rational points P with [P − P₁] in the saturation of G. Conditionally on the labelled hypothesis rank J(ℚ) ≤ 3 (which follows from analytic continuation and the standard functional equation of L(J, s), a certified nonvanishing L'''(J,1)≠0 (Stoll’s value 0.836… is numerical, and his reported lower-derivative vanishings are only to working precision), and the weak Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture for J; Stoll §4 and Theorem 7), X(ℚ) = {P₀, …, P₉}. Certificate: O = P₁; G with generators of G ∩ J(ℚ_5)¹ given by D₁ = P₇ − P₉, D₂ = P₀ − 6P₁ + 2P₅ + P₇ + P₈ + P₉, D₃ = P₀ − 3P₁ + 2P₂ + P₄ + P₆ − P₇ − P₈; p = 5 (the model has good reduction away from 2 and 8029187); the annihilating differential ω, computed by ED.4/kernel-of-reduction-evaluation at P₁ = (0, −1) with parameter u, has reduction ω̄ = ω̄₂ = w ω̄₀; verdicts: at (∞, −1), m = 1 < p − 2 = 3, N = 2, Z_rat = {P₇, P₉}; at (∞, 0), where ω̄ also vanishes, the explicit expansion λ = γτ(1 − (2 + O(5))5τ + O(5²)) gives N = 1, Z_rat = {P₃}; at every other point of X̃(𝔽_5), ω̄ does not vanish and N = 1, and each such disc contains one of the P_i (the reduction map on {P₀, …, P₉} is onto X̃(𝔽_5)).
hypotheses: Conditionality label: 'conditional on rank J(ℚ)≤3'. An analytic derivation additionally needs certified analytic order≤3, along with analytic continuation/functional equation and weak BSD; Stoll’s numerical evidence is not that certificate. The unconditional statement concerns the saturation of G.

ED.3/stoll-genus-four-subgroup supplies the unconditional part of the rank input (G ≅ ℤ³, trivial torsion) and labels the analytic rank bound; under rank J(ℚ) = 3 the Chabauty step uses the saturation of G directly, so no p-saturation certificate is needed.
proofSteps: Rank: G ≅ ℤ³ by reduction maps at S = {3, 5, 7, 11, 13} and six explicit relations (Stoll Lemma 4); under the labelled hypothesis G has finite index in J(ℚ).

Annihilator: Ann_5(G) is one-dimensional (g − 3 = 1); the integrals ⟨D_j, ω_i⟩ are computed by ED.4/kernel-of-reduction-evaluation from degree-four divisors supported in the disc of P₁, and the kernel of the 4 × 3 matrix gives ω (ED.4/annihilator-precision).
Verdicts: ED.4/residue-disc-zero-bound (b) at (∞, −1) and on the discs where ω̄ ≠ 0; (d) with Stoll's explicit expansion at (∞, 0) based at P₃.
Conclusion: ED.4/chabauty-coleman-completeness in its conditional form; its unconditional part gives Stoll Lemma 5, since ω kills the saturation of G.
acceptance: Supplies part (c) of the ArithmeticDynamics request to ED.4 (consumer ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/stoll-conditional-no-rational-six-cycles), keeping the conditionality label.
Check: 10 points in 9 residue classes, the only shared class being that of (∞, −1) with N = 2.

nodes.title: Strassmann's theorem: zeros of a restricted power series on the closed unit disc
nodes.statement: Let K be a field with a complete nonarchimedean (ultrametric) absolute value |·| (for example ℚ_p or a finite extension of ℚ_p), and let f = Σ_{n≥0} a_n x^n ∈ K[[x]] be nonzero with |a_n| → 0 (f is restricted at radius 1, Mathlib's PowerSeries.IsRestricted 1). Let N be the largest index with |a_N| = max_n |a_n| (it exists: the last coefficient attaining the Gauss norm at radius 1). Then f has at most N distinct zeros in the closed unit disc {x ∈ K : |x| ≤ 1}. In particular a nonzero restricted power series has finitely many zeros there, and if N = 0 it has none.
hypotheses: K complete with respect to a nonarchimedean absolute value; f ∈ K[[x]], f ≠ 0, |a_n| → 0.
Zeros are counted as distinct points x with |x| ≤ 1, at which the series Σ a_n x^n converges.
proofSteps: Existence of N: TauCeti.PowerSeries.exists_max_eq_gaussNorm_of_isRestricted at radius c = 1 gives an index N with |a_N| equal to the Gauss norm PowerSeries.gaussNorm and |a_m| strictly smaller for every m > N.
Induction on N. If N = 0 then |a_0| > |a_n| ≥ |a_n x^n| for n ≥ 1 and |x| ≤ 1, so |f(x)| = |a_0| ≠ 0 by the ultrametric inequality.

If f(α) = 0 with |α| ≤ 1, write f(x) = f(x) − f(α) = (x − α)g(x) with g = Σ_j b_j x^j, b_j = Σ_{n>j} a_n α^{n−1−j}; the b_j tend to 0, |b_j| ≤ |a_N| for all j, |b_{N−1}| = |a_N| and |b_j| < |a_N| for j ≥ N, so the last dominant index of g is N − 1.
Every zero of f in the closed unit disc other than α is a zero of g, so f has at most 1 + (N − 1) = N zeros (Flynn–Poonen–Schaefer, Theorem 4, citing Cassels' Local Fields p.62).
acceptance: f = x − x² over ℚ_p: N = 2 (|a_1| = |a_2| = 1) and the zeros 0, 1 are exactly two.
f = 1 + p x: N = 0 and f has no zero in ℤ_p (its zero −1/p has absolute value p).
LV.3's acceptance instance: Strassmann's bound for 1 + pX + X² + pX⁵ over ℚ_p is 2.
Applied to f(pT) for a Coleman integral on a residue disc, it bounds the zeros in the disc (ED.4/residue-disc-zero-bound).

sources.excerpt: Define r uniquely by: |cr |p ≥ |ci |p for all i ≥ 0, and |cr |p > |ci |p for all i > r. Then there are at most r values of x ∈ Zp such that θ(x) = 0.

nodes.title: Admissible quotient classes
nodes.statement: Write q_L:Γ→Γ/L for the native quotient map, G_{L,i}=Gᵢ/φᵢ(L), q_{L,i}:Gᵢ→G_{L,i}, and φ_{L,i}:Γ/L→G_{L,i} for the native induced map. Write A_S(L) for admissibleClasses(S,L,φ,X). Define A_S(L)={a∈Γ/L : φ_{L,i}(a)∈q_{L,i}(Xᵢ) for every i∈S}. This is the filter of the finite enumeration of Γ/L by these conditions. Xᵢ is a set of allowed local values, not a subgroup. The construction quotients the local group by the image φᵢ(L), not by L itself.
hypotheses: Γ is an abelian group; S is a finite set of local indices; each Gᵢ is an abelian group; φᵢ:Γ→Gᵢ is an additive homomorphism; Xᵢ is a finite subset of Gᵢ.

L is an additive subgroup and Γ/L has a specified finite enumeration. Surjectivity of φᵢ, finite generation of Γ and finiteness of Gᵢ are not required for these statements; the source application provides them.
proofSteps: Use native subgroup image to form φᵢ(L); Subgroup.le_comap_map gives the containment needed for the native induced quotient map, through its additive companion.

Form each allowed image with Finset.image. Filter Finset.univ by the finite conjunction of local membership tests. Classical decidability in the suggested signatures specifies the mathematics; certified finite presentations must supply executable comparisons in an implementation.
No new finite-group carrier, quotient-group construction or general certificate schema is introduced.
acceptance: Empty S retains every quotient class.
An empty Xᵢ at a selected index rejects all classes.
The torsion group ℤ/4 and the allowed set {1,3} retain both odd classes.
With one selected index, membership is exactly that single local test.
Replacing g by g+ℓ for ℓ∈L does not change admissibility.
For L=0, the congruence becomes equality with a value in Xᵢ.
Adding a vacuous local test leaves the set unchanged; adding an incompatible test can make it empty.
For the zero map ℤ/2→ℤ/4 and X={1}, the hypothesis fails and the initial candidate set is empty.
With S empty the condition is vacuous and the unique class survives.
Replacing {1} by {1,3} for the identity map on ℤ/4 can add a survivor; it cannot remove one.

nodes.statement: Write q_L:Γ→Γ/L for the native quotient map, G_{L,i}=Gᵢ/φᵢ(L), q_{L,i}:Gᵢ→G_{L,i}, and φ_{L,i}:Γ/L→G_{L,i} for the native induced map. Write A_S(L) for admissibleClasses(S,L,φ,X). Define refineClasses(S,K,L,σ,B) as the union, over a∈B, of {σ(a)+z : z∈ker π}, followed by the local filter defining A_S(K). The kernel is enumerated inside the finite quotient Γ/K. Correctness requires π(σ(a))=a for a∈B; the function is defined even if that check fails.
hypotheses: Γ is an abelian group; S is a finite set of local indices; each Gᵢ is an abelian group; φᵢ:Γ→Gᵢ is an additive homomorphism; Xᵢ is a finite subset of Gᵢ.

For each a∈B, translate the kernel enumeration by σ(a), using Finset.image; take Finset.biUnion over B.
Filter the resulting set by membership in A_S(K). All loops are finite for the supplied enumerations. The specification imposes no claim about the cost of computing them.

nodes.title: A subgroup covers a coprime sieve quotient
nodes.statement: Let H,L≤Γ for an abelian group Γ, let N be a natural number, assume NΓ⊆L and gcd([Γ:H],N)=1, with the native natural index. Then H→Γ/L, h↦q_L(h), is surjective. The usual application has [Γ:H] finite and N>0. The statement also includes the harmless N=1 boundary even if the native index is zero.
hypotheses: Γ is an abelian group; H,L are additive subgroups; NΓ⊆L; gcd(H.index,N)=1.
proofSteps: Set d=[Γ:H]. The additive companion of Subgroup.pow_index_mem gives d·g∈H for every g.
By Nat.gcd_eq_gcd_ab and coprimality choose integers u,v with d u+N v=1. Put h=u·(d·g), an element of H.
The difference g−h equals v·(N·g), which lies in L. Native quotient equality therefore gives q_L(h)=q_L(g). Surjectivity of q_L completes the proof.
This establishes coverage of the sieve quotient only. It does not certify H=Γ, its index, saturation, or the image of H under a finer local map.
acceptance: H=2ℤ and L=3ℤ cover all three residue classes.
H=2ℤ and L=2ℤ do not cover ℤ/2; the coprimality assumption fails.
For N=1 the quotient is trivial.

sources.excerpt: It is sufficient to know generators of a finite-index subgroup whose index is coprime to a certain set of primes.
sources.match: The source's remark that a subgroup of index prime to the relevant primes suffices; the node proves the group-theoretic core (surjectivity onto Γ/L when NΓ ⊆ L and the index is prime to N). The full transfer of the sieve is coprime-index-transfer.

nodes.title: Applying the obstruction to commuting maps

Let P be an existing type, j:P→Γ a map, and rᵢ:P→Gᵢ maps with φᵢ(j(p))=rᵢ(p) and rᵢ(p)∈Xᵢ for every p and every i∈S. If A_S(L)=∅ then P is empty. hypotheses: Γ is an abelian group; S is a finite set of local indices; each Gᵢ is an abelian group; φᵢ:Γ→Gᵢ is an additive homomorphism; Xᵢ is a finite subset of Gᵢ.

L is an additive subgroup and Γ/L has a specified finite enumeration. Surjectivity of φᵢ, finite generation of Γ and finiteness of Gᵢ are not required for these statements; the source application provides them.
proofSteps: Any p gives a global element j(p). Commutativity and local containment show that it satisfies all local constraints.
Apply empty-sieve-obstruction. This argument consumes actual maps and equalities on their values.
For P = C(ℚ) the points, the Abel–Jacobi map, the reduction maps, the local images and the commuting squares are supplied by jacobian-reduction-data; the curve instance is curve-sieve-soundness.
acceptance: A certified local superset can be used through local-overapproximations.
An arbitrary type P with the displayed maps is a legitimate test case; calling it a curve is not part of the theorem.

sources.excerpt: Under the assumptions made, now we can compute the images of α and β and check whether they are disjoint.
sources.match: Disjointness of the two images in the commutative diagram is the obstruction; the node states it for an arbitrary type of points with value-level commuting maps.

nodes.title: Completeness from unique residue fibres
nodes.statement: Write q_L:Γ→Γ/L for the native quotient map, G_{L,i}=Gᵢ/φᵢ(L), q_{L,i}:Gᵢ→G_{L,i}, and φ_{L,i}:Γ/L→G_{L,i} for the native induced map. Write A_S(L) for admissibleClasses(S,L,φ,X). Let P be an existing type with j:P→Γ and W⊆P finite. Assume every j(p) satisfies all local constraints; every a∈A_S(L) equals q_L(j(w)) for some w∈W; and q_L∘j is injective. Then every p∈P belongs to W.
hypotheses: Γ is an abelian group; S is a finite set of local indices; each Gᵢ is an abelian group; φᵢ:Γ→Gᵢ is an additive homomorphism; Xᵢ is a finite subset of Gᵢ.

L is an additive subgroup and Γ/L has a specified finite enumeration. Surjectivity of φᵢ, finite generation of Γ and finiteness of Gᵢ are not required for these statements; the source application provides them.
proofSteps: Global-soundness puts the residue of j(p) in A_S(L). The coverage hypothesis provides w∈W with the same residue.
Injectivity of q_L∘j identifies p with w. Transfer membership in W along this equality.

In geometric applications injectivity requires a Chabauty residue-disc uniqueness theorem or a height separation bound. A finite sieve by itself supplies no such injectivity, and many curves do not satisfy it for a given modulus.
acceptance: The conclusion can fail without the uniqueness hypothesis even if all quotient classes are represented by known points.
A singleton quotient can establish completeness only when the relevant point set has at most one element.

sources.excerpt: in each of the cosets or residue classes under consideration there can be at most one rational point, then this provides a way of determining the set of rational points on the curve
sources.match: The source's completeness principle: uniqueness in each class plus a represented sieve set determines the points. The node states it with injectivity of P ↦ q_L(j(P)) as an explicit hypothesis.

nodes.title: Reduction data for a curve and its Jacobian
nodes.statement: Let C/ℚ be a smooth projective geometrically integral curve of genus g ≥ 1 with Jacobian J = Pic⁰_{C/ℚ}, and let D₁ be a ℚ-rational divisor of degree one (D₁ = P₀ for a rational point P₀, or D₁ = D − W with D a rational divisor of degree three and W a canonical divisor on a genus-two curve). Put ι: C(ℚ) → J(ℚ), ι(P) = [P − D₁]. Let S be a finite set of primes p at which C has a smooth proper model 𝒞_p over ℤ_(p) with geometrically connected fibres; write C̃_p for the special fibre and J̃_p = Pic⁰ of C̃_p. The construction produces for each p ∈ S: (a) the reduction of points red_p: C(ℚ) → C̃_p(𝔽_p), the special point of the unique section of 𝒞_p extending P; (b) the reduction homomorphism ρ_p: J(ℚ) → J̃_p(𝔽_p), the specialisation map of the Néron model of J over ℤ_(p), which is the abelian scheme Pic⁰ of 𝒞_p; (c) the reduced divisor D̄₁ (closure of D₁ in 𝒞_p restricted to the special fibre) and ι_p: C̃_p(𝔽_p) → J̃_p(𝔽_p), ι_p(R) = [R − D̄₁]; (d) the commuting square ρ_p(ι(P)) = ι_p(red_p(P)) for all P ∈ C(ℚ), and more generally ρ_p([E − d·D₁]) = [Ē − d·D̄₁] for every rational effective divisor E of degree d, which gives the same square on the symmetric power C^(d)(ℚ); (e) the finite local image X_p = ι_p(C̃_p(𝔽_p)) ⊆ J̃_p(𝔽_p). The output is the record JacobianReductionData (points P = C(ℚ) or C^(d)(ℚ), group Γ = J(ℚ) or a subgroup containing the image of ι, residue points, local groups, ι, red_p, ρ_p, ι_p and the square), which is exactly the input of admissible-classes and certified-map-obstruction. In genus one with D₁ = O it is the reduction of points on a minimal Weierstrass model, and ι, ι_p are the identifications E ≅ Pic⁰.
hypotheses: C/ℚ smooth, projective, geometrically integral, of genus g ≥ 1; D₁ a ℚ-rational divisor of degree one.
Every p ∈ S is a prime of good reduction: C has a smooth proper model over ℤ_(p) with geometrically connected fibres.
The Lean interface takes the points, the groups and the maps as inputs together with the square; the geometric construction above produces them.
proofSteps: Valuative criterion of properness: C(ℚ) = 𝒞_p(ℤ_(p)); composing a section with the closed point gives red_p. The smooth model is a regular proper model with smooth special fibre in the sense of StableReduction Layer 5.

Pic⁰ of 𝒞_p is an abelian scheme over ℤ_(p) with generic fibre J and special fibre J̃_p (request to NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties:R11.4); by R11.1/abelian-scheme-model it is the Néron model of J, so J(ℚ) = 𝒩(ℤ_(p)) and ρ_p is the specialisation 𝒩(ℤ_(p)) → 𝒩(𝔽_p), a homomorphism because 𝒩 is a group scheme.

A rational divisor on C extends by closure to a horizontal relative divisor on 𝒞_p of the same degree; in degree zero the class of its line bundle is a ℤ_(p)-point of Pic⁰ restricting to [D] and [D̄]. Applied to P − D₁ this is the square (d); applied to E − d·D₁ it is the symmetric-power square used by relative-symmetric-sieve.
C̃_p(𝔽_p) is finite, so X_p is a finite subset of the finite group J̃_p(𝔽_p) = Pic⁰(C̃_p) (JacobianChallenge Layers D–E over 𝔽_p).

Genus one: with D₁ = O, P ↦ [P − O] is the group isomorphism of AlgebraicCurves Layer 10 (Riemann–Roch group law), ρ_p is the reduction of points on a minimal Weierstrass equation from EllipticCurves Layer 4, ι_p is a bijection and X_p = Ẽ(𝔽_p).
Executable presentations of J̃_p(𝔽_p), of ρ_p on generators and of X_p (Mumford representation, Cantor's algorithm, discrete logarithms) are the recorded gap on certified finite presentations.
acceptance: The commuting square holds for every rational point and every place in S, and for every rational effective divisor of degree d.
For an elliptic curve with D₁ = O every local image is the whole group, so good places alone never give an obstruction.

uses.how: the diagram C(ℚ) → J(ℚ)/NJ(ℚ), ∏ C(𝔽_p) → ∏ J(𝔽_p)/NJ(𝔽_p) is this record composed with the quotient by N (mapLocal).
φ_p is ρ_p on generators of J(ℚ), and the image of C(𝔽_p) is X_p, computed with ι(P) = [P + W − D].
ι(x) = I·([x] − ∞) on X^(2)(ℚ) with its reduction ι_p is the symmetric-square instance.
each consumes the record: points, local images and the square.

nodes.title: Rational points survive the Mordell–Weil sieve
nodes.statement: Let D be jacobian reduction data for C/ℚ with places S, L ≤ Γ a subgroup with Γ/L finite, and for each p ∈ S let Y_p ⊆ G_p be a finite set containing X_p (the exact local image or a certified superset, for instance from bad or deep information). Then for every P ∈ C(ℚ) the class q_L(ι(P)) lies in admissibleClasses(S, L, ρ, Y). Hence if this set is empty then C(ℚ) = ∅. With L = NΓ and the local data composed with G_p → G_p/NG_p this says that the image of C(ℚ) in J(ℚ)/NJ(ℚ) lies in Bruin–Stoll's A(S, N).
hypotheses: D is jacobian reduction data; S ⊆ the places of D; Γ/L is finite; X_p ⊆ Y_p for every p ∈ S.
Γ is an abelian group, S a finite set of places, each G_i an abelian group, φ_i: Γ → G_i additive and X_i ⊆ G_i finite; L ≤ Γ has finite quotient Γ/L. Surjectivity of φ_i is not assumed.
proofSteps: red_aj_mem_localImage gives ρ_p(ι(P)) ∈ X_p ⊆ Y_p for every p ∈ S.

global-soundness applied to g = ι(P) gives q_L(ι(P)) ∈ admissibleClasses(S, L, ρ, Y); certified-map-obstruction with j = ι and r_p = ι_p ∘ red_p gives emptiness of C(ℚ) from emptiness of the sieve set.
local-overapproximations justifies working with Y_p ⊇ X_p; for mapLocal data the local sets are the images of X_p in the quotients.
acceptance: For an elliptic curve with D₁ = O the local images are full, the sieve set is Γ/L for every S, and the theorem holds without giving an obstruction.
For Γ = ℤ/2 with two places and local sets {0}, {1}, A_S(Γ) = {0} is nonempty although no element of Γ satisfies both conditions: nonemptiness proves nothing.

nodes.title: Local sieve data from finite quotients of J(ℚ_p)
nodes.statement: Let ι: C(ℚ) → J(ℚ) be as in jacobian-reduction-data, p any prime (of good or bad reduction) and U ≤ J(ℚ_p) an open subgroup of finite index: J¹(ℚ_p) (kernel of reduction for a given model), J⁰(ℚ_p) (points reducing into the identity component) or Jⁿ(ℚ_p) (the pⁿℤ_p-points of the formal group). Put Γ = J(ℚ), K_U = Γ ∩ U, G_U = Γ/K_U with quotient map φ_U, and X_U = {c ∈ G_U : some g ∈ Γ with class c has (g + U) ∩ ι(C(ℚ_p)) ≠ ∅}, or any certified finite superset X′_U ⊇ X_U. For every P ∈ C(ℚ), φ_U(ι(P)) ∈ X_U, so (G_U, φ_U, X_U) is a valid local datum for admissible-classes. For U = J¹(ℚ_p) at a prime of good reduction, the reduction isomorphism J(ℚ_p)/J¹(ℚ_p) ≅ J̃_p(𝔽_p) identifies G_U with ρ_p(Γ) and X_U with X_p ∩ ρ_p(Γ): this is the normalisation of Bruin–Stoll §3.1, where G_p is replaced by the image of φ_p and X_p by its intersection with that image.
hypotheses: ι: C(ℚ) → J(ℚ) from a rational degree-one class; U ≤ J(ℚ_p) open of finite index; X′_U ⊇ X_U finite.
In the Lean interface J(ℚ_p) is an abelian group A with a homomorphism incl: Γ → A, U an additive subgroup of A and Y ⊆ A the image of the local points; finiteness of Γ/(Γ ∩ U) is an input.
proofSteps: Finiteness: J¹(ℚ_p) has index #𝒩(𝔽_p) in J(ℚ_p) and the logarithm maps Jⁿ(ℚ_p) onto (pⁿℤ_p)^g for p odd (and for n ≥ 2 when p = 2), so each Jⁿ, and every subgroup U containing one of them, has finite index (ED.4/abelian-logarithm (c)); Γ/K_U injects into J(ℚ_p)/U.
Soundness: for P ∈ C(ℚ) take g = ι(P) and the local point ι(P) ∈ ι(C(ℚ_p)).

Good reduction: J¹(ℚ_p) is the kernel of ρ_p on J(ℚ_p) and Jⁿ(ℚ_p) the pⁿℤ_p-points of the formal group (ED.4/abelian-logarithm); ρ_p is onto J̃_p(𝔽_p) by Hensel's lemma, and g + J¹ meets ι(C(ℚ_p)) iff ρ_p(g) ∈ ι_p(C̃_p(𝔽_p)), because every 𝔽_p-point of the smooth special fibre lifts to C(ℚ_p).
Bad and deep places: genus-two-bad-information and genus-two-deep-information supply computable supersets X′_U and generators of K_U (subgroup-from-membership-test, or the kernel of the logarithm).
acceptance: At a good prime with U = J¹ the datum agrees with the good-reduction datum of jacobian-reduction-data restricted to the image of Γ.
Γ = G = ℤ/2, φ = id, two places with X₀ = {0}, X₁ = {1}: at L = 0 (below the kernels) A_S(0) = ∅, while at L = Γ the sieve set is {0}.
Box's sieve for X₀(N): the intersection of the sets φ_p^{-1}(ι_p(M_p)) ⊆ ℤⁿ is empty iff the finite sieve at ⋂ ker φ_p is empty.

uses.how: bad information J(ℚ_p)/J¹(ℚ_p) at regular odd primes and deep information J(ℚ_p)/Jⁿ(ℚ_p) are instances, with Y computed by the Kummer and dual Kummer tests.
bad and deep information keep the sets A(L) small for ranks three and four.

nodes.title: Computing the sieve on a subgroup of index prime to N
nodes.statement: Let Γ be an abelian group, H ≤ Γ and N ≥ 1 with gcd([Γ:H], N) = 1 (native index; ED.3/finite-index-subgroup-certificate and ED.3/saturation-certificate supply H by generators with this coprimality for the primes dividing N). Then (i) H ∩ NΓ = NH; (ii) the inclusion induces a group isomorphism H/NH ≅ Γ/NΓ; (iii) for local data φ_i: Γ → G_i and finite X_i ⊆ G_i (i ∈ S) put ψ_i = (G_i → G_i/NG_i) ∘ φ_i|_H and X̄_i = the image of X_i in G_i/NG_i; for every γ ∈ Γ with φ_i(γ) ∈ X_i for all i ∈ S there is h ∈ H with h − γ ∈ NΓ, and the class of h in H/NH lies in admissibleClasses(S, NH, ψ, X̄); by (ii) this class is determined by γ. Consequently the sieve computed from the generators of H alone, with targets G_i/NG_i, contains the class of every rational point, and its emptiness proves C(ℚ) = ∅. No element of Γ outside H is used.
hypotheses: Γ abelian; H ≤ Γ; N ≥ 1; gcd([Γ:H], N) = 1 with the native index (an infinite index is represented by 0 and is then coprime only to N = 1).
S finite; φ_i: Γ → G_i additive; X_i ⊆ G_i finite; H/NH has a finite enumeration.
proofSteps: (i) NH ⊆ H ∩ NΓ. Conversely let h = Nγ ∈ H and d = [Γ:H]; Subgroup.pow_index_mem gives dγ ∈ H, Nat.gcd_eq_gcd_ab gives du + Nv = 1, so γ = u(dγ) + vh ∈ H and h ∈ NH.
(ii) Surjectivity is subgroup-covers-quotient with L = NΓ; injectivity is (i).
(iii) ψ_i(NH) = 0 in G_i/NG_i, so the test at i is exact there. If h − γ = Nγ′ then φ_i(h) − φ_i(γ) ∈ NG_i, so ψ_i(h) is the image of φ_i(γ) ∈ X_i; global-soundness for (H, ψ, X̄) gives the claim.
Testing modulo NG_i instead of φ_i(NΓ) makes the computation independent of the unknown part of Γ: φ_i(Γ) cannot be computed from H when [Γ:H] > 1.
acceptance: Γ = ℤ, H = 3ℤ, N = 2: H ∩ 2ℤ = 6ℤ = 2H and 3ℤ/6ℤ ≅ ℤ/2; with G = ℤ/6 and φ the reduction, the class of 3 is tested modulo 2G = {0, 2, 4} exactly as γ = 1.
H = 2ℤ, N = 2: the map H/2H → Γ/2Γ is zero and the odd class is lost; the coprimality hypothesis fails.

nodes.title: The sieve along a descending chain of subgroups
nodes.statement: Given places S, local data (φ_i, X_i), subgroups L_0 ≥ L_1 ≥ L_2 ≥ … of Γ with finite quotients, proposed lifts σ_j: Γ/L_j → Γ/L_{j+1} and test sets T_j ⊆ S, define siftChain by A_0 = admissibleClasses(S, L_0, φ, X) and A_{j+1} = refineClasses(T_j, L_{j+1}, L_j, σ_j, A_j). Bruin–Stoll's computation of A(NΓ) is the instance L_0 = Γ with the chain N_0Γ ⊇ N_1Γ ⊇ … ⊇ N_mΓ refined by PrepareLift into steps L_{j−1} ⊇ L_j, σ_j a choice of representatives and T_j = I_j. The value at each level is a finite set; that the chain has reached its intended final level NΓ is recorded in the certificate.
hypotheses: Γ is an abelian group, S a finite set of places, each G_i an abelian group, φ_i: Γ → G_i additive and X_i ⊆ G_i finite; L ≤ Γ has finite quotient Γ/L. Surjectivity of φ_i is not assumed.
L_{j+1} ≤ L_j for all j; every Γ/L_j has a finite enumeration; σ_j and T_j are arbitrary data, checked only in sieve-chain-correct.
proofSteps: Recursion on j using coset-lift; each step is a finite loop over A_j and the kernel of Γ/L_{j+1} → Γ/L_j.
The chain is indexed by ℕ and evaluated at a given level, so no termination question arises.
PrepareLift's choice of the L_j (prepared-step-target, prepared-step-progress) and FindQSequence's choice of the q_k affect only the cost.
acceptance: Every level is computed by finitely many finite loops; no expected-size estimate enters.
A = ℤ/4, q = 2, M = 2: v₂(4) = 2 > 1 and 4A = 0 ≠ 2A = {0, 2}; the place is relevant.
A = ℤ has exponent 0 and is excluded: 2ℤ ≠ ℤ although padicValNat 2 0 = 0.

uses.how: A(N_kΓ) is computed iteratively with PrepareLift and Lift.
the certificate's candidate set is siftChain at its final level.

nodes.title: Correctness of the iterated sieve

Then siftChain at level j equals A_S(L_j) for every j. In particular, if L_t = NΓ the computed set is A(NΓ), and if some level is empty every subsequent level is empty.

nodes.title: A finite-index subgroup from a membership test (GetSubgroup)
nodes.statement: Let Γ be an abelian group generated by b_1, …, b_r and K ≤ Γ a subgroup of finite index with decidable membership. GetSubgroup processes the generators in order, keeping a list A′ of representatives of the image of ⟨b_1, …, b_{k−1}⟩ in Γ/K: for b = b_k it finds the least j ≥ 1 such that jb + a ∈ K for some a ∈ A′, records g_k = jb + a, and replaces A′ by {a + ib : a ∈ A′, 0 ≤ i < j}. The output (g_1, …, g_r) has length r, lies in K and generates K. Bruin–Stoll apply it with Γ = J(ℚ) and K = J(ℚ) ∩ J⁰(ℚ_p), membership being Proposition 5.10's test v_p(δ(κ(P))) = 4v_p(κ(P)). The source states it for a free group; the argument below needs only a generating list.
hypotheses: Γ abelian, generated by the list b; K ≤ Γ of finite index; membership in K decidable.
proofSteps: Termination: [Γ:K]·b ∈ K (pow_index_mem), so the least j is at most [Γ:K].
Invariant: A′ is a set of distinct representatives of (K + ⟨b_1, …, b_k⟩)/K; minimality of j makes the cosets a + ib distinct.

Generation: by induction on k, K ∩ ⟨b_1, …, b_k⟩ = ⟨g_1, …, g_k⟩. For x = c·b_k + y ∈ K with y ∈ ⟨b_1, …, b_{k−1}⟩, the integers c with c·b_k ∈ K + ⟨b_1, …, b_{k−1}⟩ form jℤ, so j | c and x − (c/j)·g_k ∈ K ∩ ⟨b_1, …, b_{k−1}⟩.
With ⟨b_1, …, b_r⟩ = Γ this gives ⟨g_1, …, g_r⟩ = K (Subgroup.closure_le for one inclusion).
acceptance: The output generates K whenever the input generates Γ, with torsion allowed.

nodes.title: Each coset of NΓ has at most one point of small height
nodes.statement: Let Γ be an abelian group and ĥ: Γ → ℝ a quadratic map over ℤ (ĥ(nx) = n²ĥ(x), ĥ(x+y) + ĥ(x−y) = 2ĥ(x) + 2ĥ(y)) with ĥ ≥ 0. Let m be such that ĥ(x) ≥ m for every x of infinite order, let N ≥ 1 kill the torsion of Γ (N·x = 0 for every x of finite order; in Bruin–Stoll the exponent of J(ℚ)_tors divides N), and let H′ satisfy N²m > 4H′. If x, y ∈ Γ satisfy x − y ∈ NΓ and ĥ(x), ĥ(y) ≤ H′, then x = y. For Γ = J(ℚ) the Néron–Tate height is such a map and m is the minimal canonical height of a point of infinite order (certified by a short-vector enumeration).
hypotheses: ĥ a quadratic map Γ → ℝ over ℤ with ĥ ≥ 0.
m ≤ ĥ(x) for all x of infinite order; N·x = 0 for all x of finite order; 4H′ < N²m.
proofSteps: Write x − y = Nz. The parallelogram law and ĥ(x + y) ≥ 0 give ĥ(x − y) ≤ 2ĥ(x) + 2ĥ(y) ≤ 4H′.
If z has infinite order then ĥ(x − y) = N²ĥ(z) ≥ N²m > 4H′ (QuadraticMap.map_smul), a contradiction.
So z has finite order and x − y = Nz = 0.

For elliptic curves Tau Ceti's canonical height is a quadratic map with ĥ ≥ 0 vanishing exactly on torsion, so the hypotheses are met with any certified m; for Jacobians the Néron–Tate height is requested from RP.0.
acceptance: Γ = ℤ, ĥ(x) = x², m = 1, N = 3, H′ = 2: 9 > 8, and the coset 1 + 3ℤ contains only 1 with x² ≤ 2.
Γ = ℤ/2 × ℤ, ĥ(a, x) = x², m = 1, N = 1, H′ = 0.1: (1, 0) and (0, 0) both have height 0 and differ by an element of NΓ; the torsion condition N·(1, 0) = 0 fails.

nodes.title: All points of bounded height from the sieve
nodes.statement: Let D be jacobian reduction data (P = C(ℚ), Γ = J(ℚ)), ĥ a quadratic map on Γ as in height-coset-separation, h a height on C(ℚ) with ĥ(ι(P)) ≤ d·h(P) + δ for all P (d ≥ 0), H a bound and H′ = dH + δ. Let L ≤ Γ have finite index, S places whose local sets contain the true local images, and for every a ∈ A_S(L) let T_a ⊆ Γ be a finite set containing every x ∈ Γ with q_L(x) = a and ĥ(x) ≤ H′ (certified by a closest-vector enumeration in the lattice (L, ĥ) around a representative, ED.1/short-vector-enumeration-complete). Then every P ∈ C(ℚ) with h(P) ≤ H has ι(P) ∈ T_a for some a ∈ A_S(L). If moreover L ⊆ NΓ with N as in height-coset-separation, each T_a contains at most one element of height at most H′, so the points of height at most H inject into A_S(L); a candidate x ∈ T_a is accepted by exhibiting a preimage under ι, or rejected by a reduction test (kummer-curve-test in genus two).
hypotheses: D jacobian reduction data with local sets containing the true images; L ≤ Γ of finite index.
ĥ quadratic over ℤ; ĥ(ι(P)) ≤ d·h(P) + δ for all P with d ≥ 0; T_a contains every element of the class a of height at most dH + δ.
proofSteps: curve-sieve-soundness puts q_L(ι(P)) in A_S(L).
ĥ(ι(P)) ≤ d·h(P) + δ ≤ dH + δ = H′ because d ≥ 0, so ι(P) ∈ T_{q_L(ι(P))}.
height-coset-separation bounds the number of elements of height at most H′ in each class by one when L ⊆ NΓ.

The constants d and δ come from a height-difference bound (ED.3/explicit-height-difference-bound) and the explicit embedding; their certification for genus-two Jacobians is the recorded height-comparison gap, and the canonical height of J(ℚ) is requested from RP.0.
acceptance: If A_S(L) = ∅ there is no rational point of height at most H.
With N divisible by the exponent of J(ℚ)_tors and N² > 4H′/m, each element of A(S, N) corresponds to at most one point of height at most H (Bruin–Stoll §4.2).

nodes.title: Recognising points of a genus-two curve by reduction
nodes.statement: Let C: y² = F(x, z) be a genus-two curve over ℚ with integral binary sextic F, P₀ ∈ C(ℚ) with x(P₀) = (a : b) for coprime integers a, b, and ι(P) = [P − P₀]. For Q ∈ J(ℚ) let (k₁ : k₂ : k₃ : k₄) be its image on the Kummer surface with coprime integer coordinates and h(Q) = log max|k_j|; let γ ≥ h − ĥ on J(ℚ). Let p₁, …, p_m be distinct primes of good reduction with p₁⋯p_m > 3·e^{H′+γ}·max(|a|, |b|)², and, if P₀ ≠ P̄₀, such that the product of those p_j modulo which P₀ and its hyperelliptic conjugate P̄₀ remain distinct exceeds e^{H′+γ} (for instance, every p_j separates them). If Q ∈ J(ℚ) has ĥ(Q) ≤ H′ and the reduction of Q modulo every p_j lies in ι_{p_j}(C̃(𝔽_{p_j})), then Q ∈ ι(C(ℚ)). The factor 3 corrects the printed bound (source issue EffectiveDiophantineMethods/E12). The arithmetic core: if |k_j| ≤ B, every p_j divides k₁a² − k₂ab + k₃b², and ∏ p_j > 3B·max(|a|, |b|)², then k₁a² − k₂ab + k₃b² = 0.
hypotheses: C of genus two with integral sextic model; P₀ rational with x(P₀) = (a : b), gcd(a, b) = 1; ι(P) = [P − P₀].
γ ≥ h − ĥ on J(ℚ); distinct good primes with p₁⋯p_m > 3e^{H′+γ}max(|a|,|b|)²; if P₀ ≠ P̄₀, the p_j separating P₀ and P̄₀ have product > e^{H′+γ}.
The prime condition on the separating primes corrects the gap EffectiveDiophantineMethods/E17 in the published proof.
proofSteps: The quadratic k₁X² − k₂XZ + k₃Z² vanishes at the x-coordinates of the degree-two divisor representing Q (Kummer coordinates (1 : x₁+x₂ : x₁x₂ : β₀), gap on the Cassels–Flynn model). If Q mod p_j = ι_{p_j}(R) = [R − (P₀ mod p_j)] = [R + P₀′ − W], with P₀′ the hyperelliptic conjugate and W a canonical divisor, then the degree-two divisor of Q mod p_j contains a point with x-coordinate x(P₀) mod p_j, so p_j divides k₁a² − k₂ab + k₃b² (the printed proof writes k₁b² − k₂ab + k₃a², source issue EffectiveDiophantineMethods/E13).

|k_j| ≤ e^{h(Q)} ≤ e^{ĥ(Q)+γ} ≤ e^{H′+γ}, so |k₁a² − k₂ab + k₃b²| ≤ (|k₁| + |k₂| + |k₃|)·max(|a|,|b|)² ≤ 3e^{H′+γ}max(|a|,|b|)²; the product of the distinct p_j divides this integer, which therefore vanishes (kummerLineValue_eq_zero).

Vanishing means the divisor of Q contains a point with x-coordinate x(P₀), so Q = [P − P₀] or Q = [P − P̄₀] with P ∈ C(ℚ). In the second case with P ≠ P̄₀ (so P₀ ≠ P̄₀ and Q ≠ 0): at a prime p_j separating P₀ and P̄₀, Q mod p_j = [P̃ + P̃₀ − W] equals some ι_{p_j}(R) = [R + P̄̃₀ − W] only if P̃ = P̄̃₀, because an effective degree-two divisor outside the canonical class is the only effective divisor in its class; then Q ≡ 0 modulo p_j, so p_j divides k₁, k₂, k₃, which are not all zero, and the product of the separating primes is at most max|k_j| ≤ e^{H′+γ}, a contradiction. (The printed proof distinguishes the cases at a single p_{j₀}, which fails when P ≡ P̄₀ modulo p_{j₀}.)
γ is the genus-two height-difference bound (height-comparison gap; ED.3/explicit-height-difference-bound covers elliptic curves).
acceptance: Arithmetic core: a = b = 1, |k_j| ≤ 10, primes {2, 3, 5, 7}: an integer divisible by 210 with absolute value at most 30 is zero.
The printed estimate fails for (k₁, k₂, k₃) = (1, −1, 1) and a = b = 1: the value is 3 while max|k_j|·max(|a|,|b|)² = 1.

nodes.title: Refining the subgroup represented by known points (Siksek's step)
nodes.statement: Let j: P → Γ be a map (P = C(ℚ) or the integral points, j = ι), W ⊆ Γ finite and L ≤ Γ such that W represents the image of P in Γ/L: every j(p) lies in W + L. Let φ: Γ → A be a homomorphism with φ(j(p)) ∈ Y for all p (for a good prime q: φ = ρ_q and Y = ι_q(C̃(𝔽_q))), L′ = L ∩ ker φ, and R ⊆ Γ a set meeting every nontrivial coset of L′ in L (every ℓ ∈ L∖L′ is congruent modulo L′ to some r ∈ R). If φ(w + r) ∉ Y for all w ∈ W and r ∈ R, then W represents the image of P in Γ/L′: every j(p) lies in W + L′. Only the values φ(w + r) are needed, not a discrete logarithm of the local image.
hypotheses: j: P → Γ; W ⊆ Γ finite; every j(p) ∈ W + L.
φ: Γ → A with φ(j(p)) ∈ Y; R meets every nontrivial coset of L ∩ ker φ in L; φ(w + r) ∉ Y for w ∈ W, r ∈ R.
proofSteps: Write j(p) = w + ℓ with ℓ ∈ L. If ℓ ∉ L′ choose r ∈ R and ℓ′ ∈ L′ with ℓ = r + ℓ′; then φ(j(p)) = φ(w + r) since φ(ℓ′) = 0, so φ(w + r) ∈ Y, contradicting the test.
Hence ℓ ∈ L′.
Iterating over primes q gives a decreasing chain of subgroups with the same invariant; (L : L′) is computed from ρ_q on generators.
acceptance: If φ(w + r) ∈ Y for some pair the step gives no conclusion.

nodes.title: Integral points on hyperelliptic curves from a sieve lower bound
nodes.statement: Let f ∈ ℤ[x] be separable of degree n ≥ 5, C the smooth projective curve of genus g = ⌊(n−1)/2⌋ with affine model y² = f(x) (AlgebraicCurves Layer 10), 𝓘 = {(x, y) ∈ ℤ² : y² = f(x)} ⊆ C(ℚ), and ι: C(ℚ) → J(ℚ) from jacobian-reduction-data (for n odd, D₁ = ∞, the unique point at infinity). The covering map is the inclusion of the integral points of the affine Weierstrass model into C(ℚ), followed by ι. Let W ⊆ 𝓘 be finite and L ≤ J(ℚ) such that (i) ι(P) ∈ ι(W) + L for all P ∈ 𝓘 (from curve-sieve-soundness with known representatives and siksek-lattice-step); (ii) μ > 0 with ĥ(ℓ) ≥ μ for every nonzero ℓ ∈ L (a short-vector certificate in (L, ĥ)); (iii) ĥ(ι(P)) ≤ d·log max(1, |x(P)|) + δ on 𝓘 with d ≥ 0; (iv) log max(1, |x|) ≤ B for all (x, y) ∈ 𝓘, supplied by DT.4/baker-superelliptic-theorem with n = 2 and b = 1, B = (4N)^{2^{12}N⁴}·e^{50N⁴h(f)} for N = deg f and h(f) = log max(1, |coefficients of f|), or by any certified sharper bound. Put w* = max_{w∈W} ĥ(ι(w)). If √w* < √μ and dB + δ < (√μ − √w*)², then 𝓘 = W.
hypotheses: f separable, deg f ≥ 5; 𝓘 the integral points of y² = f(x); ι injective (genus ≥ 1).
(i)–(iv) as stated, each certified: the sieve and Siksek steps for (i), short vectors for (ii), the height comparison for (iii), the DT.4 bound for (iv).
proofSteps: Let P ∈ 𝓘∖W. By (i) ι(P) − ι(w) ∈ L for some w ∈ W; it is nonzero because ι is injective, so ĥ(ι(P) − ι(w)) ≥ μ by (ii).

√ĥ is a seminorm: ĥ(sx + ty) ≥ 0 for all integers s, t, hence for all reals by homogeneity and continuity, which is the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality for the polar form. So √ĥ(ι(P)) ≥ √μ − √ĥ(ι(w)) ≥ √μ − √w* > 0.
Squaring, ĥ(ι(P)) ≥ (√μ − √w*)² > dB + δ ≥ d·log max(1, |x(P)|) + δ ≥ ĥ(ι(P)), a contradiction.
The upper bound is stated for the equation itself, so no descent covering is needed; the constants d, δ for the Kummer height of [P − ∞] are the recorded height-comparison gap.
acceptance: Toy instance: Γ = ℤ, ĥ(x) = x², L = 10ℤ, μ = 100, w* = 4, d = 1, δ = 0, B = 30: (10 − 2)² = 64 > 30, so every point is known.

The bounds must actually cross: Bruin–Stoll report N near 10^100 from the sieve and subgroups of index up to 10^1800 from the second stage, against Baker-type bounds near 10^600; an uncrossed pair of bounds gives no conclusion.

nodes.title: Combination of Chabauty–Coleman with the Mordell–Weil sieve
nodes.statement: Let D be jacobian reduction data for a curve C/ℚ of genus g ≥ 2 whose Jacobian has rank r < g, and p₀ ∈ S a prime of good reduction with p₀ ≥ 3 and a nonzero ω ∈ Ann_{p₀}(J(ℚ)) (ED.4/annihilating-differentials), scaled to be integral with nonzero reduction ω̄. Let Ū ⊆ C̃(𝔽_{p₀}) be the residue classes R for which ED.4/residue-disc-zero-bound gives at most one rational point reducing to R (for instance those with ω̄(R) ≠ 0). Let L ≤ J(ℚ) have finite index with L ⊆ ker ρ_{p₀} (for instance L ⊆ NJ(ℚ) with the exponent of J̃(𝔽_{p₀}) dividing N). Then: (i) if ι(P) − ι(P′) ∈ L then red_{p₀}(P) = red_{p₀}(P′); (ii) P ↦ q_L(ι(P)) is injective on {P ∈ C(ℚ) : red_{p₀}(P) ∈ Ū}; (iii) (residue-class decision) if the sieve with the local set ι_{p₀}(C̃(𝔽_{p₀})∖Ū) at p₀ and the full local images elsewhere is empty, every rational point reduces into Ū; the residue classes outside Ū may instead be settled one at a time by valid ED.4/residue-disc-verdicts, whose lists Z_rat are the rational points of those classes; (iv) if W ⊆ C(ℚ) is a finite set of known points containing every rational point that reduces outside Ū (for instance there is none, by (iii)) and every class of A_S(L) equals q_L(ι(w)) for some w ∈ W, then C(ℚ) = W. While some class of A_S(L) is not represented by W, the computation is open: enlarging S or refining L continues it, and no conclusion about C(ℚ) is drawn.
hypotheses: C/ℚ of genus g ≥ 2, rank r < g; D jacobian reduction data; p₀ ∈ S good, p₀ ≥ 3, with ω ∈ Ann_{p₀}(J(ℚ)) integral with nonzero reduction (ED.4/annihilating-differentials).
Ū ⊆ C̃(𝔽_{p₀}) certified by ED.4/residue-disc-zero-bound; L of finite index with L ⊆ ker ρ_{p₀}.
proofSteps: (i) ρ_{p₀}(ι(P) − ι(P′)) = 0 since L ⊆ ker ρ_{p₀}; the square gives ι_{p₀}(red P) = ι_{p₀}(red P′), and ι_{p₀} is injective because the Abel–Jacobi map of a curve of genus at least one is a closed immersion (JacobianChallenge Layer F).
(ii) Two points with the same class share a residue class in Ū, which contains at most one rational point.
(iii) certified-map-obstruction applied to the points reducing outside Ū, with the smaller local set at p₀.

(iv) For P reducing into Ū, curve-sieve-soundness puts q_L(ι(P)) in A_S(L), so q_L(ι(P)) = q_L(ι(w)) for some w ∈ W; by (i) w reduces to the same class of Ū, and by (ii) P = w (known-points-completeness on the points reducing into Ū). Points reducing outside Ū lie in W by hypothesis.
If L ⊆ NJ(ℚ) and the exponent of J̃(𝔽_{p₀}) divides N then ρ_{p₀}(L) ⊆ N·J̃(𝔽_{p₀}) = 0.

Without L ⊆ ker ρ_{p₀}, two rational points in different residue classes can share a class modulo a coarse L, injectivity fails and the known points need not be all points.

nodes.title: The relative symmetric Mordell–Weil sieve
nodes.statement: Let X/ℚ be a smooth projective non-hyperelliptic curve of genus g ≥ 3 with Jacobian J (the setting of ED.4/relative-symmetric-chabauty and Box §2), possibly with a degree-two map π: X → C to a smooth curve C/ℚ, and X^(2) its symmetric square. Input: primes p₁, …, p_r of good reduction for X (and for C, with π extending to the models); divisors D₁, …, D_n generating a subgroup G ≤ J(ℚ) of finite index; an integer I ≥ 1 with I·J(ℚ) ⊆ G; a finite set L ⊆ X^(2)(ℚ) containing a rational degree-two divisor ∞; and for each i a subset L_i^good ⊆ L of known points to which ED.4/relative-symmetric-chabauty applies at p_i (Box Theorem 2.1: the point is the only point of X^(2)(ℚ) in its residue class; or Box Theorem 2.4 for x = π*(P): every point of its residue class comes from C(ℚ)). Put ι(x) = I·([x] − ∞) ∈ G and ι_p(R) = I·([R] − ∞̃) on X̃^(2)(𝔽_p), so that red_p(ι(x)) = ι_p(red_p(x)) (jacobian-reduction-data for degree-two divisors), and M_i^bad = ι_{p_i}^{-1}(red_{p_i}(G)) ∖ red_{p_i}(L_i^good). If no g ∈ G satisfies red_{p_i}(g) ∈ ι_{p_i}(M_i^bad) for every i, then X^(2)(ℚ) = L ∪ π*C(ℚ) (= L when there is no π). The hypothesis is decided finitely: for L₀ = ⋂_i ker(red_{p_i}|_G), of finite index, it holds iff admissibleClasses(S, L₀, red, ι(M^bad)) = ∅ (kernel-level-exactness). This is Caraiani–Newton Theorem 7.4.2 = Box Theorem 2.6.
hypotheses: X smooth projective non-hyperelliptic of genus g ≥ 3 over ℚ; π: X → C of degree two when present; the p_i of good reduction for X and C with π extending. Without π, L_i^good is defined by ED.4/symmetric-chabauty alone.
G ≤ J(ℚ) generated by D₁, …, D_n with I·J(ℚ) ⊆ G; ∞ ∈ L ⊆ X^(2)(ℚ) finite; L_i^good certified by ED.4/relative-symmetric-chabauty at p_i.
proofSteps: Caraiani–Newton Proposition 7.4.1 (from ED.4/relative-symmetric-chabauty): if red_{p_i}(x) ∈ red_{p_i}(L_i^good) for some i then x ∈ L ∪ π*C(ℚ).

Let x ∉ L ∪ π*C(ℚ). For every i, R = red_{p_i}(x) ∉ red_{p_i}(L_i^good) and ι_{p_i}(R) = red_{p_i}(ι(x)) ∈ red_{p_i}(G), so R ∈ M_i^bad and g = ι(x) ∈ G satisfies all conditions, a contradiction (certified-map-obstruction).

Finite form: kernel-level-exactness for Γ = G, φ_i = red_{p_i}|_G, X_i = ι_{p_i}(M_i^bad); G/L₀ embeds in ∏ J̃(𝔽_{p_i}). Box intersects cosets in ℤⁿ through φ: ℤⁿ → G; the formulations agree because φ is onto G.
ι need not be injective (multiplication by I kills torsion); only ι(x) ∈ G is used. ED.3/finite-index-subgroup-certificate supplies G and the bound I.
acceptance: Caraiani–Newton Proposition 7.4.5(2): for X = X(s3, ns5) and C = X(ns3, ns5) the sieve with G = ⟨5G₂, Jac_{C₂}(ℚ)[2]⟩ with G₂ = ⟨π₂*D⟩ (printed ⟨5G₁, …⟩), I = 10 and the primes listed in its proof determines the quadratic points not coming from C(ℚ).

nodes.title: Reduction at bad primes for genus-two curves
nodes.statement: Let O be a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformiser π, residue field k with char k ≠ 2 and fraction field L, F ∈ O[X, Z] a squarefree binary sextic, C_F: Y² = F(X, Z) in weighted projective space, J_F ⊆ ℙ¹⁵ the Cassels–Flynn model of its Jacobian, J_F¹(L) = {P : P̄ = O} its kernel of reduction for this model, and J_{F̄}^0 the component of the smooth locus of the special fibre containing the origin. (a) (Theorem 5.11) J_{F̄}^0 is a commutative algebraic group whose law on Mumford pairs (A, B) is Cantor composition and reduction, except when both A vanish at the same singular point x = 0, where φ(X², λXZ²) + φ(X², μXZ²) = φ(X², ((f₂ + λμ)/(λ + μ))XZ²) and the sum is zero if λ + μ = 0. (b) (Proposition 5.10) P ∈ J_F lies in J_F^0 iff δ(κ(P)) ≠ 0. (c) (Corollaries 5.14–5.15) If C_F/O is regular and F̄ is not a square, then 0 → J_F¹(L) → J_F(L) → J_{F̄}^0(k) → 0 is exact, the map reducing the Mumford representation. For an odd prime p at which the given model is regular with one-component special fibre this computes the local datum of padic-quotient-sieve-datum with U = J¹(ℚ_p) as at good primes; at an odd prime where the model is not regular or the special fibre has several components, J(ℚ) ∩ J⁰(ℚ_p) is computed by subgroup-from-membership-test with the test v_p(δ(κ(P))) = 4v_p(κ(P)), and the image of C(ℚ_p) modulo J¹(ℚ_p) by the dual Kummer test of genus-two-deep-information with n = 1. Remark 5.16 (the regular model minus singular points is the Néron model) is stated without proof in the source and is not used.
hypotheses: O complete DVR, char k ≠ 2; F squarefree of degree six over O; for (c) the model C_F/O is regular and F̄ is not a square.
proofSteps: Lift F̄ to a squarefree F̃ over O; for P with P̄ ∈ J^0 and Q in the kernel of reduction the biquadratic forms give κ(P ± Q) = κ(P̄), so P + Q reduces to P̄; hence the kernel is a subgroup acting on the points with smooth origin-component reduction, the quotient is J_{F̄}^0(k), and the group law is inherited; Cantor's algorithm commutes with reduction outside the special case, which follows by a limit argument (Theorem 5.11).
Proposition 5.5 describes the singular points through (A, B) ∈ D_F, Lemma 5.7 the components, and Proposition 5.10 identifies J^0 by δ(κ(P)) ≠ 0.
Lemma 5.13 and Corollary 5.14: under regularity, points outside the kernel reduce to smooth points of the origin component; surjectivity of reduction is Hensel's lemma (Corollary 5.15).
The explicit model facts (the 72 quadrics, the Kummer surface, δ, the biquadratic forms, D_F) are the Cassels–Flynn gap; regular models are StableReduction Layer 5.
acceptance: Remark 5.12: for k = 𝔽_q with q odd, #J_F^0(𝔽_q) depends only on the factorisation pattern of F (Figure 1).
F = H² a nonzero square: J_F has three components, the two not containing the origin are principal homogeneous spaces under J_F^0, and the exact sequence (c) is not claimed.

nodes.title: Deep information for genus-two curves
nodes.statement: Let C be a genus-two curve over ℚ with a Weierstrass model over ℤ_p, p odd, ι: C → J from a rational degree-one class, Jⁿ(ℚ_p) the pⁿℤ_p-points of the formal group (n ≥ 1) and log: J¹(ℚ_p) → (pℤ_p)² the formal logarithm. (a) For Γ = J(ℚ) and K_n = Γ ∩ Jⁿ(ℚ_p), K_n is the kernel of K₁ → (pℤ_p/pⁿℤ_p)² ≅ (ℤ/p^{n−1})², P ↦ log P mod pⁿ; so Γ/K_n is finite and computable from K₁ and logarithms to precision pⁿ. (b) (Lemma 6.2) If P₀ ∈ C(ℚ_p), Q ∈ Jⁿ(ℚ_p) and (η₁ : η₂ : η₃ : η₄) are coordinates of the image of P₀ + Q ∈ Pic¹ on the dual Kummer surface, normalised to minimal valuation zero, then v_p(η₁η₃ − η₂²) ≥ n and v_p(η₄) ≥ 2n. Hence the set Y_n of classes c ∈ Γ/K_n whose chosen representative g, translated to Pic¹ by g↦g+D₁ and to the dual Kummer surface, satisfies v_p(η₄) ≥ 2n and v_p(η₁η₃ − η₂²) ≥ n, contains every class whose coset meets ι(C(ℚ_p)); it is a certified superset for padic-quotient-sieve-datum with U = Jⁿ(ℚ_p). The necessary dual-Kummer congruences supply a superset only; actual membership in the curve embedded in Pic¹ must be checked separately. Translation Pic⁰→Pic¹ is defined on the whole Jacobian, unlike an inverse of the curve embedding.
hypotheses: p odd; Weierstrass model of C over ℤ_p; n ≥ 1; ι from a rational degree-one class.
proofSteps: (a) For p odd the formal logarithm is an isomorphism J¹(ℚ_p) → (pℤ_p)² carrying Jⁿ onto (pⁿℤ_p)² (ED.4/abelian-logarithm); K_n is the preimage of (pⁿℤ_p)² in K₁.

(b) After a ℤ_p-coordinate change moving P₀ to infinity, P₀ = (1 : 0 : 0 : 0) on the dual Kummer surface and Q has Kummer coordinates (αp^{2n} : βp^{2n} : γp^{2n} : 1); the biquadratic forms A (Lemma 6.1) give η₁η₁′ ≡ 1 and η₄ + η₄′ ≡ 0 modulo p^{2n}, η₄η₄′ ≡ 0 modulo p^{4n} and η₂, η₃ ≡ 0 modulo pⁿ, whence the valuations.

If a class c meets ι(C(ℚ_p)) then every representative g has translation D↦D+D₁(g) = P₀ + Q with P₀ ∈ C(ℚ_p) and Q ∈ Jⁿ(ℚ_p), so the chosen representative passes the test and c ∈ Y_n; local-overapproximations and curve-sieve-soundness apply.

The incremental computation over n = 2, 3, … and the linear forms ℓ_m reduce cost only; a verifier re-evaluates the test on the recorded representatives. The Kummer and dual Kummer surfaces and the forms A, B are the Cassels–Flynn gap.
acceptance: Bruin–Stoll §7: information modulo p^m is collected in the order 2, 3, 5, 7, 2², 11, 13, 17, 19, 23, 3², …; §8: deep information for all pⁿ < 520 shortens the hardest rank-four computation.
The test is one-sided: a class passing it need not meet the curve, and it is used only as a superset.

nodes.title: Mordell–Weil sieve certificate
nodes.statement: A Mordell–Weil sieve certificate for a curve C/ℚ consists of: (1) jacobian reduction data — the curve, a rational degree-one divisor D₁, the places S with their local groups G_p, the values of the local maps on generators, and finite local sets certified to contain the true local images (good data, or bad and deep data from padic-quotient-sieve-datum); (2) the Mordell–Weil input — generators of a subgroup H ≤ J(ℚ) with ED.3 certificates of rank and torsion and of index prime to every prime dividing the modulus N (finite-index-subgroup-certificate, saturation-certificate), or a full Mordell–Weil basis certificate; the rank is labelled conditional when its upper bound rests on an analytic hypothesis; (3) the modulus N, its factorisation and the descending chain L_0 ⊇ … ⊇ L_t with lifts σ_j and test sets T_j; (4) the exhaustive candidate set, siftChain at level t; (5) the known points W and the mode of conclusion: emptiness, Chabauty (a prime p₀ with an annihilating differential and certified residue classes Ū as in chabauty-sieve-combination, L_t ⊆ ker ρ_{p₀}, and every candidate the class of a known point), or height (a bound H, separation data and short-vector certificates). The certificate is checked when every σ_j with j<t is a section on the sieve set at level j, T_j ⊆ S, and every place outside T_j has an unchanged image subgroup. A record whose candidate set is nonempty and not covered by known points certifies nothing about C(ℚ): it is an open computation, not an empty solution set. Checked quantifies only j<length. On invariant-factor presentations, replay each projection and every local table; RawSieveStep.check verifies all new classes, including every lift, by the equivalence next(b) ↔ old(project b) ∧ all-local-tests(b). Chain compatibility and the initial full candidate set are checked separately at the finitely many recorded levels.
hypotheses: The Lean structure records the reduction data, places, chain, lifts, test sets and known points over the global group Γ (J(ℚ), or H transported by coprime-index-transfer); the ED.3 and ED.4 certificates and the height data are inputs of the soundness theorem.
proofSteps: Bundle the data; candidates is siftChain at the final level.
Checked is the conjunction of the three finite checks of sieve-chain-correct.
Presentations of the finite groups and maps used to evaluate the checks are the recorded gap on certified finite presentations.
acceptance: The certificate carries the index/saturation assumptions, the primes, the local images and the exhaustive candidate set.

uses.how: the final certificate includes the index/saturation assumptions, primes, images and exhaustive candidate set.
the stopping criterion, the Chabauty procedure and the implementation inputs are its three modes and its data.
worked examples instantiate it inside the CN.5 certificate schemas.

nodes.title: Soundness of a Mordell–Weil sieve certificate
nodes.statement: Let c be a checked sieve certificate for C/ℚ whose global group is J(ℚ), or a subgroup H of index prime to N transported by coprime-index-transfer. (a) If its candidate set is empty, C(ℚ) = ∅. (b) Chabauty mode: if p₀ carries an annihilating differential (ED.4/annihilating-differentials) with every rational point reducing into its certified residue classes Ū (chabauty-sieve-combination), L_t ⊆ ker ρ_{p₀}, and every candidate is the class of a known point, then C(ℚ) = W. (c) Height mode: every P ∈ C(ℚ) with h(P) ≤ H is among the candidates of height-bounded-points, at most one per candidate class when L_t ⊆ NΓ. Each conclusion depends on the recorded assumptions — the ED.3 index and saturation certificates (and the rank, conditional when its upper bound rests on an analytic hypothesis), the primes and local images, and the chain. A certificate whose final candidate set is nonempty and not covered proves nothing about C(ℚ).
hypotheses: c checked; the ED.3 certificates for the global group hold; for (b) the ED.4 data at p₀; for (c) the height data of height-bounded-points.
proofSteps: sieve-chain-correct identifies the candidates with A_S(L_t).
(a) curve-sieve-soundness, through coprime-index-transfer when the global group is H.
(b) chabauty-sieve-combination (iv).
(c) height-bounded-points.
Conditionality: the rank enters only through the certificate of H; ED.3/rank-upper-bound distinguishes algebraic from analytic upper bounds, and the conclusion carries the label.
acceptance: Bruin–Stoll §3.3: A(N_kΓ) = ∅ for some k proves C(ℚ) = ∅.
Bruin–Stoll §4.4: genus-two curves of rank one with a known rational base point, where the procedure terminated in all examples tried.
The ℤ/2 non-example of sieve-certificate: a nonempty candidate set with no points gives no conclusion.

sources.excerpt: However, the procedure itself is correct: if it terminates, and it has done so in all the examples we tried, then it gives the exact set of rational points on the curve.
