nodes.title: Non-existence of points on the undecided small genus-two curves
nodes.statement: Among the genus-two curves y² = f(x) with f of degree five or six and coefficients in {−3, …, 3}, the 1492 isomorphism classes left undecided after a search for rational points, a check for local points and a 2-cover descent have no rational point. For Jacobians of rank at most two the proof used good information only, for ranks three and four also bad and deep information; for some curves the rank of J(ℚ) is used under the Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture, and those cases are conditional. Each of the 1447 curves that needed a sieve computation (§8, p.301) is an instance of sieve-certificate-sound (a) with an emptiness certificate; the other 45 had rank zero or were ruled out directly by information from the Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture, and the latter are conditional.
hypotheses: The curves, Mordell–Weil generators, ranks and local data of Bruin–Stoll's experiment (gap); the BSD-conditional cases are labelled.
proofSteps: For each curve: ED.3 certificates for generators and rank (conditional where BSD is used), local data at good, bad and deep places, a chain and an empty candidate set, verified by sieve-certificate-sound.
The individual certificates are reproduced as worked examples in ED.6.
acceptance: Bruin–Stoll §8: of the 1447 curves that needed a sieve, 521 have rank one (514 decided while collecting local information), 772 rank two, 152 rank three and two rank four.
The statement is recorded as conditional on BSD for the curves whose rank was not proved.

nodes.title: Certified solution sets with completeness labels
nodes.statement: Let α be a type of candidate solutions (integer tuples, S-unit triples, points with rational coordinates), P : α → Prop the Diophantine condition, and H : Prop the conjunction of the unresolved or conditional inputs of the method (H = True for an unconditional certificate). A certified solution set CertifiedSolutionSet H P consists of a finite set S : Finset α together with (sound) every element of S satisfies P, proved unconditionally by exact evaluation, and (complete) H implies that every x with P x lies in S. The certificate is labelled unconditional when H is True and conditional on H otherwise; a conditional certificate keeps H as an explicit parameter, so that discharging or weakening H is a theorem about the certificate and never an edit of it. This is the ED.6 instance of the ComputationalNumberTheory CN.5 schema for explicit examples: the pinned exact inputs are S and the certificate data of the method that proves completeness, and the verification relation is the pair (sound, complete). A list of verified solutions without completeness, a CAS output, or a p-adic candidate list that has not been compared with global points is not a certificate.
hypotheses: α is a type, P : α → Prop and H : Prop.
Elements of S are exact objects (integers, rationals, points with rational coordinates); no floating-point value is an element of S.
Completeness may depend on H only; soundness never depends on H.
proofSteps: Define the structure with three fields: a finite set of solutions, soundness (every listed element satisfies P) and completeness (under H every x with P x is listed).

The completeness label is read off from H: H = True is unconditional; any other H is displayed in the theorem that produces the certificate (for example the Generalised Riemann Hypothesis in the descent route of BDMTV 2019 Remark 6.3).
CN.5 supplies the pinned-input record (input data, arithmetic conventions, verification cost); the mathematical content is the structure above, with no new carrier for numbers or points.
acceptance: For x² = 4 over ℤ the unconditional certificate has solutions {−2, 2}.
The Thue equation X⁴ − 12X²Y² − 8XY³ + 4Y⁴ = 1 has the unconditional certificate with eight solutions (thue-example-tdw89).

nodes.title: Comparison of p-adic candidates with global solutions
nodes.statement: Let X be a set (the p-adic points X(Q_p) of a curve, or Z_p^k for an equation in k unknowns), R ⊆ X the set of global solutions (X(Q), or the integral solutions), and Z ⊆ X a set with R ⊆ Z (the common zero set of the certified p-adic functions: quadratic Chabauty determinants, annihilating Coleman integrals, or local residue conditions). Let B_1, …, B_m ⊆ X be finitely many sets (balls of radius p^(−n) around candidates computed to absolute precision n through ED.0 p-adic embeddings) with (i) Z ⊆ B_1 ∪ … ∪ B_m and (ii) Z ∩ B_i has at most one element for each i (certified simple-root isolation). Let L ⊆ R be a finite set of verified global solutions. Call B_i matched if it contains an element of L, and excluded if R ∩ B_i = ∅ is certified (by a Mordell–Weil sieve, a second independent function whose zeros avoid B_i, or a local obstruction). If every B_i is matched or excluded then R = L, and L is a certified solution set. Without such a decision for some ball the conclusion is only L ⊆ R ⊆ L ∪ ⋃_{B_i undecided} (Z ∩ B_i), and the computation is open.
hypotheses: Each Z ∩ B_i is a subsingleton.
L is finite and L ⊆ R (each element verified exactly).
Every B_i is matched (L ∩ B_i ≠ ∅) or excluded (R ∩ B_i = ∅).
proofSteps: Let x ∈ R. Then x ∈ Z, so x ∈ B_i for some i by (i).
If B_i is excluded, x ∈ R ∩ B_i = ∅ is impossible.
If B_i is matched by P ∈ L, then P ∈ R ⊆ Z, so x and P both lie in Z ∩ B_i, a subsingleton by (ii); hence x = P ∈ L.
Together with L ⊆ R this gives R = L; package L with these proofs as an unconditional certified-solution-set.

Uniqueness (ii) is indispensable: agreement of a p-adic candidate with a known point to precision n does not prove equality, because numerical agreement never proves an algebraic identity (ED.0 acceptance).
acceptance: X_s(13) at p = 17: twenty residue discs; on each, the balls of xs13-first-chart-points, xs13-second-chart-points and xs13-p0-disc are matched by P0, …, P6 and all other balls are excluded by the second Tate class; the conclusion is xs13-rational-points.
Necessity of (ii): Z = {0, p^n} ⊆ Z_p, one ball B = p^n Z_p and L = {0}; B is matched, but Z ∩ B has two elements and the theorem does not apply.

At depth one, with Z the common zeros of annihilating Coleman integrals, this is the comparison step of ED.4/chabauty-coleman-completeness; with exclusion by the Mordell–Weil sieve it is the combination of ED.5/chabauty-sieve-combination.

nodes.title: Residue-disc certificate for quadratic Chabauty functions
nodes.statement: Fix a prime p and a residue disc of X(Q_p) with a parameter t identifying it with p Z_p (t = p s, s ∈ Z_p), produced by an ED.0 p-adic embedding certificate. A quadratic Chabauty disc certificate QCDiscCertificate p ι consists of: finitely many functions f_i : Z_p → Q_p, i ∈ ι (the determinants det T of the quadratic Chabauty pairs, written in s as convergent power series whose first coefficients are known modulo p^N and whose tail obeys height-series-valuation-bound); a finite set C ⊆ Z_p of centres; a precision n ∈ ℕ; and proofs of (covers) every common zero s of the f_i satisfies ‖s − c‖ ≤ p^(−n) for some c ∈ C, and (unique) for each c ∈ C the ball ‖s − c‖ ≤ p^(−n) contains at most one common zero. The certificate is produced by root-determination-precision applied to one f_i, the other functions serving to discard centres at which they do not vanish.
hypotheses: p is prime; ι is a finite index type; the f_i are functions on Z_p given by convergent power series in the disc parameter.
The centres are elements of Z_p known to precision n (rational or integral representatives).
proofSteps: Define the structure with fields fn, centres, prec, covers, unique; covers and unique are genuine conditions, proved for each disc by root-determination-precision.
Common zeros are {s | ∀ i, f_i s = 0}; covers and unique imply that this set is finite with at most #C elements.
acceptance: For p = 17, one function f(s) = s − 1, centres {1} and any precision: a valid certificate whose only common zero is s = 1.
A ball containing two zeros 0 and p^6 at precision 5 violates (unique).

sources.excerpt: All zeroes of det(T1(x)) and det(T2(x)) are simple, and the only simultaneous zeroes are P1, P2, P3 and P5.

nodes.title: Soundness of a quadratic Chabauty certificate
nodes.statement: Let X/Q be a smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus g ≥ 2 with b ∈ X(Q), Jacobian J of rank r = g with log : J(Q) ⊗ Q_p ≅ H⁰(X_{Q_p}, Ω¹)^*, ρ(J) ≥ 2, and p a prime of good reduction. Let Z_1, …, Z_k be nice classes and (θ_j, Υ_j) the quadratic Chabauty pairs of NC.5 with endomorphism E_j, constant c_j and pairing B_j (BDMTV Lemma 3.7, with Υ_j = {0} under potentially good reduction everywhere, Corollary 3.8). Suppose given: (a) a finite set L ⊆ X(Q) of verified rational points containing b and points P_1, …, P_m such that AJ_b(P_i) ⊗ (E_j(AJ_b(P_i)) + c_j) span E (or E_K = H⁰(Ω¹)^* ⊗_{K_p} H⁰(Ω¹)^* when the heights are K-equivariant); (b) for every x̄ ∈ X(F_p) and every choice (α_1, …, α_k) ∈ Υ_1 × ⋯ × Υ_k, a qc-disc-certificate on ]x̄[ for the family (det T_{j,α_j})_{j ≤ k} of the determinant criterion, whose power-series coefficients are computed by local-height-at-p and Coleman integration to the precision certified by height-series-valuation-bound; (c) for every centre of every disc certificate, a matching with an element of L or an exclusion. Then X(Q) = L, an unconditional certified solution set given the stated rank and Picard hypotheses (which are themselves certified inputs). If (b) or (c) fails for some disc, only L ⊆ X(Q) is asserted.
hypotheses: r = g and the p-adic closure of J(Q) has finite index in J(Q_p) (certified rank: xs13-rank-three in the example).
ρ(J) ≥ 2 and Z_1, …, Z_k are nice classes (NC.5).
p is a prime of good reduction and the residue discs are enumerated from X(F_p) exactly.
The local heights away from p are known: Υ_j is computed (or is {0} under potentially good reduction everywhere).
proofSteps: By NC.5 (BDMTV Lemma 3.7, Corollary 3.8, with the correction PAPER-BALAKRISHNAN-DOGRA-MULLER-ETAL-19/E8 that only κ(J(Q)) ⊗ Q_p is used) every x ∈ X(Q) satisfies θ_j(x) − B_j(AJ_b(x), E_j(AJ_b(x)) + c_j) ∈ Υ_j.
By the determinant criterion (BDMTV Lemma 1.5, NC.5) det T_{j,α}(x) = 0 for x ∈ X(Q_p)_α; the matrices T use the points of (a) to eliminate the unknown pairing B_j.

On each residue disc the entries of T are power series: θ_j from local-height-at-p, AJ_b from Coleman integrals (ColemanIntegration L1 via ED.4/abelian-logarithm); their coefficients are certified by height-series-valuation-bound, and root-determination-precision yields the disc certificates (b).
X(F_p) is finite, so finitely many balls cover all common zeros; apply padic-candidate-comparison with the matchings and exclusions (c).
acceptance: X_s(13), p = 17, Z_1, Z_2 from T_7 and T_11: X(Q) = {P0, …, P6} (xs13-rational-points).
Removing the disc ](1:1:1)[ from (b) leaves the computation open: only {P0, …, P6} ⊆ X(Q) follows.

nodes.title: The explicit set-up: affine chart, basis of differentials and Tate class
nodes.statement: An explicit quadratic Chabauty set-up over Q consists of: a smooth projective geometrically connected curve X/Q of genus g ≥ 2; an affine open Y ⊂ X over Q; a base point b ∈ Y(Q) integral at p; the boundary D := X ∖ Y with d := #D(Q̄) points, all defined over a number field L; differentials ω_0, …, ω_{2g+d−2} ∈ H⁰(Y, Ω¹) such that ω_0, …, ω_{2g−1} are of the second kind on X and their classes form a symplectic basis of H¹_dR(X/Q) (ω_i ∪ ω_{g+i} = 1 = −ω_{g+i} ∪ ω_i for i < g, all other cup products 0), ω_0, …, ω_{g−1} are holomorphic on X and form a basis of H⁰(X, Ω¹) (the hypothesis BDMTV §4.5 uses, PAPER-BALAKRISHNAN-DOGRA-MULLER-ETAL-19/E4), and ω_{2g}, …, ω_{2g+d−2} are of the third kind (only simple poles) and complete a basis of H¹_dR(Y/Q); V_dR(Y) := H¹_dR(Y/Q)^* with dual basis T_0, …, T_{2g+d−2}; and an admissible Tate class Z = Σ Z_ij ω_i ⊗ ω_j, i, j < 2g, given by its coefficient matrix (Z_ij) ∈ M_{2g}(Q), nonzero, with (a) Z ∈ (H¹_dR ⊗ H¹_dR)^{φ = p} over Q_p, (b) Z ∈ Fil¹, which in this basis means Z_ij = 0 for i, j ≥ g, (c) Σ Z_ij (ω_i ∪ ω_j) = 0, which in this basis means Σ_{i<g} Z_{i,g+i} = 0 once (d) holds, and (d) Zᵀ = −Z. Conditions (a)–(d) are NC.5's; the class of a nice correspondence satisfies them, and the converse of BDMTV Lemma 4.7 is not used (E5).
hypotheses: X smooth projective geometrically connected of genus g ≥ 2 over Q; p a prime of good reduction; b ∈ Y(Q) integral at p.
ω_0, …, ω_{g−1} holomorphic; ω_0, …, ω_{2g−1} of the second kind with symplectic classes; ω_{2g}, …, ω_{2g+d−2} of the third kind.
Z nonzero with (a)–(d).
D is nonempty, and L may be enlarged to a finite Galois splitting field so the local-expansion descent is stated over all conjugate boundary points.
proofSteps: Over Q, take a smooth projective geometrically connected curve X of genus g≥2, a nonempty reduced boundary divisor D of degree d=#D(Qbar) and affine open Y=X−D, b∈Y(Q), a good prime p and a smooth Z_p-model with integral b. Put A=Γ(Y,O_Y), K=Q(X)=Frac(A). Choose a finite Galois splitting field L for D and uniformizers t_x identifying completed local rings at x∈D(L) with L[[t_x]] and their fraction fields with L((t_x)); expansions must be the maps induced by K⊗L, not arbitrary Laurent-family maps. Choose ω_0,…,ω_{2g+d−2} in Ω¹(Y/Q) whose classes form a basis of H¹_dR(Y), the first2g of the second kind, the firstg a basis of H⁰(X,Ω¹), with cup matrix C=[[0,I],[-I,0]], and third-kind complement with residue map an isomorphism onto {(r_x):Σr_x=0}. Put V_dR=H¹_dR(X)^* with dual basis T_i. Take nonzero rational tensor Z with antisymmetry, lower-right g×g block0 and zero cup contraction; under crystalline/de Rham comparison require Frobenius weight p, in coordinates FᵀZF=pZ. For height applications additionally supply an actual nice correspondence whose cycle class is Z; do not infer a rational algebraic cycle from these linear/Frobenius conditions. The suggested file keeps only its separately named linear-data helper; the exact geometric signature and API are in suggestedOmissions.

The residue map from span(ω_{2g}, …, ω_{2g+d−2}) to L^D is injective with image the sum-zero hyperplane, because the kernel of H¹_dR(Y) → L^d is H¹_dR(X) (BDMTV proof of Lemma 4.10); this is the property explicit-connection uses.
Condition (b) reads Z_ij = 0 for i, j ≥ g only because ω_0, …, ω_{g−1} span Fil¹; condition (c) reads Σ_{i<g} Z_{i,g+i} = 0 only for the symplectic convention.
acceptance: X_s(13), Y = {Z ≠ 0}, b = P2 = (0,0), g = 3: ω = (1, x, y, …)dx/Q_y and Z1, Z2 of xs13-tate-classes form a set-up.
A symmetric nonzero matrix is never admissible, by (d).

nodes.title: The connection of A_Z on the affine chart and the uniqueness of η
nodes.statement: In an explicit set-up, there is a trivialisation s_0(b, ·) : (Q ⊕ V_dR ⊕ Q(1)) ⊗ O_Y ≅ A_Z(b)|_Y (26) in which ∇ = d + Λ with Λ = −[[0, 0, 0], [ω, 0, 0], [η, ωᵀZ, 0]] (27), in the ordered basis 1, T_0, …, T_{2g−1}, S, where ω = (ω_0, …, ω_{2g−1})ᵀ and η is a differential in the span of ω_{2g}, …, ω_{2g+d−2}. Moreover η is the unique differential in that span for which d + Λ extends to a connection on X without singularities (Lemma 4.10); equivalently, with the gauge data of gauge-transformation, Res_x(Ω_xᵀ Z dΩ_x − η) = 0 for every x ∈ D (30). In terms of residues: η = Σ_k c_k ω_{2g+k} where (c_k) is the unique solution of Σ_k c_k Res_x(ω_{2g+k}) = Res_x(Ω_xᵀ Z dΩ_x) for all x ∈ D.
hypotheses: An explicit set-up with admissible Tate class Z.
A_Z(b) is the filtered connection obtained by pushing out A_2^dR along Z (NC.5).
proofSteps: Kim's universal property (NC.2, BDMTV Theorem 4.2, corrected as in E6 to pointed objects with v in the fibre at b) gives A_2^dR(Y) = ⊕_{i≤2} V_dR(Y)^{⊗i} ⊗ O_Y with ∇(v ⊗ 1) = −Σ (T_i ⊗ v) ⊗ ω_i (21); Corollary 4.4 identifies A_2^dR(X)|_Y with its maximal quotient extending holomorphically to X.

Pushing out along Z (which factors through V_dR^{⊗2}/Im ∪^* by (c)) gives a connection of the form (27) with η = Σ_{i ≤ 2g+d−2} α_i ω_i; the change T_i ↦ T_i + α_i S for i < 2g removes the components of η along ω_0, …, ω_{2g−1} (Remarks 4.8–4.9).

At x ∈ D the gauge transformation C_x satisfies dg_x = Ω_xᵀ Z dΩ_x − η (29); a formal primitive g_x exists in L((t_x)) if and only if the residue (30) vanishes, which is the condition for the connection to extend over x.
By explicit-setup's residue injectivity the residue conditions at the d points determine η uniquely in the span of the third-kind differentials.
acceptance: For X_s(13) on Y = {Z ≠ 0}: η_{Z1} = −(44x² + (148/3)xy + 8y²)dx/Q_y and η_{Z2} = (−40x² + 148xy + 36y²)dx/Q_y (xs13-first-chart-hodge-data).
The printed step (i) of BDMTV §4.5 uses dΩ_xᵀZΩ_x − η, which determines a different η unless the residues of Ω_xᵀZdΩ_x vanish (PAPER-BALAKRISHNAN-DOGRA-MULLER-ETAL-19/E2); the condition here is (30).

nodes.title: Gauge transformations at the points at infinity
nodes.statement: In an explicit set-up, for x ∈ D with local parameter t_x over L, a trivialisation s_x of A_Z over L[[t_x]] with connection d exists because every unipotent connection on a formal disc is trivial, and the gauge transformation C_x := s_x^(−1) ∘ s_0 ∈ End(Q ⊕ V_dR ⊕ Q(1)) ⊗ L((t_x)) satisfies C_x^(−1) dC_x = Λ (28). Conversely every unipotent C_x with (28) defines such s_x. Explicitly C_x = [[1, 0, 0], [Ω_x, 1, 0], [g_x, Ω_xᵀZ, 1]] where Ω_x ∈ L((t_x))^{2g} and g_x ∈ L((t_x)) satisfy dΩ_x = −ω and dg_x = Ω_xᵀ Z dΩ_x − η (29); Ω_x and g_x are determined up to additive constants, and the condition of hodge-filtration-explicit does not depend on these constants.
hypotheses: An explicit set-up and the connection matrix Λ of explicit-connection.
t_x is a uniformiser at x ∈ D over L, chosen Gal(L/Q)-equivariantly.
proofSteps: Expand C^(−1)dC for C = [[1,0,0],[Ω,1,0],[g,ΩᵀZ,1]]: C^(−1) = [[1,0,0],[−Ω,1,0],[ΩᵀZΩ − g, −ΩᵀZ, 1]] (using ΩᵀZΩ = 0 by antisymmetry) and C^(−1)dC = [[0,0,0],[dΩ,0,0],[dg − ΩᵀZdΩ, dΩᵀZ, 0]].
Comparing with Λ = −[[0,0,0],[ω,0,0],[η,ωᵀZ,0]] gives dΩ = −ω, dΩᵀZ = −ωᵀZ and dg = ΩᵀZdΩ − η, which is (29).
Ω_x is a vector of formal primitives of −ω, which exist in L((t_x)) because ω_0, …, ω_{2g−1} are of the second kind; g_x exists exactly when (30) holds (explicit-connection).

Changing Ω_x by a constant vector c changes g_x by cᵀZΩ_x plus a constant; the principal parts used in hodge-filtration-explicit change by terms involving only Z's columns of holomorphic index and the holomorphic primitives, which are regular.
acceptance: The 2021 restatement of this step uses dΩ_{x,i} = ω_i and defines g_x through the integral of dΩ_xᵀZdΩ_x − η; both deviate from (29) (EffectiveDiophantineMethods/E15, EffectiveDiophantineMethods/E16).

nodes.title: Explicit Hodge filtration of A_Z (BDMTV Theorem 4.11)
nodes.statement: In an explicit set-up with gauge data (Ω_x, g_x)_{x ∈ D}, let N = (0_g, 1_g)ᵀ ∈ M_{2g×g}(Q), the matrix of Fil⁰V_dR ↪ V_dR. (i) There are unique γ_Fil ∈ O(Y) and b_Fil = (b_g, …, b_{2g−1})ᵀ ∈ Q^g such that γ_Fil(b) = 0 and g_x + γ_Fil − b_Filᵀ Nᵀ Ω_x − Ω_xᵀ Z N Nᵀ Ω_x ∈ L[[t_x]] for every x ∈ D (32). (ii) A basis of Fil⁰A_Z|_Y in the trivialisation (26) is {1 + γ_Fil S, T_g + b_g S, …, T_{2g−1} + b_{2g−1} S} (33); equivalently, with Q ⊕ V_dR ⊕ Q(1) filtered by Fil^(−1) = everything, Fil⁰ = Q ⊕ Fil⁰V_dR, Fil¹ = 0 (31), the filtered isomorphism s^Fil can be chosen with s_0^(−1) ∘ s^Fil = [[1,0,0],[0,1,0],[γ_Fil, β_Filᵀ, 1]], β_Fil = (0, …, 0, b_g, …, b_{2g−1})ᵀ (36).
hypotheses: An explicit set-up (with ω_0, …, ω_{g−1} holomorphic, E4) and the gauge transformations of gauge-transformation.
The Hodge filtration of A_Z is the one characterised by Hadian's theorem (NC.2).
proofSteps: Uniqueness in (i): if (γ, b) is the difference of two solutions then γ(b) = 0 and γ − bᵀNᵀΩ_x is regular at each x ∈ D, so dγ + Σ_{i≥g} b_i ω_i is regular on X, hence holomorphic. Its class Σ_{i≥g} b_i[ω_i] lies in Fil¹ = span([ω_0], …, [ω_{g−1}]), so b = 0 by linear independence; then γ is a regular function on X, constant, and γ(b) = 0 gives γ = 0.

With the actual gauges of the mixed connection, use the principal-parts exact sequence 0→L→Γ(Y_L,O)→⊕_{x∈D(L)} L((t_x))/L[[t_x]]→H¹(X_L,O)→0 and H¹_dR(X_L)/Fil¹≅H¹(X_L,O). The principal parts of the primitives of ω_g,…,ω_{2g−1} map to a basis of the last group. For N=(0,I)ᵀ prove existence and uniqueness of γ∈Γ(Y,O), b_Fil∈Q^g with γ(b)=0 and g_x+γ−b_FilᵀNᵀΩ_x−Ω_xᵀZNNᵀΩ_x regular at every boundary point. Descend from L by uniqueness.
The conditions in (i) do not depend on the additive constants in Ω_x and g_x: the lower right block of Z vanishes (condition (b)) and the primitives of ω_0, …, ω_{g−1} are regular.

(ii): with B_x = [[1,0],[NᵀΩ_x,1]], C_x H B_x^(−1) has entries Ω_x − NNᵀΩ_x (regular by holomorphy), Ω_xᵀZN (regular since the lower right block of Z is zero) and g_x + γ_Fil − b_FilᵀNᵀΩ_x − Ω_xᵀZNNᵀΩ_x (regular by (i)) (35); hence the subbundle H spanned by (33) extends over X.

H satisfies Hadian's three conditions (NC.2, BDMTV Theorem 4.5): Griffiths transversality is vacuous for weights 0 and −1, H maps isomorphically onto Fil⁰ of A_1 (top right block zero, middle block the inclusion), and the identity lies in Fil⁰ since γ_Fil(b) = 0; by uniqueness in Hadian's theorem H = Fil⁰A_Z.
acceptance: For Z = 0: η = 0, b_Fil = 0, γ_Fil = 0, and Fil⁰A_Z is the split filtration.

nodes.title: Algorithm for the Hodge filtration data (η, b_Fil, γ_Fil)
nodes.statement: Input: an explicit set-up with exact data over Q and L (the differentials as elements of the function field of Y, the points of D with Galois-equivariant parameters t_x) and an admissible Tate matrix Z. Steps: (i) for each x ∈ D compute the Laurent expansions of ω_0, …, ω_{2g+d−2} at x to certified orders sufficient for every residue and principal part below; these orders must account for products of primitives, not just the largest pole order of an individual differential, and formal primitives Ω_x with dΩ_x = −ω; compute η = Σ_k c_k ω_{2g+k} as the unique solution of Σ_k c_k Res_x(ω_{2g+k}) = Res_x(Ω_xᵀ Z dΩ_x) for all x ∈ D (condition (30), not the printed step (i), E2); (ii) solve dg_x = Ω_xᵀ Z dΩ_x − η for the principal part of g_x in L((t_x))/L[[t_x]]; (iii) compute the principal parts of Ω_xᵀZNNᵀΩ_x and solve the finite linear system for b_Fil ∈ Q^g and γ_Fil in a finite-dimensional space of functions on Y with certified pole bounds derived from those principal parts (for X_s(13): H⁰(X, O(2D))) with γ_Fil(b) = 0, as in hodge-filtration-explicit (32); output (η, b_Fil, γ_Fil) and β_Fil = (0, b_Fil). Given these sufficient truncation and pole bounds, all steps are finite exact linear algebra over L and terminate; the output is checked by substituting into (30) and (32), which is the certificate.
hypotheses: Exact input data over Q and L; certified sufficient Laurent truncation orders for the residue and product/principal-part computations are supplied.

A finite-dimensional Riemann–Roch space containing γ_Fil is supplied with a certified pole bound for the expressions in (32); a bound from the individual differential poles alone is not claimed sufficient.
proofSteps: Step (i) is a linear system of d equations (one per x ∈ D) in the d − 1 unknowns c_k; it has rank d − 1 by explicit-setup's residue injectivity and is consistent because η exists (explicit-connection), so its solution is unique.
Step (ii) determines the principal part of g_x because the residue of its derivative vanishes by (i).

Step (iii) has a unique solution by hodge-filtration-explicit (i) once the chosen finite-dimensional function space contains γ_Fil. A sufficient pole bound must be deduced from g_x, Ω_xᵀZNNᵀΩ_x and b_FilᵀNᵀΩ_x; the maximum pole order of the individual ω_i does not justify this. The general bound and its certified computation are recorded as a gap.
Verification: the output satisfies (30) and (32) by exact arithmetic over L; no p-adic precision enters, so the Hodge data are exact rational data.

nodes.title: Left and right multiplication matrices and parallel transport
nodes.statement: Let Z be an antisymmetric 2g × 2g matrix over a commutative ring R. The algebra A_Z(R) = R ⊕ R^{2g} ⊕ R (the quotient of the truncated tensor algebra of V_dR by the kernel of Z on degree two) has multiplication (a, b, c)·(a', b', c') = (aa', ab' + a'b, ac' + a'c + bᵀZb'). In the ordered basis 1, T_0, …, T_{2g−1}, S, left multiplication by u = (a, b, c) has matrix L(u) = [[a, 0, 0], [b, a·1, 0], [c, bᵀZ, a]] and right multiplication has matrix R(u) = [[a, 0, 0], [b, a·1, 0], [c, −bᵀZ, a]] (44). For points b, b_0, x, x_0 in residue discs, with I(x_1, x_2) = 1 + Σ_w ∫_{x_1}^{x_2} w(ω_0, …, ω_{2g+d−2}) the iterated integrals of words of length ≤ 2 (the index range corrected as in EffectiveDiophantineMethods/E24) pushed to A_Z, the transport τ_{b,x} : A_Z^dR(b_0, x_0) → A_Z^dR(b, x) is v ↦ I(x_0, x) · v · I(b, b_0) (41), so its matrix is L(I(x_0, x)) · R(I(b, b_0)), with Coleman (Besser) integrals between different discs and power-series integrals inside a disc. The Frobenius operators satisfy φ_Z(b_0, x_0) = x_0^* Φ_Z and φ_Z(b, x) = τ_{b,x} ∘ φ_Z(b_0, x_0) ∘ τ_{b,x}^(−1) (43).
hypotheses: Z antisymmetric (condition (d)); R commutative.
Iterated integrals are Coleman integrals (ColemanIntegration L1), normalised as in (40)–(41) with the orientation of E3.
proofSteps: The multiplication is associative with unit (1, 0, 0): for u = (a, b, c), v = (a', b', c'), w = (a'', b'', c'') both (uv)w and u(vw) have S-coordinate aa'c'' + aa''c' + a'a''c + a''bᵀZb' + a'bᵀZb'' + ab'ᵀZb''.
Left multiplication: u·(a', b', c') = (aa', ab' + a'b, ac' + a'c + bᵀZb') gives the columns of L(u).
Right multiplication: (a', b', c')·u = (a'a, a'b + ab', a'c + ac' + b'ᵀZb) and b'ᵀZb = −bᵀZb' by antisymmetry, giving R(u).

Path composition I(x_1, x_3) = I(x_2, x_3)·I(x_1, x_2) (Lemma 4.3, NC.2) and Besser's Frobenius-equivariant transport (NC.2, BDMTV (41)) give τ_{b,x}; the orientation is I(x_0, x) on the left and I(b, b_0) on the right (E3).
acceptance: For u = (1, 0, 0) both matrices are the identity.
L(u)L(v) = L(uv), R(u)R(v) = R(vu), and L(u)R(v) = R(v)L(u) by associativity.

nodes.title: The Frobenius structure of A_Z on a chart (BDMTV (45))
nodes.statement: In an explicit set-up over Q_p, let φ be an overconvergent Frobenius lift on a strict neighbourhood of ]U[ for an open U ⊆ Y_{F_p}, write φ^*ω = Fω + df with F ∈ M_{2g}(Q_p) and f a column vector of overconvergent functions with f(b_0) = 0 for a Teichmüller point b_0 (data from Tuitman's algorithm, RD.7), and set Λ_φ = −[[0,0,0],[φ^*ω,0,0],[φ^*η, φ^*ωᵀZ, 0]]. Then FᵀZF = pZ, and the inverse G = Φ_Z^(−1) of the Frobenius structure is the unique graded-compatible pointed inverse Frobenius of the actual universal quotient, represented by an invertible (2g+2) × (2g+2) matrix of overconvergent functions with Λ_φ G + dG = GΛ and G(b_0)^(−1) sending 1 to 1, namely G = [[1, 0, 0], [f, F, 0], [h, gᵀ, p]], where g is the column vector with dgᵀ = dfᵀZF (the constant fixed by exactness of the next equation) and h is the function with dh = ωᵀFᵀZf + dfᵀZf − gᵀω + φ^*η − pη and h(b_0) = 0.
hypotheses: An explicit set-up over Q_p; p of good reduction; φ an overconvergent Frobenius lift with b_0 Teichmüller.
Z satisfies (a): FᵀZF = pZ where F is the Frobenius matrix on H¹_dR in the basis ω (Z is φ = p-invariant, the cup product has Frobenius weight p).
proofSteps: The Frobenius structure Φ_Z : φ^*A_Z^rig ≅ A_Z^rig is a morphism of connections, so in the trivialisation s_0 its inverse G satisfies Λ_φ G + dG = GΛ.

NC.2 supplies the unique pointed Frobenius Φ_Z and graded-compatible quotient. G=Φ_Z⁻¹ has diagonal(1,F,p); Φ_Z has diagonal(1,F⁻¹,p⁻¹). Pointed normalization at b0 is f(b0)=h(b0)=0; the remaining g constant is fixed by the cohomological reduction, not by f(b0)=0 alone.

Write the block equations of Λ_φ G + dG = GΛ: the (2,1) block gives df = φ^*ω − Fω; the (3,2) block gives dgᵀ = dfᵀZF using FᵀZF = pZ; the (3,1) block gives dh = ωᵀFᵀZf + dfᵀZf − gᵀω + φ^*η − pη (checked entrywise: PAPER-BALAKRISHNAN-DOGRA-MULLER-ETAL-19/60 note).

Set g0=−FᵀZf. Actual rigid-cohomology reduction of ξ=(φ*ω)ᵀZf+φ*η−pη−g0ᵀω gives ξ=cᵀω+dh; put g=g0+c and h(b0)=0. BDMTV2021v4(4.5)–(4.7)p19 states this step. RD.7 must supply the actual overconvergent sections, exactness and precision, and NC.2 identifies them with the universal Frobenius.
acceptance: For Z = 0 and g = 1 data with φ^*ω = Fω, f = 0: G = [[1,0,0],[0,F,0],[h, 0, p]] with dh = φ^*η − pη.
At p = 17 on ]U_1[ for X_s(13) the matrices F, f, g, h are the data of xs13-first-chart-frobenius.

nodes.title: The Frobenius-equivariant splitting at Teichmüller and general points
nodes.statement: With G as in frobenius-structure-matrix and x_0 ∈ ]U[ a Teichmüller point, the Frobenius-equivariant splitting s^φ satisfies s_0(b_0, x_0)^(−1) ∘ s^φ(b_0, x_0) = [[1, 0, 0], [(I − F)^(−1)f, 1, 0], [(1/(1 − p))(gᵀ(I − F)^(−1)f + h), gᵀ(F − p)^(−1), 1]] evaluated at x_0 (the unique unipotent matrix S satisfying G(x_0)S=S diag(1,F,p), equivalently G(x_0)^(−1)S=S diag(1,F^(−1),p^(−1))). For arbitrary b, x in residue discs of ]U[ with Teichmüller representatives b_0, x_0, s_0(b, x)^(−1) ∘ s^φ(b, x) = L(I(x_0, x)) · R(I(b, b_0)) · s_0(b_0, x_0)^(−1) ∘ s^φ(b_0, x_0), with L, R from transport-matrices (the corrected orientation, E3). Writing this matrix as [[1,0,0],[α_φ,1,0],[γ_φ,β_φᵀ,1]], α_φ(b, x) = ∫_b^x ω.
hypotheses: frobenius-structure-matrix; x_0 Teichmüller (φ(x_0) = x_0); p > 1 so 1 − p and F − p, I − F are invertible (the eigenvalues of F are Weil numbers of absolute value p^(1/2)).
proofSteps: At a Teichmüller point Frobenius acts on A_Z^dR(b_0, x_0) by G(x_0)^(−1); s^φ is the unique unipotent isomorphism from Q ⊕ V_dR ⊕ Q(1) with Frobenius diag(1,F^(−1),p^(−1)).

Solving the unipotent conjugation block by block: α = (I − F)^(−1)f(x_0), β = gᵀ(F − p)^(−1), γ = (1/(1 − p))(gᵀα + h(x_0)); invertibility of I − F, F − p and 1 − p follows from the Weil bounds (ColemanIntegration L1/weil-weight-no-root-of-unity).
(I − F)^(−1)f(x_0) = ∫_{b_0}^{x_0} ω by Frobenius-equivariance of Coleman integration (ColemanIntegration L1/coleman-integration-characterisation).

General points: s^φ(b, x) = τ_{b,x} ∘ s^φ(b_0, x_0), and τ_{b,x}(v) = I(x_0, x)·v·I(b, b_0) by (41); hence the product of left multiplication by I(x_0, x), right multiplication by I(b, b_0), and the Teichmüller matrix. The (2,1) block is ∫_{x_0}^x ω + ∫_{b_0}^{x_0} ω + ∫_b^{b_0} ω = ∫_b^x ω.
acceptance: As printed (p.923) the transport factors have reversed limits, giving α_φ(b, x) = α_φ(b_0, x_0) − ∫_{x_0}^x ω − ∫_b^{b_0} ω, which is not ∫_b^x ω (E3).

nodes.title: The local height at p of A_Z(b, x) (BDMTV Lemma 5.5)
nodes.statement: Let s be a splitting of the Hodge filtration of V_dR with idempotents s_1, s_2 onto s(V_dR/Fil⁰) and Fil⁰, and χ_p the local component of the fixed idèle class character. For x ∈ X(Q_p) ∩ ]U[, with γ_Fil, β_Fil from hodge-filtration-explicit and α_φ, β_φ, γ_φ from frobenius-equivariant-splitting, the local height of the mixed extension A_Z(b, x) is h_p(A_Z(b, x)) = χ_p(γ_φ(b, x) − γ_Fil(b, x) − β_φ(b, x)ᵀ · s_1(α_φ(b, x)) − β_Fil(b)ᵀ · s_2(α_φ(b, x))). As a function of x on each residue disc it is a convergent power series in the disc parameter whose coefficients are computable from the data above, and θ_Z(x) := h_p(A_Z(b, x)) is the function of the quadratic Chabauty pair.
hypotheses: The splitting s and the character χ are fixed (independence of the zero set from both is NC.5's).
x lies in a residue disc of ]U[ where φ is defined and no basis differential has a pole.
proofSteps: By NC.5 (BDMTV Lemma 5.4) D_cris(A_Z(b, x)) ≅ A_Z^dR(b, x) as filtered φ-modules, with A_Z^dR(b, x) = x^*A_Z.
The height formula (17) (NC.5) expresses h_p of a mixed extension through the matrices of s^φ and s^Fil relative to a vector-space splitting s_0.
Take s_0 = s_0(b, x) of (26); then s_0^(−1) ∘ s^Fil is given by hodge-filtration-explicit (36) evaluated at x and s_0^(−1) ∘ s^φ by frobenius-equivariant-splitting; substitute into (17).

On a residue disc, γ_Fil is a rational function, α_φ, β_φ, γ_φ are single and double Coleman integrals in the parameter (power-series integrals inside the disc), so θ_Z is a convergent power series there.
acceptance: At x = b = b_0 (Teichmüller): h_p(A_Z(b, b)) = χ_p((1/(1−p))h(b) − 0 − β_φ(b,b)ᵀ s_1(0) − β_Fil(b)ᵀ s_2(0)) = 0.
X_s(13), p = 17: θ_{Z1}, θ_{Z2} on the discs of ]U_1[ (xs13-first-chart-frobenius).

nodes.title: Changing the base point (BDMTV Lemma 5.7)
nodes.statement: Let b' ∈ X(Q_p) lie in a residue disc where none of the basis differentials has a pole. Then β_Fil(b') = β_Fil(b) and γ_Fil(b', x) = γ_Fil(b, x) − γ_Fil(b, b') (48), and s_0(b', b')^(−1) ∘ s^φ(b', b') = [[1, 0, 0], [0, 1, 0], [0, β_φ(b, b)ᵀ + 2∫_b^{b'} ωᵀZ, 1]]. Consequently the local heights h_p(A_Z(b', x)) for x in the disc of b', and in particular in a disc where the Frobenius lift is not defined, are computed from the single integrals ∫_b^{b'} ω (Coleman integrals with the original lift) and power-series integrals inside the disc of b'. The formula changes the individual scalar height functions; only the naturally identified Chabauty–Kim locus is base-point independent. For the global rational-point application take rational b′ and transport the NC.5 height-pair data as well.
hypotheses: b' in a residue disc with no poles of ω_0, …, ω_{2g+d−2}; Coleman integrals between discs are taken with respect to the original Frobenius lift (BDMTV §5.5).
proofSteps: The Hodge data: by hodge-filtration-explicit the conditions (32) for b' differ from those for b only in the normalisation γ(b') = 0, giving (48).
The φ-equivariant unipotent isomorphism A_2^dR(Y)(b, b) → A_2^dR(Y)(b', b'), s_0(b, b)(v) ↦ s_0(b', b')(I(b, b')·v·I(b', b)) (49), passes to the quotient A_Z.

With L, R of transport-matrices the matrix is L(I(b, b')) · R(I(b, b'))^(−1) · s_0(b,b)^(−1)s^φ(b,b), where I(b', b) = I(b, b')^(−1); multiplying out with Z antisymmetric gives zero (2,1) block and (3,2) block β_φ(b, b)ᵀ + 2∫_b^{b'}ωᵀZ (PAPER-BALAKRISHNAN-DOGRA-MULLER-ETAL-19/65 note: the arXiv v1 product order L·M·R^(−1) gives a wrong (3,1) entry).
Across residue discs the integrals are Coleman integrals; the identification of (41) with the Frobenius-equivariant transport is NC.2's (B19 item 93).
acceptance: For b' = b the formula reduces to s_0(b,b)^(−1)s^φ(b,b) = [[1,0,0],[0,1,0],[0,β_φ(b,b)ᵀ,1]].

nodes.statement: (i) (BDMTV 2019 §6.4.1.) Let F_1, …, F_m ∈ Z_p[[t]] and let G(t) = Σ_n c_n t^n = Σ_{i,j} a_ij ∫F_i(∫F_j) + Σ_i a_i ∫F_i + Σ_i b_i F_i with a_ij, a_i, b_i ∈ Q_p, where ∫ denotes the formal primitive vanishing at t = 0. Then v_p(c_n) ≥ min_{i,j}{v_p(a_ij), v_p(a_i), v_p(b_i)} − 2⌊log_p n⌋ for n ≥ 1. Let d_i(η) be certified lower bounds for the actual degree i−1 coefficient of η (all coefficient/coordinate changes included); the source uses a finite polynomial-coefficient branch and0 after its degree bound, whose sufficiency must be proved for the actual model. hypotheses: F_i have p-integral coefficients (after scaling the disc parameter so that the basis differentials are integral on the disc).
The constants c_1, c_2, c_3 and i_0 are computed from certified data (ED.0 valuation certificates).

proofSteps: Integrating t^(n−1) divides by n, which costs v_p(n) ≤ ⌊log_p n⌋; a double integral costs at most twice that, and the coefficients a, b contribute their valuation: this is (i).

Compute c1 from the actual Frobenius splitting at the disc centre and derive the local transport branch φ(i) from the actual integral expansions; the underlying coordinate coefficient lower bounds must be certified. Combine Nekovář’s formula with βFil,γFil and the fixed equivariant splitting. The required coefficient semantics and all constants are spelled out in suggestedOmissions.

For i≥i0 use the three explicit threshold inequalities to select φ(i)=−2⌊log_p i⌋. Combine the actual global-height coefficient bound c3 and local-height bound to obtain Proposition4.6. For smaller i use finite certificates; zero coefficients have valuation∞. E30 records the preprint branch corrected in the published paper.
The valuations of the input constants are certified by ED.0/valuation-certificate.

nodes.title: Provable determination of roots in a residue disc
nodes.statement: (BDMTV 2021 Lemma 4.7.) Let F(x) = Σ_{i≥0} F_i x^i ∈ Q_p[[x]] such that F(pT) is restricted (its coefficients tend to zero), and integers k, m, n with n > k, m ≥ 1, min_i{ord_p(F_i) + i} = k, using ord_p(0)=+∞, and ord_p(F_i) + i ≥ n for every i ≥ m (that is, max{i : ord_p(F_i) + i < n} < m; the printed condition max{i : ord_p(F_i) + i = n} < m is too weak, EffectiveDiophantineMethods/E21), and suppose F has at most d roots counted with multiplicity over ℂ_p in the closed disc {ord_p(x) ≥ 1}, where d ≥ 1. Then the roots of F over ℂ_p in {ord_p(x) ≥ 1}, with multiplicity, are determined to precision (n − k)/d by F_0, …, F_{m−1} modulo p^n: After setting G(T)=p^(−k)F(pT), choose an actual polynomial H over Q_p with Gauss norm ||G−H||≤p^(−(n−k)). G and H have the same nonzero reduction and hence the same Weierstrass degree D≤d. Their roots in the closed unit disc over completed C_p, counted with multiplicity, admit a matching within radius p^(−(n−k)/d). Transport these balls by x=pT. A residue class solving a congruence is not itself a polynomial root and carries no multiplicity or lift guarantee. With d = 1 after recentring and rescaling (BDMTV 2021 Remark 4.8), each simple root is isolated in a ball containing no other root, which is the (unique) condition of qc-disc-certificate; the number d itself is bounded by the residue-disc zero bound of ED.4 (Strassmann).
hypotheses: F converges on the closed disc ord_p(x) ≥ 1 (ensured by height-series-valuation-bound).
The hypotheses on k, m, n are checked from certified coefficient valuations (ED.0).
proofSteps: G(x) := p^(−k)F(px) lies in Z_p[[x]] ∖ pZ_p[[x]] by the definition of k.
For α ∈ Z_p the positive slopes of the Newton polygon of G(x + α) are determined by the first m coefficients, since ord_p(F_i) + i ≥ n for i ≥ m makes G a polynomial of degree < m modulo p^(n−k).

If G is congruent modulo p^(n−k) to a polynomial H with a root α of multiplicity e, the first e coefficients of G(x + α) have valuation ≥ n − k; since G(x + α) has degree ≤ m modulo p^(n−k) and a unit coefficient, its Newton polygon has a segment of slope ≥ (n − k)/d of length at least e.
The zero count d comes from ED.4/residue-disc-zero-bound (Strassmann's theorem, ED.4/strassmann-bound).

Normalize to G with Gauss norm one, choose the nonzero last unit coefficient and identify its Weierstrass degree D with the closed-disc root count. For a polynomial H congruent to G in Gauss norm, use Weierstrass preparation and Newton polygons to match the two root multisets over completed C_p; certify cluster multiplicities and isolation separately. No implication from a bare solution modulo p^N to an actual root is used.
acceptance: A simple root (d = 1) of F in the closed disc ord_p(x) ≥ 1 is determined to precision n − k from F_0, …, F_{m−1} modulo p^n, and its ball contains no other root.

F(x) = x² − p^(2N) (N ≥ 1) has the two roots ±p^N in the disc, so d = 2 and k = 2; the lemma determines them only to precision (n − 2)/2, which illustrates the loss for clustered roots and why simple, separated roots are required for isolation.

nodes.title: Quadratic Chabauty for modular curves: algorithm with termination and failure conditions
nodes.statement: Input: a curve X/Q (a modular curve or Atkin–Lehner quotient) with certified rank r = g (from the analytic-rank-one route, GZ.8 and HE.7, or from a descent certificate ED.3), rk NS(J) > 1, and image of J(Q) in H⁰(X_{Q_p}, Ω¹)^* of rank g; a covering of X by affine patches birational to plane curves Q(x, y) = 0 monic in y with p-integral coefficients satisfying Tuitman's Assumption 1 (as corrected in June 2020, RD.7); a prime p of good reduction such that T_p generates End⁰(J); for every prime ℓ not of potentially good reduction, the local height functions X(Q_ℓ) → Ker(NS(J) → NS(X))^*_{Q_p} (NC.5, via a regular semistable model); a starting precision n and a height bound B. Steps: (1) compute X(Q)_known, the rational points of height ≤ B; (2) compute an integral symplectic basis of H¹_dR (else FAIL); (3) Frobenius on H¹_dR by Tuitman's algorithm and T_p = F_p + pF_p^(−1) (Eichler–Shimura); (4) an End(J)-equivariant splitting with isotropic kernel; (5) a basis Z_1, …, Z_{ρ−1} of Ker(NS(J) → NS(X)) as polynomials in T_p; (6) for each Z_i: λ_Fil by hodge-filtration-algorithm and λ_φ by frobenius-equivariant-splitting on each patch; solve for the height pairing from known points or from Coleman–Gross heights of r independent points of J(Q) (else FAIL); compute the roots of the quadratic Chabauty functions (else FAIL on precision loss); FAIL if a non-simple root occurs at a point of X(Q)_known; (7) return the common roots A. Output: FAIL, or a finite set A of points of X(Q_p) known to precision n' ≤ n with X(Q_p)_2 ∩ (covered discs) ⊆ A. A non-FAIL output is converted into a certified solution set only by padic-candidate-comparison (matching with X(Q)_known, exclusion by the Mordell–Weil sieve of ED.5); a FAIL output is an open computation, not an empty set.
hypotheses: The rank hypothesis r = g and the isomorphism of the p-adic logarithm are certified inputs, not outputs (BDMTV 2021 Remark 3.13–3.14).
Tuitman's Assumption 1 for each patch at p (RD.7).
Local heights away from p are supplied for every bad prime.
proofSteps: Termination: every step is a finite computation (finitely many patches, residue discs, cycles; finite linear algebra; finitely many power-series coefficients to precision n).

Soundness of a non-FAIL output: by qc-certificate-sound, each rational point lies in the common zero set on its disc, and the roots are certified by root-determination-precision with the bounds of height-series-valuation-bound.

Failure conditions are exactly: no integral symplectic basis (2); unsolvable height pairing (6b); precision loss in root finding (6c); a multiple root at a known point (6d). Increasing n remedies precision loss unless the p-adic logarithm fails to be an isomorphism or roots are multiple for geometric reasons (Remark 3.14).
Unresolved inputs advertised by the output: the rank certificate, the local heights away from p, and the comparison of A with X(Q)_known.
acceptance: X_0^+(97), p = 5: the output consists of the ten known points (x0plus-genus-three-points).
X_S4(13), p = 11 on two patches: output the four known points (xs4-13-rational-points).

nodes.title: Plane quartic model of X_s(13), its seven known points and the residue discs at 17
nodes.statement: Let B(X, Y, Z) := (−Y − Z)X³ + (2Y² + YZ)X² + (−Y³ + Y²Z − 2YZ² + Z³)X + (2Y²Z² − 3YZ³) (Baran's quartic) and Q(X, Y, Z) := Y⁴ + 5X⁴ − 6X²Y² + 6X³Z + 26X²YZ + 10XY²Z − 10Y³Z − 32X²Z² − 40XYZ² + 24Y²Z² + 32XZ³ − 16YZ³. (i) X_s(13) ≅ X_0^+(169) over Q, and the canonical model of X_0^+(169) is the smooth plane quartic B = 0, cut out by the quartic relation among the three Galois conjugates of the newform f of xs13-endomorphism-algebra (which satisfy no quadratic relation). (ii) Q(X − Y, X + Y, X + Z) = 16·B(X, Y, Z), so (X : Y : Z) ↦ (X − Y : X + Y : X + Z) is a Q-isomorphism {B = 0} → {Q = 0}; Q is monic in Y. (iii) B = 0 has good reduction at every prime ≠ 13, and Q = 0 at every prime ≠ 2, 13; Q is smooth modulo 17 and #{Q = 0}(F_17) = 20. (iv) The points P0 = (1 : 1 : 1), P1 = (1 : 1 : 2), P2 = (0 : 0 : 1), P3 = (−3 : 3 : 2), P4 = (1 : 1 : 0), P5 = (0 : 2 : 1), P6 = (−1 : 1 : 0) lie on Q = 0 and have seven distinct reductions modulo 17. (v) With U_1 := {Z ≠ 0, ∂Q/∂Y ≠ 0} and U_2 := {X ≠ 0, ∂Q/∂Y ≠ 0} in X_{F_17}, U_1 contains 17 of the 20 points of X(F_17); the other three are (1 : 1 : 0), (1 : −1 : 0) ∈ U_2 and (1 : 1 : 1), which lies in neither (the disc of P0). The boundary D = {Z = 0} consists of the four points (1 : ±1 : 0), (1 : ±√5 : 0), since Q(X, Y, 0) = (Y² − X²)(Y² − 5X²).
hypotheses: X_s(13) is defined as X(13)/C_s^+(13) over Q (R13.4a).
proofSteps: (i) Import X_s(13) ≅ X_0(169)/w_169 from R13.4a; S_2(Γ_0(169))^{w_169 = +1} has dimension 3, spanned by the conjugates of f (CN.3 request); their q-expansions give the canonical map; no quadratic relation holds (finite linear algebra on q-expansions), so the curve is not hyperelliptic and its canonical image is a plane quartic; B(f_1, f_2, f_3) is a weight-8 cusp form for Γ_0(169) vanishing to order > 8 · 182/12 at ∞, hence zero by the Sturm bound (CN.3 request).
(ii) A polynomial identity of ternary quartics over Z, checked by expansion (both sides agree on the grid {0, …, 4}³, which determines a polynomial of degree ≤ 4 in each variable).

(iii) Good reduction: an exact certificate that the ideal (B, ∂B/∂X, ∂B/∂Y, ∂B/∂Z) ⊆ Z[X, Y, Z] contains 13^k times a power of the irrelevant ideal (resultant or Gröbner certificate); likewise for Q with 2^k 13^l. Smoothness modulo 17 and the count 20 are finite computations over F_17.
(iv) Exact evaluation of Q at the seven points, and of their reductions.
(v) Finite computation over F_17: ∂Q/∂Y vanishes at (1 : 1 : 1), and the points at Z = 0 are (1 : 1 : 0), (1 : 16 : 0); Q(X, Y, 0) factors as stated over Q.
acceptance: Q(P_i) = 0 for i = 0, …, 6 (exact).
#X(F_17) = 20, so the trace of Frobenius on H¹ is 17 + 1 − 20 = −2.

nodes.title: The endomorphism algebra and Picard number of J_s(13)
nodes.statement: Let J := Jac(X_s(13)). The weight-two cusp forms for Γ_0^+(169) (that is, S_2(Γ_0(169))^{w_169 = +1}) form one Galois orbit with coefficient field K := Q(α) = Q(ζ_7)^+, α³ + 2α² − α − 1 = 0, f = q + αq² + (−α² − 2α)q³ + (α² − 2)q⁴ + (α² + 2α − 2)q⁵ + (−α − 1)q⁶ + ⋯. J is Q-isogenous to the optimal quotient A_f = J_0(169)/I_f, End(J) ⊗ Q ≅ K, J is absolutely simple of dimension 3, and ρ(J) := rk NS(J_Q̄) = 3. (Context, not used in the proofs: Chen's isogeny Jac(X_s(ℓ)) ∼ Jac(X_0^+(ℓ²)) ∼ J_0(ℓ) × Jac(X_ns(ℓ)), with J_0(13) = 0, explains why Mazur's method does not apply at ℓ = 13.)
hypotheses: f has neither complex multiplication nor inner twists: a CM newform of level N has CM field of discriminant dividing N, and no imaginary quadratic discriminant divides 169; an inner twist of a trivial-character form is by a quadratic character, here χ_13, and f ⊗ χ_13 = f^σ would give σ(a_3) = a_3 (χ_13(3) = 1), hence σ = id since a_3 generates K, and then a_2 = −a_2 (χ_13(2) = −1), contradicting a_2 = α.
proofSteps: The newform orbit and q-expansion are a certified modular-symbols computation (CN.3 request).

J ≅ Jac(X_0^+(169)) is isogenous to the w_169-invariant part of J_0(169), which is A_f because S_2(Γ_0(169))^{+} is spanned by the conjugates of f (ModularCurvesPartII R14.5/modular-quotient, R14.5/trivial-character-J0, R14.5/modular-quotient-dimension: dim A_f = [K : Q] = 3).
End(A_f) ⊗ Q ≅ K and End_Q̄(A_f) ⊗ Q ≅ K for f without CM and inner twists (Shimura Th. 7.14, Ribet Cor. 4.2; requested from R14.5), so J is absolutely simple.
NS(J_Q̄) ⊗ Q is the Rosati-fixed part of End⁰(J_Q̄) = K, which is all of K since K is totally real; hence ρ = 3.
acceptance: ρ = 3 = r = g, so r < g + ρ − 1 = 5 and X_s(13)(Q_p)_2 is finite (NC.5, BDMTV Theorem 2.3); g + ρ − 1 − r = 2 independent nice classes are available.

sources.excerpt: End(J) ⊗ Q ≃ K := Q(ζ7)+, and J is a simple abelian threefold. Therefore ρ(JQ) = 3.

nodes.title: Certified analytic rank one for the conjugates of f
nodes.statement: For each of the three real embeddings σ of K = Q(α), the L-function of f^σ satisfies L(f^σ, 1) = 0 and L'(f^σ, 1) > 0.6; hence ord_{s=1} L(f^σ, s) = 1 for every σ. The vanishing comes from the sign of the functional equation (f is w_169-invariant, so the root number of L(f^σ, s) is −1); the derivative bound is a CN.4 interval enclosure of L'(f^σ, 1) of width < 10^(−100) whose lower endpoint exceeds 0.6.
hypotheses: The functional equation of L(f^σ, s) with conductor 169 and the Atkin–Lehner eigenvalue +1.
proofSteps: f ∈ S_2(Γ_0(169))^{w_169 = +1}; for weight two the root number is minus the Atkin–Lehner eigenvalue, so Λ(f^σ, 2 − s) = −Λ(f^σ, s) and L(f^σ, 1) = 0. (BDMTV compute instead the rational number c L(f, 1)/Ω exactly by Agashe–Stein; either route is exact.)

Evaluate L'(f^σ, 1) by the rapidly convergent series from the functional equation with certified truncation and coefficient bounds (CN.4 request extending CN.4/cusp-l-value-enclosure to level 169 and to algebraic coefficient embeddings); the enclosures exclude 0.
A positive lower bound for an interval proves nonvanishing; numerical near-equality is never used as an identity (CN.4 acceptance).
acceptance: The three enclosures have lower endpoints > 0.6 (BDMTV p.927).

sources.excerpt: We found that the number L′(f, 1) was always larger than 0.6 for any embedding Q(α) ↪ C and the error in these computations was smaller than 10−100.

nodes.title: The Mordell–Weil rank of J_s(13) (BDMTV Proposition 6.2)
nodes.statement: rk J(Q) = 3 for J = Jac(X_s(13)), unconditionally; moreover Sha(J/Q) is finite, and for a prime p inert in K = Q(ζ_7)^+ (so that K_p = K ⊗ Q_p is a field) the p-adic logarithm J(Q) ⊗ Q_p → H⁰(X_{Q_p}, Ω¹)^* is an isomorphism as soon as log(AJ_b(P)) of one rational point P is nonzero; p = 17 is inert (17 ≡ 3 mod 7 and 3 has order 3 in (Z/7Z)^×/{±1}), and xs13-equivariant-height-matrices verifies the nonvanishing with P5. A second route, labelled conditional: three independent points (ED.3/reduction-rank-lower-bound) and a descent upper bound on the genus-three Jacobian (Bruin–Poonen–Stoll; no ED.3 node covers descent beyond genus two) whose class-group input for a degree-28 field of discriminant 2⁴²·13¹² is certified only under the Generalised Riemann Hypothesis (Bruin–Poonen–Stoll).
hypotheses: J ∼ A_f (xs13-endomorphism-algebra); ord_{s=1} L(f^σ, s) = 1 for all σ (xs13-analytic-rank-certificate).
proofSteps: Since J is isogenous to A_f, rk J(Q) = rk A_f(Q).

Analytic rank one for every conjugate gives rk A_f(Q) = dim A_f = 3 and finiteness of Sha by Gross–Zagier and Kolyvagin–Logachev for the modular quotient: the non-torsion trace point over an admissible imaginary quadratic field (GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights GZ.8/totally-real-trace-point-nontorsion with F = Q, B = M_2(Q)), the Kolyvagin–Logachev descent HeegnerPointEulerSystems HE.7/admissible-rm-kolyvagin-logachev (whose non-torsion hypothesis the GZ.8 trace point discharges), and the analytic-rank-one assembly and descent to Q requested from GZ.8 (PAPER-BALAKRISHNAN-DOGRA-MULLER-ETAL-19/79, PAPER-BALAKRISHNAN-DOGRA-MULLER-ETAL-19/97).

K = End⁰(J) acts on J(Q) ⊗ Q, which is therefore a K-vector space of dimension 1, and log is K_p-linear onto the free rank-one K_p-module H⁰(Ω¹)^*; when K_p is a field a single point with nonzero logarithm generates, so log is an isomorphism (the hypothesis of BDMTV §1.4).
Finiteness of Sha supplies the Selmer comparison needed in the corrected Lemma 3.7 (E8).
acceptance: The unconditional route uses only the analytic certificate and the GZ.8/HE.7 theorems; the descent route is recorded with the label conditional on GRH.

sources.excerpt: The work of Gross-Zagier [GZ86] and Kolyvagin-Logachev [KL89] proves that if the order of vanishing of the L-function L(f, s) of f at s = 1 is 1, then rk(Af / Q) = g = 3.

nodes.title: The Tate classes Z1, Z2 from the Hecke operators T_7 and T_11
nodes.statement: In the basis ω of xs13-first-chart-hodge-data, let A_q ∈ M_6(Q) be the matrix of the Hecke operator T_q on H¹_dR(X/Q) (q = 7, 11), obtained from the Eichler–Shimura relation ι(a_q) = Fr_q + q Fr_q^(−1) (50), and C the cup product matrix. Then Z_q := (6A_q − tr(A_q) I_6) C^(−1) are Z1 (q = 7) and Z2 (q = 11), the integer matrices with rows Z1: (0, −976, −1104, 10, −6, 18), (976, 0, −816, −3, 1, 3), (1104, 816, 0, −3, 3, −11), (−10, 3, 3, 0, 0, 0), (6, −1, −3, 0, 0, 0), (−18, −3, 11, 0, 0, 0); Z2: (0, 112, −656, −6, 6, 6), (−112, 0, −2576, 15, 9, 27), (656, 2576, 0, 3, 3, −3), (6, −15, −3, 0, 0, 0), (−6, −9, −3, 0, 0, 0), (−6, −27, 3, 0, 0, 0). They are linearly independent admissible Tate classes: (a) holds because they are cycle classes of the trace-zero correspondences 6T_q − tr(T_q) (NC.5), and (b)–(d) are the exact checks: antisymmetric, zero lower-right 3 × 3 block, and Z(0,3) + Z(1,4) + Z(2,5) = 0.
hypotheses: The basis ω is symplectic with ω_0, ω_1, ω_2 holomorphic (xs13-first-chart-hodge-data).
The matrices A_q are exact rational matrices (CN.3 request).
proofSteps: The Hecke correspondence T_q is defined over Q and acts on H¹_dR(X/Q); its matrix A_q in the Q-basis ω is rational. Eichler–Shimura (ModularCurvesPartII R14.6/special-fibre-eichler-shimura) gives A_q = Fr_q + q Fr_q^(−1) with Fr_q computed q-adically by Tuitman's algorithm (RD.7); the exact rational matrix is certified as requested from CN.3 (precision beyond a proved height bound, or q-expansion and duality checks).

6T_q − tr(T_q) is a symmetric trace-zero correspondence (T_q is self-adjoint for the cup product and J is absolutely simple), hence nice (NC.5, BDMTV Lemma 2.4 and §1.5); its cycle class is (6A_q − tr(A_q)I)C^(−1) in tensor coordinates, so (a)–(d) hold.
The checks (b)–(d) on the printed integer matrices are exact: antisymmetry entrywise, the lower-right block is zero, and 10 + 1 − 11 = 0, −6 + 9 − 3 = 0.
Independence: the (0,1) and (0,2) entries (−976, −1104) and (112, −656) are not proportional.
acceptance: Z1 and Z2 satisfy (b)–(d) exactly (admissibleTate_xs13_Z1).
6A_q − tr(A_q)I has trace zero.

The boundary D = X ∖ Y is the divisor Z = 0 (four points over Q(√5)), and H⁰(X, O(2D)) has basis 1, x, y, x², xy, y². The Hodge filtration data of A_{Z1}, A_{Z2} are η_{Z1} = −(44x² + (148/3)xy + 8y²)dx/Q_y, η_{Z2} = (−40x² + 148xy + 36y²)dx/Q_y, β_Fil,Z1 = (0, 0, 0, 0, 1/2, 1/2)ᵀ, β_Fil,Z2 = (0, 0, 0, 0, −1/2, −5/2)ᵀ, γ_Fil,Z1 = 5y/6 + 3x/2, γ_Fil,Z2 = −5y/6 − 15x/2.

Certificate: substitute the printed values into (30) and (32); both are identities of Laurent series over Q(√5) truncated at the pole orders, checked exactly.

nodes.title: First chart of X_s(13): Frobenius lift and the functions θ_{Z_i}
nodes.statement: Let p = 17 and U_1 := Y_{F_17} ∩ {Q_y ≠ 0}. Tuitman's algorithm (RD.7) provides an overconvergent Frobenius lift Φ on a strict neighbourhood of ]U_1[ with Φ(x) = x^17 and Φ(y) the unique overconvergent solution of Q(x^17, Φ(y)) = 0 with Φ(y) ≡ y^17 modulo 17; the base point b = P2 is a Teichmüller point for Φ. It also provides F ∈ M_6(Q_17) and overconvergent f with Φ^*ω = Fω + df, f(P2) = 0, to certified precision. For Z ∈ {Z1, Z2}, frobenius-structure-matrix gives G_Z, frobenius-equivariant-splitting gives s^φ on every residue disc of ]U_1[, and local-height-at-p gives θ_Z(x) = h_p(A_Z(P2, x)) as a power series on each of the 17 residue discs of ]U_1[, with coefficients certified to precision 17^N together with the valuation bound of height-series-valuation-bound for the tail.

nodes.title: Equivariant heights and the matrices T_1, T_2 for X_s(13)
nodes.statement: Let a_3 := a_3(f) = −α² − 2α, a generator of K, and ι(a_3) the matrix of T_3 on H¹_dR(X) (Eichler–Shimura); let s be a K-equivariant splitting of the Hodge filtration, so that the global height h is K-equivariant (NC.5, BDMTV Remark 3.9), and K_p := K ⊗ Q_17, E_K := H⁰(X_{Q_17}, Ω¹)^* ⊗_{K_p} H⁰(X_{Q_17}, Ω¹)^* (dimension 3 over Q_17). For z ∈ X(Q_17) and Z ∈ {Z1, Z2} put E_1(z) := AJ_b(z) and E_{2,Z}(z) := E_Z(AJ_b(z)) + c_Z (NC.5, BDMTV Lemma 3.7). Then: E_1(P5) ≠ 0, so it generates H⁰(Ω¹)^* over the field K_p (17 is inert in K) and log : J(Q) ⊗ Q_17 → H⁰(Ω¹)^* is an isomorphism; the vectors E_1(P_k) ⊗_{K_p} E_{2,Z1}(P_k), k = 1, 3, 5, form a Q_17-basis of E_K (certified by a nonzero determinant computed to precision); with ψ_1, ψ_2, ψ_3 the dual basis of ι(a_3)^i(E_1(P5) ⊗ E_{2,Z1}(P5)), i = 0, 1, 2, and Ψ_j(Z, z) := ψ_j(E_1(z) ⊗_{K_p} E_{2,Z}(z)), the 4 × 4 matrices T_i(x) with first row (θ_{Z_i}(x), Ψ_1(Z_i, x), Ψ_2(Z_i, x), Ψ_3(Z_i, x)) and rows (θ_{Z1}(P_k), Ψ_1(Z1, P_k), Ψ_2(Z1, P_k), Ψ_3(Z1, P_k)), k = 1, 3, 5, satisfy det T_i(x) = 0 for every x ∈ X(Q) (indeed on the set cut out by the pair (θ_{Z_i}, {0})). The relations E_1(P_k) ⊗ E_{2,Z1}(P_k) = ι(c_k)(E_1(P5) ⊗ E_1(P5)) with c_1 = 352 + 818α + 294α², c_3 = 162 + 406α + 150α², c_5 = −36 − 62α − 18α² are recorded data, not inputs of the proof.
hypotheses: X_s(13) has potentially good reduction everywhere, so the pairs (θ_Z, {0}) are quadratic Chabauty pairs (NC.5, BDMTV Corollary 3.8; R13.5).
rk J(Q) = 3 (xs13-rank-three).
proofSteps: E_1(P_k), E_{2,Z}(P_k) are the extension classes π_1, π_2 of A_Z(b, P_k), read off from the Hodge and Frobenius data at P_k (local-height-at-p data and (13)); they are computed to certified precision.
A p-adic number known modulo 17^N with valuation < N is nonzero; this certifies E_1(P5) ≠ 0 and the nonvanishing of the 3 × 3 determinant of the three vectors in E_K.

K-equivariance of h means h is determined by its values on E_K, a 3-dimensional space with basis ψ_j-dual; the global height pairing B = h is the same for Z1 and Z2, so every row (for any Z and any rational point) satisfies the same linear relation θ_Z(z) = Σ_j h_j Ψ_j(Z, z); hence det T_i vanishes at rational points (NC.5, BDMTV Lemma 1.5).
The rows of T_2 use Z1 at P1, P3, P5 deliberately: the pairing is common to both classes (PAPER-BALAKRISHNAN-DOGRA-MULLER-ETAL-19/88 note).
acceptance: det T_1 vanishes at P1, P2, P3, P5 by construction (rows repeated or zero first row at the base point); the vanishing of det T_2 at P1, P3, P5 is a nontrivial consistency check (Remark 6.9).
arXiv v1 used P4 in place of P5; the published version uses P5 (P4 is not in the first chart).

nodes.title: The rational points of X_s(13) (BDMTV Theorem 1.1)
nodes.statement: X_s(13)(Q) consists of exactly seven points: in the model Q = 0 of xs13-plane-model they are P0 = (1 : 1 : 1), P1 = (1 : 1 : 2), P2 = (0 : 0 : 1), P3 = (−3 : 3 : 2), P4 = (1 : 1 : 0), P5 = (0 : 2 : 1), P6 = (−1 : 1 : 0), and the statement is an unconditional certified solution set. Under the moduli interpretation these are the rational cusp and six CM points, with CM by the imaginary quadratic orders of class number one in which 13 splits (discriminants −3, −4, −12, −16, −27, −43; j-invariants 0, 1728, 54000, 287496, −12288000, −884736000).

padic-candidate-comparison (all balls matched or excluded) gives X(Q) = {P0, …, P6} as an unconditional certified solution set.

nodes.title: Existence of non-CM split-Cartan images for ℓ = 2, 3, 5, 7
nodes.statement: For ℓ ∈ {2, 3, 5, 7} there are infinitely many j ∈ Q such that an elliptic curve E/Q with j(E) = j has no CM and ρ_{E,ℓ}(G_Q) is contained in the normaliser C_s^+(ℓ) of a split Cartan subgroup of GL_2(F_ℓ).
hypotheses: X_s(ℓ) ≅ X_0^+(ℓ²) over Q and the rational-point criterion for X_H with −I ∈ H (R13.4a).
proofSteps: Genus zero: X_0(4), X_0(9), X_0(25) have genus 0, so their quotients X_0^+(ℓ²) do; X_0(49) has genus 1 (μ = 56, ν_2 = 0, ν_3 = 2, ν_∞ = 8, g = 1 + 56/12 − 2/3 − 4) and w_49 has h(−196) = 4 fixed points, so Riemann–Hurwitz 0 = 2(2g' − 2) + 4 gives g' = 0 (genus and fixed-point data from R13.4a).
The cusps 0 and ∞ of X_0(ℓ²) are rational and swapped by w_{ℓ²}, so their common image is a rational point of X_s(ℓ); a genus-zero curve with a rational point is isomorphic to P¹_Q.

The j-map X_s(ℓ) → X(1) is a nonconstant morphism over Q with a pole at that cusp; for a prime q, rational points t q-adically close to the cusp satisfy v_q(j(t)) < 0, and there are infinitely many such t with pairwise distinct j(t) (the fibres are finite).

CM j-invariants are algebraic integers (CM.3/integrality), so a non-integral rational j is not CM and is ≠ 0, 1728; the rational-point criterion (R13.4a) gives E/Q with j(E) = j(t) and image in C_s^+(ℓ) (no twist is needed since −I ∈ C_s^+(ℓ)).
acceptance: ℓ = 7 uses the genus-one curve X_0(49) and the four fixed points of w_49.
The argument does not use the classification of class-number-one orders.

nodes.statement: X_ns(13) ≅ X_s(13) over Q (Baran), so #X_ns(13)(Q) = 7, and all seven points are CM: they are the points above j(O_D) for the class-number-one discriminants D ∈ {−7, −8, −11, −19, −28, −67, −163}, exactly those in which 13 is inert. nodes.title: Class number one from X_ns(13) (BDMTV Remark 1.4)
nodes.statement: The imaginary quadratic fields of class number one are Q(√−d) for d ∈ {1, 2, 3, 7, 11, 19, 43, 67, 163}; equivalently their discriminants are −3, −4, −7, −8, −11, −19, −43, −67, −163.
hypotheses: nonsplit-cartan-13; class numbers of imaginary quadratic fields with |D| ≤ 52 are certified (CN.2).
proofSteps: Let K have discriminant D with h(K) = 1 and |D| > 52. Every rational prime ℓ < |D|/4 is inert in K: a split or ramified ℓ would give a principal ideal of norm ℓ, generated by (a + b√D)/2 with (a² + |D|b²)/4 = ℓ, forcing b = 0 and then a² = 4ℓ, impossible. In particular 13 is inert.

j(O_K) ∈ Q (class number one) and a CM curve E/Q with End(E_Q̄) ≅ O_K has image in a non-split Cartan normaliser at 13 (CM.4/residual-cartan-normalizer), with j ≠ 0, 1728; it gives a rational point of X_ns(13) (R13.4a), so by nonsplit-cartan-13, D ∈ {−7, −8, −11, −19, −28, −67, −163}; with |D| > 52 and D fundamental this leaves −67 and −163.
For |D| ≤ 52 a finite certified class-number computation gives −3, −4, −7, −8, −11, −19, −43, and the same computation certifies h(−67) = h(−163) = 1 (CN.2).
acceptance: The argument recovers d = 67 and d = 163 from Corollary 1.3 and the small cases from a finite computation.

nodes.title: The rational points of the exceptional curve X_S4(13) (BDMTV 2021 Theorem 1.1)
nodes.statement: Let X = X_S4(13), with canonical model 4x³y − 3x²y² + 3xy³ − x³z + 16x²yz − 11xy²z + 5y³z + 3x²z² + 9xyz² + y²z² + xz³ + 2yz³ = 0 (Banwait–Cremona). Then X(Q) = {(1 : 3 : −2), (0 : 0 : 1), (0 : 1 : 0), (1 : 0 : 0)}; the point (0 : 0 : 1) is CM with discriminant −3, and the other three are exceptional (non-CM curves with projective mod-13 image S_4, j-invariants 2⁴·5·13⁴·17³/3¹³, −2¹²·5³·11·13⁴/3¹³ and 2¹⁸·3³·13⁴·127³·139³·157³·283³·929/(5¹³·61¹³)). nodes.title: Rational points on the genus-three curves X_0^+(N), N prime (BDMTV 2021 Theorem 5.6)

For N = 97, with the model zx³ + (−y² + zy)x² + (−y³ − zy² − z³)x + (zy³ + z²y²) = 0, X_0^+(97)(Q) = {(1:0:0), (−2:1:1), (−1:0:1), (0:0:1), (0:1:0), (0:−1:1), (1:0:1), (1:1:1), (−1:1:0), (5:3:2)} (the cusp and CM points of discriminants −3, −4, −8, −11, −12, −16, −27, −43, −163). nodes.title: Two quartic Thue equations solved by Tzanakis–de Weger
nodes.statement: (i) X⁴ − 4X³Y − 12X²Y² + 4Y⁴ = 1 has exactly the integer solutions ±(1, 0). (ii) X⁴ − 12X²Y² − 8XY³ + 4Y⁴ = 1 has exactly the integer solutions ±(1, 0), ±(1, −1), ±(1, 3), ±(3, −1). Both are unconditional certified solution sets. Certificate data: K = Q(ϑ) with ϑ⁴ − 12ϑ² − 8ϑ + 4 = 0, which also contains φ = 2/ϑ with φ⁴ − 4φ³ − 12φ² + 4 = 0; the order R = Z + Zϑ + Z(ϑ²/2) + Z(ϑ³/2); fundamental units of R: ε_1 = 1 + ϑ, ε_2 = 3 + ϑ, ε_3 = ϑ²/2 (unimodularly equivalent to the system η_1, η_2, η_3 of TdW Appendix II); a solution gives a unit X − Yξ = ±ε_1^{a_1}ε_2^{a_2}ε_3^{a_3} (ξ = φ for (i), ξ = ϑ for (ii)), and for |Y| > 3 eight inhomogeneous linear forms Λ = δ + a_1μ_1 + a_2μ_2 + a_3μ_3 (TdW (2.5)–(2.6)) with C_5 = 1.211, C_6 = 6.38771·10⁴; an initial bound A := max|a_i| < 3.26·10⁴⁰; reduction with c_0 = 10¹⁴⁰ (lattices Γ_1, Γ_2 with |b_1| > 3.247·10⁴⁶ and 4.846·10⁴⁶, ‖s_3‖ > 0.029 in all eight cases) giving A ≤ 72, then c_0 = 10¹² (|b_1| > 1.293·10⁴ and 1.092·10⁴, ‖s_3‖ > 0.143) giving A ≤ 10; exhaustive enumeration of |a_i| ≤ 10 and of |Y| ≤ 3.
hypotheses: The unit group certificate for R (CN.2 request).

The initial bound comes from an imported lower bound for linear forms in logarithms through ED.2/certified-linear-form-constant; TdW used Waldschmidt's 1980 theorem (their Appendix II). If the imported DT.3 bound is weaker than 3.26·10⁴⁰, the first reduction step is rerun with a larger c_0 until the ED.1 reduction hypothesis holds, and the later steps start from the bound it returns.
proofSteps: (i) and (ii) are Norm_{K/Q}(X − Yφ) = 1 and Norm_{K/Q}(X − Yϑ) = 1, so X − Yξ ∈ R^× = ±⟨ε_1, ε_2, ε_3⟩ (CN.2).

Siegel's identity among three conjugates turns the unit equation into the linear forms (2.5)–(2.6); |Λ| ≤ C_6 exp(−(4/C_5)A) for |Y| > 3 (TdW Lemma II.2.1), and the imported lower bound gives A < 3.26·10⁴⁰ (ED.2/certified-linear-form-constant, ED.2/thue-certified-solution-set).

ED.1/inhomogeneous-reduction with the approximation lattice of ED.1/linear-form-lattice (C = c_0, W_1 = W_2 = 1), spanned by the columns of the matrix with rows (1,0,0), (0,1,0), ([c_0μ_1], [c_0μ_2], [c_0μ_3]) and the target (0, 0, −[c_0δ]): the certified lower bounds for |b_1| and ‖s_3‖ give A < (1/3.303) log(c_0 · 6.38771·10⁴ / (3 · K)) with K the previous bound, i.e. A ≤ 72 and then A ≤ 10.
Enumerate all (a_1, a_2, a_3) with |a_i| ≤ 10 and test exactly whether the unit has the shape X − Yξ; check |Y| ≤ 3 directly; ED.2/thue-certified-solution-set packages completeness.
acceptance: The TdW computation took about 35 seconds on an IBM 3083; the certified run checks the same lattices with exact integer LLL (GN.5 via ED.1).

nodes.title: Integral points on y² = x³ − 4x + 1 (Tzanakis–de Weger Theorem A)
nodes.statement: The integral points of the elliptic curve E : y² = x³ − 4x + 1 are exactly the 22 points (x, ±y) with (x, y) ∈ {(−2, 1), (−1, 2), (0, 1), (2, 1), (3, 4), (4, 7), (10, 31), (12, 41), (20, 89), (114, 1217), (1274, 45473)}; an unconditional certified solution set. Consequently the triangular numbers n(n + 1)/2 (n ≥ 1) that are products of three consecutive integers are exactly T_3, T_15, T_20, T_44, T_608, T_22736 (Mohanty's problem). Certificate data: the cubic field L = Q(ψ), ψ³ − 4ψ + 1 = 0, with ring of integers Z[ψ], discriminant 229, class number 1 and fundamental units ψ, 2 − ψ; the factorisation y² = (x − ψ)(x² + xψ + ψ² − 4) into coprime factors, so x − ψ = ±ψ^i(2 − ψ)^j α² with i, j ∈ {0, 1}; for x ≥ 1 the sign + is forced by the real embedding ψ^(1) = 0.254… and i = 0 by ψ^(2) = −2.114…; the cases j = 0 and j = 1 lead to two reducible quartic Thue equations (solved by factoring) and to the irreducible equations m⁴ − 4m³n − 12m²n² + 4n⁴ = 1 and n⁴ − 12n²m² − 8nm³ + 4m⁴ = 1 of thue-example-tdw89.
hypotheses: The class group and unit certificates for L (CN.2).
x < 0 is a finite check (only x = −2, −1 occur).
proofSteps: The two factors of x³ − 4x + 1 = (x − ψ)(x² + xψ + ψ² − 4) are coprime in Z[ψ]: a common prime divides 3ψ² − 4, of norm −229, and would force y² = ±229·□ after taking norms, impossible.
Class number one and the unit group give x − ψ = ±ψ^i(2 − ψ)^j α² (CN.2/joint-class-unit-index-certificate, CN.2/integral-basis-certificate).

nodes.title: The S-unit equation x + y = z for S = {2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13} (de Weger Theorem 6.3)
nodes.statement: Let S be the set of positive integers whose prime factors lie in {2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13}. The equation x + y = z with x, y, z ∈ S, gcd(x, y) = 1 and x ≤ y has exactly 545 solutions; 514 of them satisfy ord_2(xyz) ≤ 12, ord_3(xyz) ≤ 7, ord_5(xyz) ≤ 5, ord_7(xyz) ≤ 4, ord_11(xyz) ≤ 3, ord_13(xyz) ≤ 3, and the other 31 are listed in de Weger's Table II, the largest being 91 + 1771470 = 1771561 (7·13 + 2·3¹¹·5 = 11⁶). Certificate data: the initial bound m(xyz) := max_p ord_p(xyz) < 5.60·10²⁷ (de Weger §6.2, from Yu's p-adic and Waldschmidt's archimedean bounds); p-adic reduction with the parameters (μ_0, μ) = (2, 605), (1, 385), (1, 275), (1, 220), (1, 165), (1, 165) for p = 2, …, 13 and lattice lower bounds ℓ(Γ*_μ) > √5 · 5.60·10²⁷, giving ord_p(xyz) ≤ 606, 385, 275, 220, 165, 165, so m ≤ 606; a second round (μ = 66, 42, 30, 24, 18, 18) giving m ≤ 67; a third round (μ = 55, 35, 25, 20, 15, 15) giving m ≤ 56; then Fincke–Pohst enumeration of the short vectors of the same lattices down to f(2) = 4, f(p) = 1 for p ≥ 3, and a final exhaustive search.
hypotheses: The initial bound is supplied through ED.2/s-unit-certified-solution-set from the imported p-adic and archimedean lower bounds (DT.3, Yu and Matveev); a weaker imported bound only enlarges the first μ.
proofSteps: Reduce to the coprime S-unit equation and to linear forms in p-adic logarithms (ED.2/s-unit-certified-solution-set, ED.1/padic-linear-form-lattice).
Each p-adic reduction step: if ℓ(Γ*_μ) > √5 · X_1 then ord_p(z) ≤ μ + μ_0 − 1 for solutions with m(xyz) ≤ X_1 (de Weger Lemma 3.14, ED.1/padic-reduction); symmetry in x, y, z bounds ord_p(xyz).
Below the reduced bounds, ED.1/short-vector-enumeration-complete (Fincke–Pohst) lists all lattice points of the relevant norm; the corresponding exponent vectors are tested exactly.
Exact verification of the 545 solutions; completeness from the bounds and the enumeration.
acceptance: A brute-force search over z ≤ 3·10⁶ finds exactly 545 solutions with largest z = 1771561 (a consistency check of the list, not a completeness proof).

nodes.title: The Thue–Mahler equation x³ − 23x²y + 5xy² + 24y³ = ±2^a3^b5^c7^d (Tzanakis–de Weger 1992)
nodes.statement: The equation x³ − 23x²y + 5xy² + 24y³ = ±2^{z_1}3^{z_2}5^{z_3}7^{z_4} with x, y ∈ Z, gcd(x, y) = 1 and z_i ≥ 0 has exactly 72 solutions up to the sign ±(x, y), listed in TdW 1992 §18 with x ≥ 0; the largest is (48632, −3729), with value 2¹⁸·5¹³. Certificate data: the cubic field K = Q(ξ) with F(ξ, 1) = 0, which is not Galois; the corrected1993 route starts with c7=1.08672·10⁴⁶ and B<1.511·10⁵⁰; the same first lattices give N1=1153 and H≤4919, placing the search below the old9.844·10⁴⁹ bound so the original subsequent reduction reaches113 and86 (Fincke–Pohst). Alternatively the1993 Baker–Wüstholz route gives the original initial9.844·10⁴⁹ bound directly, followed by a sieve over the remaining exponent tuples (82 tuples, of which 79 give solutions with 10 counted twice, plus 3 exceptional solutions outside the reduced bounds). In a certified run the final test of each tuple is exact integer evaluation, not 15-digit floating point.
hypotheses: The initial bound must be obtained from corrected certified DT.3/DT.4 inputs through ED.2. The original1992 BGMMS constant is insufficient: use the1993 published corrigendum (E29), or another independently certified bound with a validated reduction transcript.
proofSteps: Reduce to the equations N_{K/Q}(x − yθ) = ±2^{z_1}⋯7^{z_4} and to S-unit equations in K (DT.4/thue-mahler-effective-finiteness via ED.2).

Apply the1993 corrigendum to the initial archimedean bound: multiply the old c7 by7^15, use B<1.511·10^50, and verify the stated same-lattice first reductions N1=1153,H≤4919. Only then invoke the original later reduction transcript. The alternative Baker–Wüstholz constants restore9.844·10^49; these are two distinct justified routes. Neither has been numerically replayed here.
Real and p-adic reduction steps (ED.1/inhomogeneous-reduction, ED.1/padic-reduction) lower the bound to 113, Fincke–Pohst enumeration (ED.1/short-vector-enumeration-complete) to 86.

The sieve over the remaining tuples (TdW §18) leaves 82 tuples; exact evaluation of F at the corresponding (x, y) rejects 3 and confirms 79, among which 10 solutions are counted twice (Cases III and V with n_3 = 1), leaving 69 solutions within the reduced bounds.
Together with the 3 exceptional solutions found during the reduction this gives 72 solutions; ED.2/thue-mahler-certified-solution-set packages completeness.

sourceIssues.locator: Published §3.3, p.279, PrepareLift: the definition of Λ, with φᵢ as defined in §3.2, p.277.
sourceIssues.printed: Λ = {Lⱼ₋₁ ∩ ker(φᵢ) : i ∈ I′}
sourceIssues.correction: At target D=NₖΓ use Lⱼ₋₁∩φᵢ⁻¹(φᵢ(D)); with the source’s surjective maps this is Lⱼ₋₁∩φᵢ⁻¹(NₖGᵢ). Equivalently, first replace Gᵢ by Gᵢ/NₖGᵢ and φᵢ by its composite into that quotient, then take its kernel. The required invariant is D≤Lⱼ≤Lⱼ₋₁.
sourceIssues.reason: Let Γ=ℤ, G=ℤ/4, φ reduction, Nₖ₋₁=1, qₖ=2 and Nₖ=2. The selected exponent test holds. The displayed original kernel produces L₁=4ℤ, which fails to contain D=2ℤ. The final assignment Lₜ=2ℤ then makes an ascending step, so the quotient Lₜ₋₁/Lₜ in Lift is not defined. The quotient-target kernel is 2ℤ and preserves the invariant. This is a defect of the literal printed notation, not a claim that the authors’ implementation has this bug.

review.reason: Independently rechecked the stated primary locator in this review. Version-of-record pp.277–279 defines the maps before target quotienting. sourceIssues.correction: y = (0, …, 0, −β′^(μ))^T, so that x − y = (x_1, …, x_{n−1}, x_n + β′^(μ))^T and Lemma 3.13 gives ord_p(x_n + β′^(μ) − Σ_{i<n} x_iθ′_i) ≥ μ, which is ord_p(Λ′) ≥ μ for Λ′ = β′ − Σ x_iθ′_i + x_n.

sourceIssues.printed: S_p is a subset of Z^(r+s) minus zero, but its vectors are repeatedly indexed through b_p. Condition(2) quantifies over every vector of V_p, including zero, and allows a scalar β in F_p.
sourceIssues.correction: Write each vector as (b₁,…,b_(r+s)). For the computable surviving subspace V′_p, choose exactly one bounded integral lift of each one-dimensional subspace of V′_p; equivalently, every nonzero a∈V′_p has a unique representative b∈S_p with a=β(b mod p) for some β∈F_p^×. Then the required coverage also holds for V_p minus zero, since V_p⊆V′_p. Zero requires no projective representative; if V′_p={0}, take S_p empty. This states a sufficient corrected representative construction, not a claim that the full numerical point-recognition procedure is certified.
sourceIssues.reason: At a=0, every b∈S_p satisfies the printed congruence with β=0, so uniqueness fails whenever S_p has at least two elements; with S_p empty existence fails. Even when S_p has one element the zero clause does not express a projective class. For example a two-dimensional F₂ surviving space has three projective classes, all representing zero when multiplied by0. The missing nonzero scope is essential to the literal condition. The b_p notation is independently dimensionally inconsistent with Z^(r+s) and the r+s-term sum(41).

suggestedOmissions.requiredSignature: Let K be a finite extension of ℚ_p with ring of integers O_K, residue field k and ramification index e, and A an abelian variety of dimension g over K. Write Lie(A) for its tangent space at 0 (a K-vector space of dimension g) and Ω_A := H⁰(A, Ω¹) for its space of regular 1-forms, which are the translation-invariant forms; evaluation at 0 identifies Ω_A with the dual Module.Dual K Lie(A). The abelian logarithm log_A : A(K) → Lie(A) is the unique group homomorphism that agrees with the formal logarithm on some open subgroup, constructed as follows. Let 𝒜 be the Néron model of A over O_K (an abelian scheme when A has good reduction), F̂ its formal group, the completion of 𝒜 along the zero section, a g-dimensional commutative formal Lie group over O_K once formal parameters s = (s₁, …, s_g) are chosen, and A¹(K) := ker(𝒜(O_K) → 𝒜(k)) = F̂(m_K). Let log_F̂ ∈ (K[[s]])^g be the formal logarithm, the unique homomorphism of formal groups F̂ → Ĝ_a^g over K whose linear term is the identity; its coordinates are the formal primitives of a basis of invariant differentials and converge on m_K^g. Put N := #𝒜(k) = [A(K) : A¹(K)] and log_A(x) := N⁻¹ log_F̂(s(N x)), identifying K^g with Lie(A) by ds at 0. The integration pairing is ⟨x, ω⟩ := ω(log_A x) ∈ K for x ∈ A(K), ω ∈ Ω_A. Properties: (a) log_A is a homomorphism, independent of the choices of formal parameters and of N among multiples of the exponent of 𝒜(k); (b) ker log_A = A(K)_tors, which is finite; (c) log_A is continuous, its differential at 0 is the identity, and for n > e/(p − 1) it maps the subgroup F̂(m_K^n) isomorphically onto the lattice (m_K^n)^g; (d) for a homomorphism φ : A → B of abelian varieties over K, log_B ∘ φ = dφ ∘ log_A, i.e. ⟨φ(x), ω⟩ = ⟨x, φ*ω⟩; for a finite extension K'/K, log_{A_{K'}} restricts to log_A on A(K); (e) the pairing A(K) × Ω_A → K is ℤ-bilinear and K-linear in ω, its kernel in Ω_A, {ω : ⟨x, ω⟩ = 0 ∀x}, is 0 and its kernel in A(K) is A(K)_tors; for each ω, x ↦ ⟨x, ω⟩ is the unique locally analytic homomorphism A(K) → K whose differential at 0 is ω. The compatible logarithms over finite K'/K first define log_A on A(ℚ̄_p). Over ℂ_p use the analytic logarithm of the ℂ_p-Lie group, extending this map continuously; the union over finite extensions alone does not define it on all A(ℂ_p) (KRZB Definition 3.8 and Proposition 3.16). Hypotheses: K finite over ℚ_p; A an abelian variety over K. Good reduction is not assumed; when A has good reduction 𝒜 is the abelian scheme extending A and 𝒜(k) is the group of points of its special fibre. Normalisation: Lie(A) = T₀A and the pairing is evaluation of an invariant differential on a tangent vector; no sign or scaling is inserted. Original API contracts: abelianLog: log_A : A(K) →+ Lie(A). abelianLog_eq_formalLog: On A¹(K) = F̂(m_K), log_A(x) = log_F̂(s(x)) for any choice of formal parameters s. abelianLog_nsmul: log_A(n • x) = n • log_A(x) for n ∈ ℤ. ker_abelianLog: log_A x = 0 ↔ x has finite order; A(K)_tors is finite. abelianLog_map: log_B(φ x) = dφ(log_A x) for a homomorphism φ : A → B; log_{id} = id and log respects composition. abelianLog_baseChange: For K'/K finite, log_{A_{K'}}(x) = log_A(x) ⊗ 1 for x ∈ A(K). integrationPairing: ⟨x, ω⟩ := ω(log_A x) for x ∈ A(K), ω ∈ Ω_A = Module.Dual K Lie(A). integrationPairing_eq_zero_iff: ⟨x, ω⟩ = 0 for all ω iff x is torsion; ⟨x, ω⟩ = 0 for all x iff ω = 0. abelianLog_unique: A continuous homomorphism λ : A(K) → Lie(A) that agrees with log_F̂ on some open subgroup equals log_A. Original geometric regressions: abelianLog_elliptic: For an elliptic curve E over ℚ_p with good reduction and minimal Weierstrass model, log_E on E¹(ℚ_p) is the formal-group logarithm of the Weierstrass formal group in the parameter z = −x/y (dimension one, the case of Mathlib's FormalGroup). abelianLog_torsion: log_A(x) = 0 for every torsion point x; for dim A = 0 the logarithm is the zero map to the zero space. abelianLog_E11_five_torsion: For E : y² + y = x³ − x² over ℚ_5 the point (0, 0) has order 5, so log_E(0, 0) = 0: log_A is not injective, and a definition requiring an inverse exponential on all of A(K) is wrong. abelianLog_C05_kernel_point: For the Jacobian of y² = x⁶ + 8x⁵ + 22x⁴ + 22x³ + 5x² + 6x + 1 over ℚ_3, D' = [(0, −1) + (−3, 1) − ∞⁺ − ∞⁻] lies in J¹(ℚ_3) with Flynn's local parameters (s₁, s₂) = (−9/14, 426/49), and its formal logarithm is ≡ (36, 3) (mod 3⁴) (Flynn–Poonen–Schaefer p.22). integrationPairing_leftKernel: If ω ∈ Ω_A satisfies ⟨x, ω⟩ = 0 for all x ∈ A(K), then ω = 0.
